<p></p></div><div name="India" term="India" wikidataID="Q668" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: India<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India">India</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>India</b>, officially the <b>Republic of India</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>j<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a country in <a href="/wiki/South_Asia" title="South Asia">South Asia</a>.  It is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area" title="List of countries and dependencies by area">seventh-largest country by area</a>; the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_population_(United_Nations)" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by population (United Nations)">most populous country</a> since 2023;<sup id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and, since its independence in 1947, the world's most populous democracy.<sup id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-stein-arnold_33-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-stein-arnold-33"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEFisher2018184&#8211;185_34-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFisher2018184%E2%80%93185-34"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Bounded by the <a href="/wiki/Indian_Ocean" title="Indian Ocean">Indian Ocean</a> on the south, the <a href="/wiki/Arabian_Sea" title="Arabian Sea">Arabian Sea</a> on the southwest, and the <a href="/wiki/Bay_of_Bengal" title="Bay of Bengal">Bay of Bengal</a> on the southeast, it shares land borders with <a href="/wiki/Pakistan" title="Pakistan">Pakistan</a> to the west;<sup id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-36"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>k<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nepal" title="Nepal">Nepal</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Bhutan" title="Bhutan">Bhutan</a> to the north; and <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh" title="Bangladesh">Bangladesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Myanmar" title="Myanmar">Myanmar</a> to the east. In the <a href="/wiki/Indian_Ocean" title="Indian Ocean">Indian Ocean</a>, India is near <a href="/wiki/Sri_Lanka" title="Sri Lanka">Sri Lanka</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Maldives" title="Maldives">Maldives</a>; its <a href="/wiki/Andaman_and_Nicobar_Islands" title="Andaman and Nicobar Islands">Andaman and Nicobar Islands</a> share a <a href="/wiki/Maritime_boundary" title="Maritime boundary">maritime border</a> with Myanmar, <a href="/wiki/Thailand" title="Thailand">Thailand</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Indonesia" title="Indonesia">Indonesia</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:India_(orthographic_projection).svg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Image of a globe centred on India, with India highlighted." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/250px-India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="250" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/500px-India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="541" data-file-height="541"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="ICAR" term="ICAR" wikidataID="Q16785275" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICAR" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: ICAR<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICAR">ICAR</a></p><p></p></div><div name="rice" term="rice" wikidataID="Q5090" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: rice<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice">Rice</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Rice</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Cereal_grain" class="mw-redirect" title="Cereal grain">cereal grain</a> and in its <a href="/wiki/Domestication" title="Domestication">domesticated</a> form is the <a href="/wiki/Staple_food" title="Staple food">staple food</a> of over half of the <a href="/wiki/World%27s_population" class="mw-redirect" title="World's population">world's population</a>, particularly in <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Africa" title="Africa">Africa</a>. Rice is the seed of the grass species <i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_sativa" title="Oryza sativa">Oryza sativa</a></i> (Asian rice)&#8212;or, much less commonly, <i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_glaberrima" title="Oryza glaberrima">Oryza glaberrima</a></i> (African rice). Asian rice was domesticated in <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a> some 13,500 to 8,200 years ago; African rice was domesticated in Africa about 3,000 years ago. Rice has become commonplace in many cultures worldwide; in 2023, 800 million tons were produced, placing it third after <a href="/wiki/Sugarcane" title="Sugarcane">sugarcane</a> and <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">maize</a>. Only some 8% of rice is traded internationally. China, India, and Indonesia are the largest consumers of rice. A substantial amount of the rice produced in developing nations is lost after harvest through factors such as poor transport and storage. Rice yields can be reduced by pests including <a href="/wiki/Insect" title="Insect">insects</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rodent" title="Rodent">rodents</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Bird" title="Bird">birds</a>, as well as by <a href="/wiki/Weed" title="Weed">weeds</a>, and by <a href="/wiki/List_of_rice_diseases" title="List of rice diseases">diseases</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Rice_blast" class="mw-redirect" title="Rice blast">rice blast</a>. Traditional <a href="/wiki/Rice_polyculture" title="Rice polyculture">rice polycultures</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Rice-duck_farming" title="Rice-duck farming">rice-duck farming</a>, and modern <a href="/wiki/Integrated_pest_management" title="Integrated pest management">integrated pest management</a> seek to control damage from pests in a <a href="/wiki/Sustainable_agriculture" title="Sustainable agriculture">sustainable</a> way.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg/500px-20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg" decoding="async" width="340" height="191" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg/960px-20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="720"></a><figcaption>Rice plant (<i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_sativa" title="Oryza sativa">Oryza sativa</a></i>) with branched <a href="/wiki/Panicle" title="Panicle">panicles</a> containing many grains on each stem</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Plant Varieties" term="Plant Varieties" wikidataID="Q7201547" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_varieties" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Plant Varieties<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_varieties">Plant varieties</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Plant variety</b> may refer to:
</p>
<p></p></div><div name="genotypes" term="genotypes" wikidataID="Q106016" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotypes" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: genotypes<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotypes">Genotypes</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>genotype</b> of an organism is its complete set of genetic material.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Genotype can also be used to refer to the <a href="/wiki/Allele" title="Allele">alleles</a> or variants an individual carries in a particular gene or genetic location.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The number of alleles an individual can have in a specific gene depends on the number of copies of each <a href="/wiki/Chromosome" title="Chromosome">chromosome</a> found in that species, also referred to as <a href="/wiki/Ploidy" title="Ploidy">ploidy</a>. In diploid species like humans, two full sets of chromosomes are present, meaning each individual has two alleles for any given gene. If both alleles are the same, the genotype is referred to as <a href="/wiki/Zygosity" title="Zygosity">homozygous</a>. If the alleles are different, the genotype is referred to as heterozygous.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg/250px-Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="250" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg/500px-Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="550" data-file-height="550"></a><figcaption>Here the relation between genotype and phenotype is illustrated, using a <a href="/wiki/Punnett_square" title="Punnett square">Punnett square</a>, for the character of petal colour in a <a href="/wiki/Pea_plant" class="mw-redirect" title="Pea plant">pea plant</a>. The letters B and b represent alleles for colour and the pictures show the resultant flowers. The diagram shows the cross between two heterozygous parents where B represents the dominant allele (purple) and b represents the recessive allele (white).</figcaption></figure></div><p></p></div><div name="farmers" term="farmers" wikidataID="Q131512" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmers" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: farmers<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmers">Farmers</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>farmer</b> is a person engaged in <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a>, raising living organisms for food or raw materials.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The term usually applies to people who do some combination of raising field <a href="/wiki/Crops" class="mw-redirect" title="Crops">crops</a>, <a href="/wiki/Orchard" title="Orchard">orchards</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vineyard" title="Vineyard">vineyards</a>, <a href="/wiki/Poultry" title="Poultry">poultry</a>, or other <a href="/wiki/Livestock" title="Livestock">livestock</a>. A farmer might own the <a href="/wiki/Farmland" class="mw-redirect" title="Farmland">farmland</a> or might work as a <a href="/wiki/Laborer" title="Laborer">laborer</a> on land owned by others. In most <a href="/wiki/Developed_economies" class="mw-redirect" title="Developed economies">developed economies</a>, a "farmer" is usually a <a href="/wiki/Farm" title="Farm">farm</a> owner (<a href="/wiki/Landowner" class="mw-redirect" title="Landowner">landowner</a>), while employees of the farm are known as <i><a href="/wiki/Farm_workers" class="mw-redirect" title="Farm workers">farm workers</a></i> (or farmhands). However, in other older definitions a farmer was a person who promotes or improves the growth of plants, land, or crops or raises animals (as livestock or fish) by labor and attention.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Woman_at_work,_Gujarat.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Woman_at_work%2C_Gujarat.jpg/250px-Woman_at_work%2C_Gujarat.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="179" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Woman_at_work%2C_Gujarat.jpg/500px-Woman_at_work%2C_Gujarat.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3838" data-file-height="2741"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="NRRI" term="NRRI" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=NRRI" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: NRRI<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=NRRI">NRRI</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">
<i>The page "<a href="/w/index.php?title=NRRI&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="NRRI (page does not exist)">NRRI</a>" does not exist. You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="sugarcane" term="sugarcane" wikidataID="Q36940" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarcane" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: sugarcane<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarcane">Sugarcane</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Sugarcane</b> or <b>sugar cane</b> is a species of tall, <a href="/wiki/Perennial_plant" class="mw-redirect" title="Perennial plant">perennial</a> grass (in the genus <i><a href="/wiki/Saccharum" title="Saccharum">Saccharum</a></i>, tribe <a href="/wiki/Andropogoneae" title="Andropogoneae">Andropogoneae</a>) that is used for <a href="/wiki/Sugar" title="Sugar">sugar</a> <a href="/wiki/Sugar_industry" title="Sugar industry">production</a>. The plants are 2&#8211;6 m (6&#8211;20 ft) tall with stout, jointed, fibrous stalks that are rich in <a href="/wiki/Sucrose" title="Sucrose">sucrose</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> which accumulates in the <a href="/wiki/Plant_stem" title="Plant stem">stalk internodes</a>. Sugarcanes belong to the grass family, <a href="/wiki/Poaceae" title="Poaceae">Poaceae</a>, an economically important <a href="/wiki/Flowering_plant" title="Flowering plant">flowering plant</a> family that includes maize, wheat, rice, and <a href="/wiki/Sorghum" title="Sorghum">sorghum</a>, and many <a href="/wiki/Forage" title="Forage">forage</a> crops. It is native to <a href="/wiki/New_Guinea" title="New Guinea">New Guinea</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-POWO_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-POWO-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Saccharum_officinarum_-_K%C3%B6hler%E2%80%93s_Medizinal-Pflanzen-125.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Saccharum_officinarum_-_K%C3%B6hler%E2%80%93s_Medizinal-Pflanzen-125.jpg/250px-Saccharum_officinarum_-_K%C3%B6hler%E2%80%93s_Medizinal-Pflanzen-125.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="340" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/74/Saccharum_officinarum_-_K%C3%B6hler%E2%80%93s_Medizinal-Pflanzen-125.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="437" data-file-height="595"></a><figcaption><i><a href="/wiki/Saccharum_officinarum" title="Saccharum officinarum">Saccharum officinarum</a></i></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="reference varieties" term="reference varieties" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=reference%20varieties" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: reference varieties<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=reference%20varieties">reference varieties</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Agriculture" term="Agriculture" wikidataID="Q11451" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Agriculture<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture">Agriculture</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Agriculture</b> is the practice of cultivating the soil, planting, raising, and harvesting both food and non-food crops, as well as <a href="/wiki/Livestock" title="Livestock">livestock</a> production. Broader definitions also include <a href="/wiki/Forestry" title="Forestry">forestry</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aquaculture" title="Aquaculture">aquaculture</a>. Agriculture was a key factor in the rise of <a href="/wiki/Sedentism" title="Sedentism">sedentary</a> human <a href="/wiki/Civilization" title="Civilization">civilization</a>, whereby farming of <a href="/wiki/Domestication" title="Domestication">domesticated</a> plants and animals created food <a href="/wiki/Economic_surplus" title="Economic surplus">surpluses</a> that enabled people to live in the cities. While humans started gathering grains at least 105,000 years ago, nascent farmers only began planting them around 11,500 years ago. Sheep, goats, pigs, and cattle were domesticated around 10,000 years ago. Plants were independently cultivated in at least 11 regions of the world. In the 20th century, <a href="/wiki/Industrial_agriculture" title="Industrial agriculture">industrial agriculture</a> based on large-scale <a href="/wiki/Monoculture" title="Monoculture">monocultures</a> came to dominate agricultural output.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:PivotWithDrops.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PivotWithDrops.JPG/250px-PivotWithDrops.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="179" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PivotWithDrops.JPG/500px-PivotWithDrops.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="2100" data-file-height="1500"></a><figcaption>Modern agriculture: a <a href="/wiki/Center_pivot_irrigation" class="mw-redirect" title="Center pivot irrigation">center pivot irrigation</a> system on a field</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="cassava" term="cassava" wikidataID="Q83124" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassava" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: cassava<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassava">Cassava</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><i><b>Manihot esculenta</b></i>, <a href="/wiki/Common_name" title="Common name">commonly called</a> <b>cassava</b>, <b>manioc</b>, or <b>yuca</b> (among numerous regional names), is a woody <a href="/wiki/Shrub" title="Shrub">shrub</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Spurge" class="mw-redirect" title="Spurge">spurge</a> family, <a href="/wiki/Euphorbiaceae" title="Euphorbiaceae">Euphorbiaceae</a>, native to South America, from Brazil, Paraguay and parts of the <a href="/wiki/Andes" title="Andes">Andes</a>. Although a <a href="/wiki/Perennial" title="Perennial">perennial</a> plant, cassava is extensively cultivated in <a href="/wiki/Tropical" class="mw-redirect" title="Tropical">tropical</a> and <a href="/wiki/Subtropical" class="mw-redirect" title="Subtropical">subtropical</a> regions as an annual <a href="/wiki/Crop" title="Crop">crop</a> for its edible <a href="/wiki/Starch" title="Starch">starchy</a> <a href="/wiki/Tuber" title="Tuber">tuberous</a> root. Cassava is predominantly consumed in boiled form, but substantial quantities are processed to extract cassava starch, called <a href="/wiki/Tapioca" title="Tapioca">tapioca</a>, which is used for food, animal feed, and industrial purposes. The Brazilian <span title="Brazilian Portuguese-language text"><i lang="pt-BR">farofa</i></span>, and the related <i><a href="/wiki/Garri" title="Garri">garri</a></i> of West Africa, is an edible coarse flour obtained by grating cassava roots, pressing moisture off the obtained grated pulp, and finally drying and roasting it.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Thailand_19_lo_(4039130033).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Thailand_19_lo_%284039130033%29.jpg/250px-Thailand_19_lo_%284039130033%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Thailand_19_lo_%284039130033%29.jpg/500px-Thailand_19_lo_%284039130033%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4288" data-file-height="2848"></a><figcaption>An agronomist examines a diseased cassava crop in Thailand.</figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Genetic Improvement" term="Genetic Improvement" wikidataID="Q137398938" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_improvement" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Genetic Improvement<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_improvement">Genetic improvement</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Software" title="Software">computer software</a> development, <b>genetic improvement</b> is the use of <a href="/wiki/Mathematical_optimization" title="Mathematical optimization">optimisation</a> and <a href="/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning">machine learning</a> techniques, particularly <a href="/wiki/Search-based_software_engineering" title="Search-based software engineering">search-based software engineering</a> techniques such as <a href="/wiki/Genetic_programming" title="Genetic programming">genetic programming</a> to improve existing <a href="/wiki/Software" title="Software">software</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
The improved <a href="/wiki/Computer_program" title="Computer program">program</a> need not behave identically to the original. For example, <a href="/wiki/Automatic_bug_fixing" title="Automatic bug fixing">automatic bug fixing</a> improves <a href="/wiki/Executable_code" class="mw-redirect" title="Executable code">executable code</a> by reducing or eliminating <a href="/wiki/Software_bug" title="Software bug">buggy</a> behaviour.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
In other cases the improved software should behave identically to the old version but is better because,
for example:
it runs faster,<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
it uses less <a href="/wiki/Computer_memory" title="Computer memory">memory</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
it uses less <a href="/wiki/Electrical_energy" title="Electrical energy">energy</a><sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
or
it runs on a different type of computer.<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
GI differs from, for example, <a href="/wiki/Formal_methods" title="Formal methods">formal program translation</a>, in that it primarily verifies the behaviour of the new mutant version by running both the new and the old software on <a href="/wiki/Software_testing" title="Software testing">test inputs</a> and comparing their output and performance in order to see if the new software can still do what is wanted of the original program and is now better.
</p><p></p></div><div name="Nutritional Security" term="Nutritional Security" wikidataID="Q1229911" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutritional_security" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Nutritional Security<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutritional_security">Nutritional security</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Food security</b> is the state of having reliable access to a sufficient quantity of affordable, healthy <a href="/wiki/Human_food" title="Human food">food</a>. The availability of food for people of any class, gender, status, ethnicity, or religion is another element of food protection. Similarly, <a href="/wiki/Household" title="Household">household</a> food security is considered to exist when all the members of a family have consistent access to enough food for an active, <a href="/wiki/Health" title="Health">healthy</a> life.<sup id="cite_ref-usda_measuring_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-usda_measuring-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Food-secure individuals do not live in <a href="/wiki/Hunger" title="Hunger">hunger</a> or fear of <a href="/wiki/Starvation" title="Starvation">starvation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FAO_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FAO-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Food security includes resilience to future disruptions of food supply. Such a disruption could occur due to various risk factors such as <a href="/wiki/Drought" title="Drought">droughts</a> and <a href="/wiki/Flood" title="Flood">floods</a><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>, shipping disruptions, fuel shortages, economic instability, and wars.<sup id="cite_ref-FAO-2013_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FAO-2013-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <b>Food insecurity</b> is the opposite of food security: a state where there is only limited or uncertain availability of suitable food.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Africa_Food_Security_18_(10665134354).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg/250px-Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="376" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg/500px-Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1880" data-file-height="2825"></a><figcaption>Women selling <a href="/wiki/Produce" title="Produce">produce</a> at a market in <a href="/wiki/Lilongwe" title="Lilongwe">Lilongwe</a>, <a href="/wiki/Malawi" title="Malawi">Malawi</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="grain yield" term="grain yield" wikidataID="Q889514" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grain_yield" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: grain yield<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grain_yield">Grain yield</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a>, the <b>yield</b> is a measurement of the amount of a <a href="/wiki/Crop" title="Crop">crop</a> grown, or product such as wool, meat or milk produced, per unit area of land. The <b>seed ratio</b> is another way of calculating yields.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cereal-crop-yield-vs-fertilizer-application_(OWID_0112).png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Cereal-crop-yield-vs-fertilizer-application_%28OWID_0112%29.png/330px-Cereal-crop-yield-vs-fertilizer-application_%28OWID_0112%29.png" decoding="async" width="275" height="194" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Cereal-crop-yield-vs-fertilizer-application_%28OWID_0112%29.png/500px-Cereal-crop-yield-vs-fertilizer-application_%28OWID_0112%29.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c4/Cereal-crop-yield-vs-fertilizer-application_%28OWID_0112%29.png 2x" data-file-width="850" data-file-height="600"></a><figcaption>Cereal yield in tons per hectare and kilograms of nitrogenous fertilizer applied per hectare of cropland.</figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Climate Change" term="Climate Change" wikidataID="Q125928" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_Change" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Climate Change<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_Change">Climate Change</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">Present-day <b>climate change</b> includes both <b>global warming</b>&#8212;the ongoing increase in <a href="/wiki/Global_surface_temperature" title="Global surface temperature">global average temperature</a>&#8212;and its wider effects on Earth's <a href="/wiki/Climate_system" title="Climate system">climate system</a>. <a href="/wiki/Climate_variability_and_change" title="Climate variability and change">Climate change in a broader sense</a> also includes previous long-term changes to Earth's <a href="/wiki/Climate" title="Climate">climate</a>. The modern-day rise in global temperatures is <a href="/wiki/Scientific_consensus_on_climate_change" title="Scientific consensus on climate change">driven by human activities</a>, especially <a href="/wiki/Fossil_fuel" title="Fossil fuel">fossil fuel</a> (<a href="/wiki/Coal" title="Coal">coal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Petroleum" title="Petroleum">oil</a> and <a href="/wiki/Natural_gas" title="Natural gas">natural gas</a>) burning since the <a href="/wiki/Industrial_Revolution" title="Industrial Revolution">Industrial Revolution</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Lynas_2021_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Lynas_2021-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Fossil fuel use, <a href="/wiki/Deforestation_and_climate_change" title="Deforestation and climate change">deforestation</a>, and some <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions_from_agriculture" title="Greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture">agricultural</a> and industrial practices release <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_gas" title="Greenhouse gas">greenhouse gases</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Our_World_in_Data-2020_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Our_World_in_Data-2020-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> These gases <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_effect" title="Greenhouse effect">absorb some of the heat</a> that the Earth <a href="/wiki/Thermal_radiation" title="Thermal radiation">radiates</a> after it warms from sunlight, warming the lower atmosphere. Earth's atmosphere now has <a href="/wiki/Carbon_dioxide_in_the_atmosphere_of_Earth" title="Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere of Earth">roughly 50% more carbon dioxide</a>, the main gas driving global warming, than it did at the end of the <a href="/wiki/Pre-industrial_society" title="Pre-industrial society">pre-industrial era</a>, reaching levels not seen for millions of years.<sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Common_Era_Temperature.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Common_Era_Temperature.svg/500px-Common_Era_Temperature.svg.png" decoding="async" width="340" height="255" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Common_Era_Temperature.svg/960px-Common_Era_Temperature.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="720"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Global_surface_temperature" title="Global surface temperature">Global surface temperature</a> reconstruction over the past 2000 years using proxy data from tree rings, corals, and ice cores in blue.<sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Directly observed data is in red.<sup id="cite_ref-nasa_temperatures_44-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nasa_temperatures-44"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>

title="Odisha">Odisha</a>. It is also the headquarters of the <a href="/wiki/Cuttack_district" title="Cuttack district">Cuttack district</a>. The name of the city is an anglicised form of the <a href="/wiki/Odia_language" title="Odia language">Odia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sanskrit" title="Sanskrit">Sanskrit</a> name <i>Kataka</i>, which literally means <i>the fort</i>, a reference to the ancient <a href="/wiki/Barabati_Fort" class="mw-redirect" title="Barabati Fort">Barabati Fort</a> around which the city initially developed. Cuttack is known as the <i>Millennium City</i> as well as the <i>Silver City</i> due to its history of 1000 years and famous silver filigree works respectively. The <a href="/wiki/Orissa_High_Court" title="Orissa High Court">Orissa High Court</a><sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and some other Odisha State Govt. offices are located there, and the city is the judicial capital of Odisha.

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="germplasm" term="germplasm" wikidataID="Q589029" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germplasm" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: germplasm<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germplasm">Germplasm</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Germplasm</b> refers to <a href="/wiki/Genetic_resources" title="Genetic resources">genetic resources</a> such as seeds, tissues, and DNA sequences that are maintained for the purpose of <a href="/wiki/Animal_husbandry" title="Animal husbandry">animal</a> and <a href="/wiki/Plant_breeding" title="Plant breeding">plant breeding</a>, conservation efforts, agriculture, and other research uses. These resources may take the form of seed collections stored in <a href="/wiki/Seedbank" class="mw-redirect" title="Seedbank">seed banks</a>, trees growing in nurseries, animal breeding lines maintained in animal breeding programs or <a href="/wiki/Gene_bank" title="Gene bank">gene banks</a>. Germplasm collections can range from collections of wild species to elite, domesticated breeding lines that have undergone extensive human selection. Germplasm collection is important for the maintenance of biological diversity, food security, and conservation efforts.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:INTA_-_Banco_de_germoplasma.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/INTA_-_Banco_de_germoplasma.jpg/250px-INTA_-_Banco_de_germoplasma.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/INTA_-_Banco_de_germoplasma.jpg/500px-INTA_-_Banco_de_germoplasma.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3216" data-file-height="2136"></a><figcaption>Germplasm bank of the <a href="/wiki/Instituto_Nacional_de_Tecnolog%C3%ADa_Agropecuaria" class="mw-redirect" title="Instituto Nacional de Tecnolog&#237;a Agropecuaria">Instituto Nacional de Tecnolog&#237;a Agropecuaria</a>.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="sweet potato" term="sweet potato" wikidataID="Q37937" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet_potato" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: sweet potato<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet_potato">Sweet potato</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>sweet potato</b> or <b>sweetpotato</b><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> (<i>Ipomoea batatas</i>) is a <a href="/wiki/Dicotyledon" title="Dicotyledon">dicotyledonous</a> plant in the morning glory family, <a href="/wiki/Convolvulaceae" title="Convolvulaceae">Convolvulaceae</a>. Its sizeable, <a href="/wiki/Starch" title="Starch">starchy</a>, sweet-tasting <a href="/wiki/Tuberous_root" class="mw-redirect" title="Tuberous root">tuberous roots</a> are used as a <a href="/wiki/Root_vegetable" title="Root vegetable">root vegetable</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Purseglove,_1991_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Purseglove,_1991-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Woolfe,_1992_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Woolfe,_1992-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> which is a <a href="/wiki/Staple_food" title="Staple food">staple food</a> in parts of the world. <a href="/wiki/Sweet_potato_cultivars" class="mw-redirect" title="Sweet potato cultivars">Cultivars of the sweet potato</a> have been bred to bear tubers with flesh and skin of various colors. Moreover, the young shoots and leaves are occasionally eaten as <a href="/wiki/Leaf_vegetable" title="Leaf vegetable">greens</a>. The sweet potato and the <a href="/wiki/Potato" title="Potato">potato</a> are only distantly related, both being in the order <a href="/wiki/Solanales" title="Solanales">Solanales</a>. Although darker sweet potatoes are often known as yams in parts of North America, they are even more distant from actual <a href="/wiki/Yam_(vegetable)" title="Yam (vegetable)">yams</a>, which are <a href="/wiki/Monocots" class="mw-redirect" title="Monocots">monocots</a> in the order <a href="/wiki/Dioscoreales" title="Dioscoreales">Dioscoreales</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Genasu_gadde_(Kannada_%E0%B2%97%E0%B3%86%E0%B2%A3%E0%B2%B8%E0%B3%81_%E0%B2%97%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%8D%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%86)_(49108875711).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Genasu_gadde_%28Kannada_%E0%B2%97%E0%B3%86%E0%B2%A3%E0%B2%B8%E0%B3%81_%E0%B2%97%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%8D%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%86%29_%2849108875711%29.jpg/250px-Genasu_gadde_%28Kannada_%E0%B2%97%E0%B3%86%E0%B2%A3%E0%B2%B8%E0%B3%81_%E0%B2%97%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%8D%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%86%29_%2849108875711%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Genasu_gadde_%28Kannada_%E0%B2%97%E0%B3%86%E0%B2%A3%E0%B2%B8%E0%B3%81_%E0%B2%97%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%8D%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%86%29_%2849108875711%29.jpg/500px-Genasu_gadde_%28Kannada_%E0%B2%97%E0%B3%86%E0%B2%A3%E0%B2%B8%E0%B3%81_%E0%B2%97%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%8D%E0%B2%A1%E0%B3%86%29_%2849108875711%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4864" data-file-height="3648"></a><figcaption>The flowers, buds, and leaves of the sweet potato, which resemble those of the <a href="/wiki/Morning_glory" title="Morning glory">morning glory</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="drought" term="drought" wikidataID="Q43059" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: drought<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought">Drought</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>drought</b> is a period of drier-than-normal conditions.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 1157">:&#8202;1157&#8202;</span></sup> A drought can last for days, months or years. Drought often has large impacts on the <a href="/wiki/Ecosystem" title="Ecosystem">ecosystems</a> and <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a> of affected regions, and causes harm to the local <a href="/wiki/Economy" title="Economy">economy</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Annual dry seasons in the <a href="/wiki/Tropics" title="Tropics">tropics</a> significantly increase the chances of a drought developing, with subsequent increased <a href="/wiki/Wildfire" title="Wildfire">wildfire</a> risks.<sup id="cite_ref-Brando_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Brando-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Heat_wave" title="Heat wave">Heat waves</a> can significantly worsen drought conditions by increasing <a href="/wiki/Evapotranspiration" title="Evapotranspiration">evapotranspiration</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Merzdorf_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Merzdorf-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This dries out forests and other vegetation, and increases the amount of fuel for wildfires.<sup id="cite_ref-Brando_4-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Brando-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Hartmann_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hartmann-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Fields_outside_benambra.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Fields_outside_benambra.jpg/500px-Fields_outside_benambra.jpg" decoding="async" width="400" height="164" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Fields_outside_benambra.jpg/960px-Fields_outside_benambra.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2250" data-file-height="924"></a><figcaption>Fields outside <a href="/wiki/Benambra,_Victoria" class="mw-redirect" title="Benambra, Victoria">Benambra</a>, Australia suffering from drought in 2006.</figcaption></figure>

spelled <b>Orissa</b> until 2011,<sup id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India" title="States and union territories of India">state</a> located in <a href="/wiki/East_India" title="East India">Eastern India</a>. It is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_area" title="List of states and union territories of India by area">eighth-largest state by area</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_population" title="List of states and union territories of India by population">eleventh-largest by population</a>, with over 41 million inhabitants. The state also has the third-largest population of <a href="/wiki/Scheduled_Castes_and_Scheduled_Tribes" title="Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes">Scheduled Tribes</a> in <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It neighbours the states of <a href="/wiki/Jharkhand" title="Jharkhand">Jharkhand</a> and <a href="/wiki/West_Bengal" title="West Bengal">West Bengal</a> to the north, <a href="/wiki/Chhattisgarh" title="Chhattisgarh">Chhattisgarh</a> to the west, and <a href="/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh" title="Andhra Pradesh">Andhra Pradesh</a> to the south. Odisha has a <a href="/wiki/Coastline" class="mw-redirect" title="Coastline">coastline</a> of 485 kilometres (301&#160;mi) along the <a href="/wiki/Bay_of_Bengal" title="Bay of Bengal">Bay of Bengal</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Indian_Ocean" title="Indian Ocean">Indian Ocean</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-CoastalSecurity_21-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CoastalSecurity-21"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The region is also known as <b>Utka&#7735;a</b> and is mentioned by this name in India's national anthem, <a href="/wiki/Jana_Gana_Mana" title="Jana Gana Mana">Jana Gana Mana</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:IN-OD.svg" class="mw-file-description" title="Location of Odisha in India"><img alt="The map of India showing Odisha" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/IN-OD.svg/330px-IN-OD.svg.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="342" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/IN-OD.svg/500px-IN-OD.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/IN-OD.svg/960px-IN-OD.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="512" data-file-height="583"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="DUS testing" term="DUS testing" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=DUS%20testing" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: DUS testing<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=DUS%20testing">DUS testing</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">
<i>The page "<a href="/w/index.php?title=DUS_testing&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="DUS testing (page does not exist)">DUS testing</a>" does not exist. You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Rice Pests" term="Rice Pests" wikidataID="Q5090" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_pests" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Rice Pests<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_pests">Rice pests</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Rice</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Cereal_grain" class="mw-redirect" title="Cereal grain">cereal grain</a> and in its <a href="/wiki/Domestication" title="Domestication">domesticated</a> form is the <a href="/wiki/Staple_food" title="Staple food">staple food</a> of over half of the <a href="/wiki/World%27s_population" class="mw-redirect" title="World's population">world's population</a>, particularly in <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Africa" title="Africa">Africa</a>. Rice is the seed of the grass species <i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_sativa" title="Oryza sativa">Oryza sativa</a></i> (Asian rice)&#8212;or, much less commonly, <i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_glaberrima" title="Oryza glaberrima">Oryza glaberrima</a></i> (African rice). Asian rice was domesticated in <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a> some 13,500 to 8,200 years ago; African rice was domesticated in Africa about 3,000 years ago. Rice has become commonplace in many cultures worldwide; in 2023, 800 million tons were produced, placing it third after <a href="/wiki/Sugarcane" title="Sugarcane">sugarcane</a> and <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">maize</a>. Only some 8% of rice is traded internationally. China, India, and Indonesia are the largest consumers of rice. A substantial amount of the rice produced in developing nations is lost after harvest through factors such as poor transport and storage. Rice yields can be reduced by pests including <a href="/wiki/Insect" title="Insect">insects</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rodent" title="Rodent">rodents</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Bird" title="Bird">birds</a>, as well as by <a href="/wiki/Weed" title="Weed">weeds</a>, and by <a href="/wiki/List_of_rice_diseases" title="List of rice diseases">diseases</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Rice_blast" class="mw-redirect" title="Rice blast">rice blast</a>. Traditional <a href="/wiki/Rice_polyculture" title="Rice polyculture">rice polycultures</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Rice-duck_farming" title="Rice-duck farming">rice-duck farming</a>, and modern <a href="/wiki/Integrated_pest_management" title="Integrated pest management">integrated pest management</a> seek to control damage from pests in a <a href="/wiki/Sustainable_agriculture" title="Sustainable agriculture">sustainable</a> way.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg/500px-20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg" decoding="async" width="340" height="191" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg/960px-20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="720"></a><figcaption>Rice plant (<i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_sativa" title="Oryza sativa">Oryza sativa</a></i>) with branched <a href="/wiki/Panicle" title="Panicle">panicles</a> containing many grains on each stem</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Plant Genetic Resources" term="Plant Genetic Resources" wikidataID="Q55630097" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_Genetic_Resources" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Plant Genetic Resources<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_Genetic_Resources">Plant Genetic Resources</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Plant genetic resources</b> describe the variability within plants that comes from human and natural selection over millennia. Their intrinsic value mainly concerns agricultural crops (<a href="/wiki/Crop_biodiversity" class="mw-redirect" title="Crop biodiversity">crop biodiversity</a>).
</p><p></p></div><div name="Productivity" term="Productivity" wikidataID="Q2111958" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Productivity" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Productivity<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Productivity">Productivity</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b><a href="/wiki/Normative_economics" class="mw-redirect" title="Normative economics">Prescriptive</a> and policy</b>
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Labour_productivity_levels_in_europe.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Labour_productivity_levels_in_europe.svg/250px-Labour_productivity_levels_in_europe.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="176" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Labour_productivity_levels_in_europe.svg/500px-Labour_productivity_levels_in_europe.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="744" data-file-height="524"></a><figcaption>Labour productivity levels in 2012 in Europe. <a href="/wiki/OECD" title="OECD">OECD</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="agriculture" term="agriculture" wikidataID="Q11451" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: agriculture<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture">Agriculture</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Agriculture</b> is the practice of cultivating the soil, planting, raising, and harvesting both food and non-food crops, as well as <a href="/wiki/Livestock" title="Livestock">livestock</a> production. Broader definitions also include <a href="/wiki/Forestry" title="Forestry">forestry</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aquaculture" title="Aquaculture">aquaculture</a>. Agriculture was a key factor in the rise of <a href="/wiki/Sedentism" title="Sedentism">sedentary</a> human <a href="/wiki/Civilization" title="Civilization">civilization</a>, whereby farming of <a href="/wiki/Domestication" title="Domestication">domesticated</a> plants and animals created food <a href="/wiki/Economic_surplus" title="Economic surplus">surpluses</a> that enabled people to live in the cities. While humans started gathering grains at least 105,000 years ago, nascent farmers only began planting them around 11,500 years ago. Sheep, goats, pigs, and cattle were domesticated around 10,000 years ago. Plants were independently cultivated in at least 11 regions of the world. In the 20th century, <a href="/wiki/Industrial_agriculture" title="Industrial agriculture">industrial agriculture</a> based on large-scale <a href="/wiki/Monoculture" title="Monoculture">monocultures</a> came to dominate agricultural output.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:PivotWithDrops.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PivotWithDrops.JPG/250px-PivotWithDrops.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="179" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PivotWithDrops.JPG/500px-PivotWithDrops.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="2100" data-file-height="1500"></a><figcaption>Modern agriculture: a <a href="/wiki/Center_pivot_irrigation" class="mw-redirect" title="Center pivot irrigation">center pivot irrigation</a> system on a field</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="genotype" term="genotype" wikidataID="Q106016" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: genotype<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genotype">Genotype</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>genotype</b> of an organism is its complete set of genetic material.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Genotype can also be used to refer to the <a href="/wiki/Allele" title="Allele">alleles</a> or variants an individual carries in a particular gene or genetic location.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The number of alleles an individual can have in a specific gene depends on the number of copies of each <a href="/wiki/Chromosome" title="Chromosome">chromosome</a> found in that species, also referred to as <a href="/wiki/Ploidy" title="Ploidy">ploidy</a>. In diploid species like humans, two full sets of chromosomes are present, meaning each individual has two alleles for any given gene. If both alleles are the same, the genotype is referred to as <a href="/wiki/Zygosity" title="Zygosity">homozygous</a>. If the alleles are different, the genotype is referred to as heterozygous.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg/250px-Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="250" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg/500px-Punnett_square_mendel_flowers.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="550" data-file-height="550"></a><figcaption>Here the relation between genotype and phenotype is illustrated, using a <a href="/wiki/Punnett_square" title="Punnett square">Punnett square</a>, for the character of petal colour in a <a href="/wiki/Pea_plant" class="mw-redirect" title="Pea plant">pea plant</a>. The letters B and b represent alleles for colour and the pictures show the resultant flowers. The diagram shows the cross between two heterozygous parents where B represents the dominant allele (purple) and b represents the recessive allele (white).</figcaption></figure></div><p></p></div><div name="hybrids" term="hybrids" wikidataID="Q676784" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrids" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: hybrids<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrids">Hybrids</a></p><p></p></div><div name="Biotechnology" term="Biotechnology" wikidataID="Q7108" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Biotechnology<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology">Biotechnology</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Biotechnology</b> is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of <a href="/wiki/Natural_science" title="Natural science">natural sciences</a> and <a href="/wiki/Engineering_Science" class="mw-redirect" title="Engineering Science">engineering sciences</a> in order to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Specialists in the field are known as <b>biotechnologists</b>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg/250px-Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="385" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg/500px-Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3629" data-file-height="5594"></a><figcaption>A biologist conducting research in a biotechnology laboratory</figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Sustainability" term="Sustainability" wikidataID="Q219416" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainability" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Sustainability<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainability">Sustainability</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Sustainability</b> (from the latin <i>sustinere</i> - hold up, hold upright; furnish with means of support; bear, undergo, endure) is the ability to continue over a long period of time.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In modern usage it generally refers to a state in which the environment, economy, and society will continue to exist over a long period of time.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Many definitions emphasize the environmental dimension.<sup id="cite_ref-Kotze-2022_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kotze-2022-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Bosselmann-2010_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bosselmann-2010-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This can include addressing key <a href="/wiki/Environmental_issues" title="Environmental issues">environmental problems</a>, such as <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">climate change</a> and <a href="/wiki/Biodiversity_loss" title="Biodiversity loss">biodiversity loss</a>. The idea of sustainability can guide decisions at the global, national, organizational, and individual levels.<sup id="cite_ref-Berg-2020_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Berg-2020-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A related concept is that of <a href="/wiki/Sustainable_development" title="Sustainable development">sustainable development</a>, and the terms are often used to mean the same thing.<sup id="cite_ref-EB-2022_7-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EB-2022-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> distinguishes the two like this: "<i>Sustainability</i> is often thought of as a long-term goal (i.e. a more sustainable world), while <i>sustainable development</i> refers to the many processes and pathways to achieve it."<sup id="cite_ref-UNESCO-2015_8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UNESCO-2015-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp/250px-Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="159" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp/500px-Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp.png 1.5x" data-file-width="869" data-file-height="553"></a><figcaption>Three visual representations of sustainability and its three dimensions. The left image shows sustainability as three intersecting circles. The top right is a nested approach where social and economic sustainability are contained within environmental sustainability. The bottom right shows pillars with the different components holding up sustainability.</figcaption></figure>

arecanut<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arecanut">Arecanut</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>areca nut</b> (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/&#712;/: primary stress follows">&#712;</span><span title="/&#230;r/: 'arr' in 'marry'">&#230;r</span><span title="/&#618;/: 'i' in 'kit'">&#618;</span><span title="'k' in 'kind'">k</span><span title="/&#601;/: 'a' in 'about'">&#601;</span></span>/</a></span></span> or <span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/&#601;/: 'a' in 'about'">&#601;</span><span title="/&#712;/: primary stress follows">&#712;</span><span title="'r' in 'rye'">r</span><span title="/i&#720;/: 'ee' in 'fleece'">i&#720;</span><span title="'k' in 'kind'">k</span><span title="/&#601;/: 'a' in 'about'">&#601;</span></span>/</a></span></span>) (also improperly called <b>betel nut</b>) (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/&#712;/: primary stress follows">&#712;</span><span title="'b' in 'buy'">b</span><span title="/i&#720;/: 'ee' in 'fleece'">i&#720;</span><span title="'t' in 'tie'">t</span><span title="/&#601;/: 'a' in 'about'">&#601;</span><span title="'l' in 'lie'">l</span></span>/</a></span></span>) is the seed of a palm belonging to the <a href="/wiki/Areca" title="Areca">areca</a> genus (<i><a href="/wiki/Areca_catechu" title="Areca catechu">Areca catechu</a></i>). The palm is originally native to the <a href="/wiki/Philippines" title="Philippines">Philippines</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Zumbroich2007_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Zumbroich2007-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-powo_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-powo-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> but was carried widely through the tropics by the <a href="/wiki/Austronesian_expansion" class="mw-redirect" title="Austronesian expansion">Austronesian migrations</a> and <a href="/wiki/Spice_trade" title="Spice trade">trade</a> since at least 1500 BCE due to its use in <a href="/wiki/Betel_nut_chewing" title="Betel nut chewing">betel nut chewing</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Zumbroich2007_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Zumbroich2007-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is widespread in cultivation and is considered naturalized in much of the tropical Pacific (<a href="/wiki/Melanesia" title="Melanesia">Melanesia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Micronesia" title="Micronesia">Micronesia</a>), <a href="/wiki/South_Asia" title="South Asia">South Asia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Asia" title="Southeast Asia">Southeast Asia</a>, and parts of east Africa. It is not to be confused with <a href="/wiki/Betel" title="Betel">betel</a> (<i>Piper betle</i>) leaves that are often used to wrap it. The practice of betel nut chewing, often together with other herbs as a <a href="/wiki/Stimulant_drug" class="mw-redirect" title="Stimulant drug">stimulant drug</a>, dates back thousands of years, and continues to the present day in many countries.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Bago,_mercado_23.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/Bago%2C_mercado_23.jpg/250px-Bago%2C_mercado_23.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/Bago%2C_mercado_23.jpg/500px-Bago%2C_mercado_23.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4288" data-file-height="2848"></a><figcaption>Areca nuts</figcaption></figure>
