Well-known <a href="/wiki/Taxonomy_of_wheat" title="Taxonomy of wheat">wheat species and hybrids</a> include the most widely grown <a href="/wiki/Common_wheat" title="Common wheat">common wheat</a> (<i>T. aestivum</i>), <a href="/wiki/Spelt" title="Spelt">spelt</a>, <a href="/wiki/Durum" class="mw-redirect" title="Durum">durum</a>, <a href="/wiki/Emmer" title="Emmer">emmer</a>, <a href="/wiki/Einkorn" title="Einkorn">einkorn</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Khorasan_wheat" title="Khorasan wheat">Khorasan or Kamut</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Archaeological_record" title="Archaeological record">archaeological record</a> suggests that wheat was first cultivated in the regions of the <a href="/wiki/Fertile_Crescent" title="Fertile Crescent">Fertile Crescent</a> around 9600 BC.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:K%C3%B6hler%27s_Medizinal-Pflanzen_in_naturgetreuen_Abbildungen_mit_kurz_erl%C3%A4uterndem_Texte_(Plate_87)_(8231709397).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/K%C3%B6hler%27s_Medizinal-Pflanzen_in_naturgetreuen_Abbildungen_mit_kurz_erl%C3%A4uterndem_Texte_%28Plate_87%29_%288231709397%29.jpg/250px-K%C3%B6hler%27s_Medizinal-Pflanzen_in_naturgetreuen_Abbildungen_mit_kurz_erl%C3%A4uterndem_Texte_%28Plate_87%29_%288231709397%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="358" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/K%C3%B6hler%27s_Medizinal-Pflanzen_in_naturgetreuen_Abbildungen_mit_kurz_erl%C3%A4uterndem_Texte_%28Plate_87%29_%288231709397%29.jpg/500px-K%C3%B6hler%27s_Medizinal-Pflanzen_in_naturgetreuen_Abbildungen_mit_kurz_erl%C3%A4uterndem_Texte_%28Plate_87%29_%288231709397%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1402" data-file-height="2005"></a><figcaption>A: Plant; B ripe ear of corn; 1 <a href="/wiki/Spikelet" title="Spikelet">spikelet</a> before flowering; 2 the same, flowering and spread, enlarged; 3 flowers with <a href="/wiki/Glume" title="Glume">glumes</a>; 4 <a href="/wiki/Stamen" title="Stamen">stamens</a>; 5 <a href="/wiki/Pollen" title="Pollen">pollen</a>; 6 and 7 ovaries with juice scales; 8 and 9 parts of the scar; 10 fruit husks; 11, 12, 13 seeds, natural size and enlarged; 14 the same cut up, enlarged.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="nutritional security" term="nutritional security" wikidataID="Q1229911" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutritional_security" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: nutritional security<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutritional_security">Nutritional security</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Food security</b> is the state of having reliable access to a sufficient quantity of affordable, healthy <a href="/wiki/Human_food" title="Human food">food</a>. The availability of food for people of any class, gender, status, ethnicity, or religion is another element of food protection. Similarly, <a href="/wiki/Household" title="Household">household</a> food security is considered to exist when all the members of a family have consistent access to enough food for an active, <a href="/wiki/Health" title="Health">healthy</a> life.<sup id="cite_ref-usda_measuring_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-usda_measuring-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Food-secure individuals do not live in <a href="/wiki/Hunger" title="Hunger">hunger</a> or fear of <a href="/wiki/Starvation" title="Starvation">starvation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FAO_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FAO-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Food security includes resilience to future disruptions of food supply. Such a disruption could occur due to various risk factors such as <a href="/wiki/Drought" title="Drought">droughts</a> and <a href="/wiki/Flood" title="Flood">floods</a><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>, shipping disruptions, fuel shortages, economic instability, and wars.<sup id="cite_ref-FAO-2013_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FAO-2013-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <b>Food insecurity</b> is the opposite of food security: a state where there is only limited or uncertain availability of suitable food.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Africa_Food_Security_18_(10665134354).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg/250px-Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="376" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg/500px-Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1880" data-file-height="2825"></a><figcaption>Women selling <a href="/wiki/Produce" title="Produce">produce</a> at a market in <a href="/wiki/Lilongwe" title="Lilongwe">Lilongwe</a>, <a href="/wiki/Malawi" title="Malawi">Malawi</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Plant Pathology" term="Plant Pathology" wikidataID="Q188956" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_Pathology" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Plant Pathology<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_Pathology">Plant Pathology</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Plant pathology</b> or <b>phytopathology</b> is the scientific study of <a href="/wiki/Plant_disease" title="Plant disease">plant diseases</a> caused by <a href="/wiki/Pathogen" title="Pathogen">pathogens</a> (infectious organisms) and environmental conditions (physiological factors).<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Plant pathology involves the study of pathogen identification, disease <a href="/wiki/Etiology" title="Etiology">etiology</a>, disease cycles, economic impact, <a href="/wiki/Plant_disease_epidemiology" title="Plant disease epidemiology">plant disease epidemiology</a>, <a href="/wiki/Plant_disease_resistance" title="Plant disease resistance">plant disease resistance</a>, how plant diseases affect humans and animals, <a href="/wiki/Pathosystem" title="Pathosystem">pathosystem</a> genetics, and management of plant diseases.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Black_rot_lifecycle.tif" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Black_rot_lifecycle.tif/lossy-page1-440px-Black_rot_lifecycle.tif.jpg" decoding="async" width="440" height="353" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Black_rot_lifecycle.tif/lossy-page1-660px-Black_rot_lifecycle.tif.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Black_rot_lifecycle.tif/lossy-page1-880px-Black_rot_lifecycle.tif.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1270" data-file-height="1020"></a><figcaption>Life cycle of the black rot pathogen, the <a href="/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria" title="Gram-negative bacteria">gram negative</a> bacterium <a href="/wiki/Xanthomonas_campestris_pv._campestris" title="Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris"><i>Xanthomonas campestris</i> pathovar <i>campestris</i></a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="coconut" term="coconut" wikidataID="Q13187" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: coconut<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut">Coconut</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>coconut</b> (<i><b>Cocos nucifera</b></i>) is a member of the palm <a href="/wiki/Family_(biology)" title="Family (biology)">family</a> (<a href="/wiki/Arecaceae" title="Arecaceae">Arecaceae</a>) and the only living <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Genus" title="Genus">genus</a> <i>Cocos</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-WCSP_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WCSP-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The term "coconut" (or the archaic "<b>cocoanut</b>")<sup id="cite_ref-COD_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-COD-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> can denote the whole <b>coconut palm</b> <a href="/wiki/Tree" title="Tree">tree</a> or the large hard <a href="/wiki/Fruit" title="Fruit">fruit</a>. Originally native to <a href="/wiki/Central_Indo-Pacific" title="Central Indo-Pacific">Central Indo-Pacific</a>, they are ubiquitous in coastal tropical regions.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg/250px-Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="253" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg/330px-Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg/500px-Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg 2x" data-file-width="6000" data-file-height="8000"></a><figcaption>Fruit with husk partly removed, showing hard thin shell of <a href="/wiki/Endocarp" class="mw-redirect" title="Endocarp">endocarp</a> (left), <a href="/wiki/Coir" title="Coir">coir</a> fibre of exocarp (right)</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="USA" term="USA" wikidataID="Q30" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: USA<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA">USA</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>United States of America</b> (<b>USA</b>), also known as the <b>United States</b> (<b>U.S.</b>) or <b>America</b>, is a country primarily located in <a href="/wiki/North_America" title="North America">North America</a>. It is a <a href="/wiki/Federal_republic" title="Federal republic">federal republic</a> of 50 <a href="/wiki/U.S._state" title="U.S. state">states</a> and a <a href="/wiki/Capital_districts_and_territories" title="Capital districts and territories">federal capital district</a>, <a href="/wiki/Washington,_D.C." title="Washington, D.C.">Washington, D.C.</a> The 48 <a href="/wiki/Contiguous_states" class="mw-redirect" title="Contiguous states">contiguous states</a> border <a href="/wiki/Canada" title="Canada">Canada</a> to the north and <a href="/wiki/Mexico" title="Mexico">Mexico</a> to the south, with the <a href="/wiki/Semi-exclave" class="mw-redirect" title="Semi-exclave">semi-exclave</a> of <a href="/wiki/Alaska" title="Alaska">Alaska</a> in the northwest and the <a href="/wiki/Archipelago" title="Archipelago">archipelago</a> of <a href="/wiki/Hawaii" title="Hawaii">Hawaii</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Pacific_Ocean" title="Pacific Ocean">Pacific Ocean</a>. The United States also asserts sovereignty over five <a href="/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States" title="Territories of the United States">major island territories</a> and <a href="/wiki/United_States_Minor_Outlying_Islands" title="United States Minor Outlying Islands">various uninhabited islands</a> in <a href="/wiki/Oceania" title="Oceania">Oceania</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Caribbean" title="Caribbean">Caribbean</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>j<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is a <a href="/wiki/Megadiverse_country" class="mw-redirect" title="Megadiverse country">megadiverse country</a>, with the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area" title="List of countries and dependencies by area">third-largest land area</a><sup id="cite_ref-largestcountry_15-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-largestcountry-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>c<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population" title="List of countries and dependencies by population">third-largest population</a>, exceeding 341 million.<sup id="cite_ref-pop_clock_32-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pop_clock-32"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>k<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Extreme_Makeover,_Mesa_Verde_Edition_-_panoramio.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Extreme_Makeover%2C_Mesa_Verde_Edition_-_panoramio.jpg/250px-Extreme_Makeover%2C_Mesa_Verde_Edition_-_panoramio.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Extreme_Makeover%2C_Mesa_Verde_Edition_-_panoramio.jpg/500px-Extreme_Makeover%2C_Mesa_Verde_Edition_-_panoramio.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4256" data-file-height="2832"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Cliff_Palace" title="Cliff Palace">Cliff Palace</a>, a settlement of <a href="/wiki/Ancestral_Puebloans" title="Ancestral Puebloans">ancestors of</a> the <a href="/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States" title="Native Americans in the United States">Native American</a> <a href="/wiki/Pueblo_peoples" title="Pueblo peoples">Pueblo peoples</a> in present-day <a href="/wiki/Montezuma_County,_Colorado" title="Montezuma County, Colorado">Montezuma County, Colorado</a>, built between <abbr title="circa">c.</abbr><span style="white-space:nowrap;">&#8201;1200 and 1275</span><sup id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>34<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="fungicides" term="fungicides" wikidataID="Q193237" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungicides" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: fungicides<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungicides">Fungicides</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Fungicides</b> are <a href="/wiki/Pesticide" title="Pesticide">pesticides</a> used to kill <a href="/wiki/Parasitic_fungi" class="mw-redirect" title="Parasitic fungi">parasitic fungi</a> or their <a href="/wiki/Spore" title="Spore">spores</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-KO_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-KO-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ullmann_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ullmann-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  Fungi can cause serious damage in <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a>, resulting in losses of yield and quality. Fungicides are used both in agriculture and to fight <a href="/wiki/Fungal_infections_in_animals" class="mw-redirect" title="Fungal infections in animals">fungal infections in animals</a>, including humans. Fungicides are also used to control <a href="/wiki/Oomycetes" class="mw-redirect" title="Oomycetes">oomycetes</a>, which are not <a href="/wiki/Taxonomy" title="Taxonomy">taxonomically</a>/genetically fungi, although sharing similar methods of infecting plants. Fungicides can either be contact, translaminar or systemic. Contact fungicides are not taken up into the plant tissue and protect only the plant where the spray is deposited. Translaminar fungicides redistribute the fungicide from the upper, sprayed leaf surface to the lower, unsprayed surface. Systemic fungicides are taken up and redistributed through the xylem vessels. Few fungicides move to all parts of a plant. Some are locally systemic, and some move upward.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Similar_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Similar-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg/120px-Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg.png" decoding="async" width="120" height="81" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg/250px-Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="389" data-file-height="261"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Captan" title="Captan">Captan</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Phthalimide" title="Phthalimide">phthalimide</a>, is a major commercial fungicide.</figcaption></figure></div><p></p></div><div name="Rice Based Production System" term="Rice Based Production System" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=Rice%20Based%20Production%20System" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Rice Based Production System<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=Rice%20Based%20Production%20System">Rice Based Production System</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="genes" term="genes" wikidataID="Q7187" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: genes<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes">Genes</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a>, the word <b>gene</b> has two meanings. The Mendelian gene is a basic unit of <a href="/wiki/Heredity" title="Heredity">heredity</a>. The molecular gene is a sequence of <a href="/wiki/Nucleotide" title="Nucleotide">nucleotides</a> in <a href="/wiki/DNA" title="DNA">DNA</a> that is transcribed to produce <a href="/wiki/RNA" title="RNA">RNA</a>. There are two types of molecular genes: protein-coding genes and non-coding genes.<sup id="cite_ref-mendgene2_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mendgene2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-MedlinePlus_2020_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MedlinePlus_2020-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> During <a href="/wiki/Gene_expression" title="Gene expression">gene expression</a> (the synthesis of <a href="/wiki/Gene_product" title="Gene product">RNA or protein</a> from a gene), DNA is first <a href="/wiki/Transcription_(biology)" title="Transcription (biology)">copied into RNA</a>. RNA can be <a href="/wiki/Non-coding_RNA" title="Non-coding RNA">directly functional</a> or be the intermediate <a href="/wiki/Protein_biosynthesis" title="Protein biosynthesis">template</a> for the synthesis of a protein.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Gregor_Mendel_-_American_Breeders_Magazine,_1910.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Photograph of Gregor Mendel" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Gregor_Mendel_-_American_Breeders_Magazine%2C_1910.jpg/250px-Gregor_Mendel_-_American_Breeders_Magazine%2C_1910.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="256" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Gregor_Mendel_-_American_Breeders_Magazine%2C_1910.jpg/330px-Gregor_Mendel_-_American_Breeders_Magazine%2C_1910.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Gregor_Mendel_-_American_Breeders_Magazine%2C_1910.jpg/500px-Gregor_Mendel_-_American_Breeders_Magazine%2C_1910.jpg 2x" data-file-width="780" data-file-height="1000"></a><figcaption>Gregor Mendel</figcaption></figure>

'tie'">t</span><span title="/o&#650;/: 'o' in 'code'">o&#650;</span></span>/</a></span></span>; <i><b>Solanum lycopersicum</b></i>) is a plant whose fruit is an edible <a href="/wiki/Berry_(botany)" title="Berry (botany)">berry</a> that is eaten as a vegetable. The tomato is a member of the <a href="/wiki/Nightshade_family" class="mw-redirect" title="Nightshade family">nightshade family</a> that includes <a href="/wiki/Tobacco" title="Tobacco">tobacco</a>, <a href="/wiki/Potato" title="Potato">potato</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Chili_pepper" title="Chili pepper">chili peppers</a>. It originated from western <a href="/wiki/South_America" title="South America">South America</a>, and may have been domesticated there, in <a href="/wiki/Mexico" title="Mexico">Mexico</a>, or in <a href="/wiki/Central_America" title="Central America">Central America</a>. The Spanish introduced tomatoes to <a href="/wiki/Eurasia" title="Eurasia">Eurasia</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Columbian_exchange" title="Columbian exchange">Columbian exchange</a> in the 16th century.

The modern-day rise in global temperatures is <a href="/wiki/Scientific_consensus_on_climate_change" title="Scientific consensus on climate change">driven by human activities</a>, especially <a href="/wiki/Fossil_fuel" title="Fossil fuel">fossil fuel</a> (<a href="/wiki/Coal" title="Coal">coal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Petroleum" title="Petroleum">oil</a> and <a href="/wiki/Natural_gas" title="Natural gas">natural gas</a>) burning since the <a href="/wiki/Industrial_Revolution" title="Industrial Revolution">Industrial Revolution</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Lynas_2021_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Lynas_2021-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Fossil fuel use, <a href="/wiki/Deforestation_and_climate_change" title="Deforestation and climate change">deforestation</a>, and some <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions_from_agriculture" title="Greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture">agricultural</a> and industrial practices release <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_gas" title="Greenhouse gas">greenhouse gases</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Our_World_in_Data-2020_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Our_World_in_Data-2020-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> These gases <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_effect" title="Greenhouse effect">absorb some of the heat</a> that the Earth <a href="/wiki/Thermal_radiation" title="Thermal radiation">radiates</a> after it warms from sunlight, warming the lower atmosphere. Earth's atmosphere now has <a href="/wiki/Carbon_dioxide_in_the_atmosphere_of_Earth" title="Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere of Earth">roughly 50% more carbon dioxide</a>, the main gas driving global warming, than it did at the end of the <a href="/wiki/Pre-industrial_society" title="Pre-industrial society">pre-industrial era</a>, reaching levels not seen for millions of years.<sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Common_Era_Temperature.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Common_Era_Temperature.svg/500px-Common_Era_Temperature.svg.png" decoding="async" width="340" height="255" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Common_Era_Temperature.svg/960px-Common_Era_Temperature.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="720"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Global_surface_temperature" title="Global surface temperature">Global surface temperature</a> reconstruction over the past 2000 years using proxy data from tree rings, corals, and ice cores in blue.<sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Directly observed data is in red.<sup id="cite_ref-nasa_temperatures_44-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nasa_temperatures-44"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>

Located in the western <a href="/wiki/Pacific_Ocean" title="Pacific Ocean">Pacific Ocean</a>, it consists of about <a href="/wiki/List_of_islands_of_the_Philippines" title="List of islands of the Philippines">7,641 islands</a>, with a total area of about 300,000 square kilometers, which are broadly categorized in <a href="/wiki/Island_groups_of_the_Philippines" title="Island groups of the Philippines">three main geographical divisions</a> from north to south: <a href="/wiki/Luzon" title="Luzon">Luzon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Visayas" title="Visayas">Visayas</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Mindanao" title="Mindanao">Mindanao</a>. With a population of over 112 million, it is the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population" title="List of countries and dependencies by population">fourteenth-most-populous country</a>.

Members of the genus grow as tall, <a href="/wiki/Wetland" title="Wetland">wetland</a> grasses, growing to 1&#8211;2 metres (3&#8211;7&#160;ft) tall; the genus includes both <a href="/wiki/Annual_plant" title="Annual plant">annual</a> and <a href="/wiki/Perennial_plant" class="mw-redirect" title="Perennial plant">perennial</a> species.<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Biochemistry" term="Biochemistry" wikidataID="Q7094" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Biochemistry<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry">Biochemistry</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Biochemistry</b>, or <b>biological chemistry</b> (distinct from <a href="/wiki/Chemical_biology" title="Chemical biology">chemical biology</a>), is the study of <a href="/wiki/Chemical_process" title="Chemical process">chemical processes</a> within and relating to living <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organisms</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  A sub-discipline of both <a href="/wiki/Chemistry" title="Chemistry">chemistry</a> and <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a>, biochemistry may be divided into three fields: <a href="/wiki/Structural_biology" title="Structural biology">structural biology</a>, <a href="/wiki/Enzymology" class="mw-redirect" title="Enzymology">enzymology</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Metabolism" title="Metabolism">metabolism</a>. Over the last decades of the 20th century, biochemistry has become successful at explaining living processes through these three disciplines.  Almost all <a href="/wiki/List_of_life_sciences" title="List of life sciences">areas of the life sciences</a> are being uncovered and developed through biochemical methodology and research.<sup id="cite_ref-Voet_2005_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Voet_2005-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  Biochemistry focuses on understanding the chemical basis that allows <a href="/wiki/Biomolecule" title="Biomolecule">biological molecules</a> to give rise to the processes that occur within living <a href="/wiki/Cell_(biology)" title="Cell (biology)">cells</a> and between cells,<sup id="cite_ref-Karp2009_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Karp2009-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> in turn relating greatly to the understanding of <a href="/wiki/Tissue_(biology)" title="Tissue (biology)">tissues</a> and <a href="/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)" class="mw-redirect" title="Organ (anatomy)">organs</a> as well as organism structure and function.<sup id="cite_ref-MillerSpoolman2012_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MillerSpoolman2012-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Biochemistry is closely related to <a href="/wiki/Molecular_biology" title="Molecular biology">molecular biology</a>, the study of the <a href="/wiki/Molecule" title="Molecule">molecular</a> mechanisms of biological phenomena.<sup id="cite_ref-fn_1_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fn_1-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Gerty_Theresa_Radnitz_Cori_(1896-1957)_and_Carl_Ferdinand_Cori_-_restoration1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Gerty_Theresa_Radnitz_Cori_%281896-1957%29_and_Carl_Ferdinand_Cori_-_restoration1.jpg/250px-Gerty_Theresa_Radnitz_Cori_%281896-1957%29_and_Carl_Ferdinand_Cori_-_restoration1.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="234" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Gerty_Theresa_Radnitz_Cori_%281896-1957%29_and_Carl_Ferdinand_Cori_-_restoration1.jpg/330px-Gerty_Theresa_Radnitz_Cori_%281896-1957%29_and_Carl_Ferdinand_Cori_-_restoration1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Gerty_Theresa_Radnitz_Cori_%281896-1957%29_and_Carl_Ferdinand_Cori_-_restoration1.jpg/500px-Gerty_Theresa_Radnitz_Cori_%281896-1957%29_and_Carl_Ferdinand_Cori_-_restoration1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3098" data-file-height="3822"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Gerty_Cori" title="Gerty Cori">Gerty Cori</a> and <a href="/wiki/Carl_Cori" class="mw-redirect" title="Carl Cori">Carl Cori</a> jointly won the <a href="/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine" title="Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine">Nobel Prize</a> in 1947 for their discovery of the <a href="/wiki/Cori_cycle" title="Cori cycle">Cori cycle</a> at RPMI.</figcaption></figure>

</div><p></p></div><div name="maize" term="maize" wikidataID="Q11575" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: maize<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize">Maize</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Maize</b> (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="'m' in 'my'">m</span><span title="/e&#618;/: 'a' in 'face'">e&#618;</span><span title="'z' in 'zoom'">z</span></span>/</a></span></span>; <i><b>Zea mays</b></i>), also known as <b>corn</b> in <a href="/wiki/North_American_English" title="North American English">North American English</a>, is a tall stout <a href="/wiki/Poaceae" title="Poaceae">grass</a> that produces <a href="/wiki/Cereal_grain" class="mw-redirect" title="Cereal grain">cereal grain</a>. The leafy <a href="/wiki/Plant_stem" title="Plant stem">stalk</a> of the plant gives rise to male <a href="/wiki/Inflorescence" title="Inflorescence">inflorescences</a> or tassels which produce <a href="/wiki/Pollen" title="Pollen">pollen</a>, and female inflorescences called <a href="/wiki/Ear_(botany)" title="Ear (botany)">ears</a>. The ears yield grain, known as <a href="/wiki/Corn_kernels" class="mw-redirect" title="Corn kernels">kernels</a> or seeds. In modern commercial varieties, these are usually yellow or white; other varieties can be of many colors. Maize was domesticated by <a href="/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_Mexico" title="Indigenous peoples of Mexico">indigenous peoples in southern Mexico</a> about 9,000 years ago from wild <a href="/wiki/Teosinte" class="mw-redirect" title="Teosinte">teosinte</a>. Native Americans planted it alongside <a href="/wiki/Bean" title="Bean">beans</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cucurbita" title="Cucurbita">squashes</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Three_Sisters_(agriculture)" title="Three Sisters (agriculture)">Three Sisters</a> <a href="/wiki/Polyculture" title="Polyculture">polyculture</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Frameless"><a href="/wiki/File:Maize_plant_diagram,_large_labels.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Parts of a maize plant" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Maize_plant_diagram%2C_large_labels.svg/250px-Maize_plant_diagram%2C_large_labels.svg.png" decoding="async" width="200" height="404" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Maize_plant_diagram%2C_large_labels.svg/330px-Maize_plant_diagram%2C_large_labels.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Maize_plant_diagram%2C_large_labels.svg/500px-Maize_plant_diagram%2C_large_labels.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="394" data-file-height="795"></a><figcaption></figcaption></figure></div><p></p></div><div name="tropical tuber crops" term="tropical tuber crops" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=tropical%20tuber%20crops" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: tropical tuber crops<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=tropical%20tuber%20crops">tropical tuber crops</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Genetic improvement" term="Genetic improvement" wikidataID="Q137398938" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_improvement" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Genetic improvement<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_improvement">Genetic improvement</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Software" title="Software">computer software</a> development, <b>genetic improvement</b> is the use of <a href="/wiki/Mathematical_optimization" title="Mathematical optimization">optimisation</a> and <a href="/wiki/Machine_learning" title="Machine learning">machine learning</a> techniques, particularly <a href="/wiki/Search-based_software_engineering" title="Search-based software engineering">search-based software engineering</a> techniques such as <a href="/wiki/Genetic_programming" title="Genetic programming">genetic programming</a> to improve existing <a href="/wiki/Software" title="Software">software</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
The improved <a href="/wiki/Computer_program" title="Computer program">program</a> need not behave identically to the original. For example, <a href="/wiki/Automatic_bug_fixing" title="Automatic bug fixing">automatic bug fixing</a> improves <a href="/wiki/Executable_code" class="mw-redirect" title="Executable code">executable code</a> by reducing or eliminating <a href="/wiki/Software_bug" title="Software bug">buggy</a> behaviour.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
In other cases the improved software should behave identically to the old version but is better because,
for example:
it runs faster,<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
it uses less <a href="/wiki/Computer_memory" title="Computer memory">memory</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
it uses less <a href="/wiki/Electrical_energy" title="Electrical energy">energy</a><sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
or
it runs on a different type of computer.<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
GI differs from, for example, <a href="/wiki/Formal_methods" title="Formal methods">formal program translation</a>, in that it primarily verifies the behaviour of the new mutant version by running both the new and the old software on <a href="/wiki/Software_testing" title="Software testing">test inputs</a> and comparing their output and performance in order to see if the new software can still do what is wanted of the original program and is now better.
</p><p></p></div><div name="National Conference" term="National Conference" wikidataID="Q6971759" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Conference" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: National Conference<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Conference">National Conference</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>National Conference</b> may refer to:

When it is fresh, the fruit has a light green smooth skin and white flesh.

</div><p></p></div><div name="insecticides" term="insecticides" wikidataID="Q181322" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insecticides" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: insecticides<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insecticides">Insecticides</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Insecticides</b> are <a href="/wiki/Pesticide" title="Pesticide">pesticides</a> used to kill <a href="/wiki/Insect" title="Insect">insects</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> They include ovicides and <a href="/wiki/Larvicides" class="mw-redirect" title="Larvicides">larvicides</a> used against insect <a href="/wiki/Egg_(biology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Egg (biology)">eggs</a> and <a href="/wiki/Larva" title="Larva">larvae</a>, respectively. The major use of insecticides is in <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a>, but they are also used in home and garden settings, industrial buildings, for <a href="/wiki/Vector_control" title="Vector control">vector control</a>, and control of insect <a href="/wiki/Parasitism" title="Parasitism">parasites</a> of animals and humans.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:FLIT_Spray_Can_1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/FLIT_Spray_Can_1.jpg/250px-FLIT_Spray_Can_1.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="200" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/FLIT_Spray_Can_1.jpg/500px-FLIT_Spray_Can_1.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2938" data-file-height="2350"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/FLIT" class="mw-redirect" title="FLIT">FLIT</a> manual spray pump from 1928</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="elephant foot yam" term="elephant foot yam" wikidataID="Q151527" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elephant_foot_yam" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: elephant foot yam<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elephant_foot_yam">Elephant foot yam</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><i><b>Amorphophallus paeoniifolius</b></i>, the <b>elephant foot yam</b><sup id="cite_ref-GRIN_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GRIN-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> or <b>whitespot giant arum</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a tropical plant native to <a href="/wiki/Island_Southeast_Asia" class="mw-redirect" title="Island Southeast Asia">Island Southeast Asia</a>. It is cultivated for its edible tubers in Southeast Asia, South Asia, Madagascar, New Guinea, and the Pacific islands. Because of its production potential and popularity as a vegetable in various cuisines, it can be raised as a <a href="/wiki/Cash_crop" title="Cash crop">cash crop</a>.

the ability by which a <a href="/wiki/Plant" title="Plant">plant</a> maintains its biomass production during <a href="/wiki/Arid" class="mw-redirect" title="Arid">arid</a> or <a href="/wiki/Drought" title="Drought">drought</a> conditions.<sup id="cite_ref-:7_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:1_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:0_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Some plants are naturally adapted to dry conditions<i>,</i> surviving with protection mechanisms such as <a href="/wiki/Desiccation_tolerance" title="Desiccation tolerance">desiccation tolerance</a>, <a href="/wiki/Detoxification" title="Detoxification">detoxification</a>, or repair of <a href="/wiki/Xylem" title="Xylem">xylem</a> embolism.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_3-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Other plants, specifically crops like <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">corn</a>, <a href="/wiki/Wheat" title="Wheat">wheat</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a>, have become increasingly tolerant to drought with new varieties created via <a href="/wiki/Genetic_engineering" title="Genetic engineering">genetic engineering</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> From an evolutionary perspective, the type of mycorrhizal associations formed in the roots of plants can determine how fast plants can adapt to drought.

A high level of <a href="/wiki/Morphology_(biology)" title="Morphology (biology)">morphological</a> diversity is found within the species with large variations in the size, shape, and structure of the plant. class="wpage_first_para"><b>Nutrient management</b> is the science and practice directed to link <a href="/wiki/Soil" title="Soil">soil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Crop" title="Crop">crop</a>, <a href="/wiki/Weather" title="Weather">weather</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Hydrologic" class="mw-redirect" title="Hydrologic">hydrologic</a> factors with cultural, <a href="/wiki/Irrigation" title="Irrigation">irrigation</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Soil_conservation" title="Soil conservation">soil</a> and <a href="/wiki/Water_conservation" title="Water conservation">water conservation</a> practices to achieve optimal nutrient use efficiency, <a href="/wiki/Crop_yield" title="Crop yield">crop yields</a>, crop quality, and <a href="/wiki/Economic_returns" class="mw-redirect" title="Economic returns">economic returns</a>, while reducing off-site transport of <a href="/wiki/Soil_nutrient" class="mw-redirect" title="Soil nutrient">nutrients</a> (<a href="/wiki/Fertilizer" title="Fertilizer">fertilizer</a>) that may <a href="/wiki/Environmental_impact_of_agriculture" title="Environmental impact of agriculture">impact the environment</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It involves matching a specific field soil, climate, and crop management conditions to rate, source, timing, and place (commonly known as the <b>4R nutrient stewardship</b>) of nutrient application.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Fertilizer_applied_to_corn_field.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Fertilizer_applied_to_corn_field.jpg/250px-Fertilizer_applied_to_corn_field.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="179" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Fertilizer_applied_to_corn_field.jpg/500px-Fertilizer_applied_to_corn_field.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2100" data-file-height="1500"></a><figcaption>Nitrogen <a href="/wiki/Fertilizer" title="Fertilizer">fertilizer</a> being applied to growing corn (<a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">maize</a>) in a <a href="/wiki/Contour_plowing" title="Contour plowing">contoured</a>, <a href="/wiki/No-till_farming" title="No-till farming">no-tilled</a> field in <a href="/wiki/Iowa" title="Iowa">Iowa</a>.</figcaption></figure>

title="Drought">drought</a> conditions.<sup id="cite_ref-:7_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:1_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:0_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Some plants are naturally adapted to dry conditions<i>,</i> surviving with protection mechanisms such as <a href="/wiki/Desiccation_tolerance" title="Desiccation tolerance">desiccation tolerance</a>, <a href="/wiki/Detoxification" title="Detoxification">detoxification</a>, or repair of <a href="/wiki/Xylem" title="Xylem">xylem</a> embolism.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_3-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Other plants, specifically crops like <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">corn</a>, <a href="/wiki/Wheat" title="Wheat">wheat</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a>, have become increasingly tolerant to drought with new varieties created via <a href="/wiki/Genetic_engineering" title="Genetic engineering">genetic engineering</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> From an evolutionary perspective, the type of mycorrhizal associations formed in the roots of plants can determine how fast plants can adapt to drought.

These prevention mechanisms include the conduction of regular reviews of biosafety in laboratory settings, as well as strict guidelines to follow. Biosafety is used to protect from harmful incidents. Many laboratories handling biohazards employ an ongoing risk management assessment and enforcement process for biosafety.  Failures to follow such protocols can lead to increased risk of exposure to biohazards or pathogens. <a href="/wiki/Human_error" title="Human error">Human error</a> and poor technique contribute to unnecessary exposure and compromise the best safeguards set into place for protection.
</p>

Like <a href="/wiki/Animal_fat" title="Animal fat">animal fats</a>, vegetable fats are <i>mixtures</i> of <a href="/wiki/Triglyceride" title="Triglyceride">triglycerides</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Ullmann_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ullmann-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Soybean_oil" title="Soybean oil">Soybean oil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rapeseed_oil" title="Rapeseed oil">canola oil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Grape_seed_oil" title="Grape seed oil">grapeseed oil</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Cocoa_butter" title="Cocoa butter">cocoa butter</a> are examples of seed oils, or fats from seeds. <a href="/wiki/Olive_oil" title="Olive oil">Olive oil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Palm_oil" title="Palm oil">palm oil</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Rice_bran_oil" title="Rice bran oil">rice bran oil</a> are examples of fats from other parts of plants. In common usage, vegetable <i>oil</i> may refer exclusively to vegetable fats which are liquid at room temperature.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Vegetable oils are usually edible and are <a href="/wiki/Generally_recognized_as_safe" title="Generally recognized as safe">generally recognized as safe</a> (GRAS) by the <a href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</a> <a href="/wiki/Food_and_Drug_Administration" title="Food and Drug Administration">Food and Drug Administration</a> (FDA).<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

This original meaning is still commonly used, and is applied to plants collectively to refer to all edible plant matter, including <a href="/wiki/Edible_flower" title="Edible flower">flowers</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fruit" title="Fruit">fruits</a>, <a href="/wiki/Edible_plant_stem" title="Edible plant stem">stems</a>, <a href="/wiki/Leaf_vegetable" title="Leaf vegetable">leaves</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_root_vegetables" class="mw-redirect" title="List of root vegetables">roots</a>, and <a href="/wiki/List_of_edible_seeds" title="List of edible seeds">seeds</a>. An alternative definition is applied somewhat arbitrarily, often by <a href="/wiki/Culinary" class="mw-redirect" title="Culinary">culinary</a> and cultural tradition; it may include savoury fruits such as <a href="/wiki/Tomato" title="Tomato">tomatoes</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cucurbita" title="Cucurbita">squash</a>, <a href="/wiki/Flower" title="Flower">flowers</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Broccoli" title="Broccoli">broccoli</a>, and seeds such as <a href="/wiki/Pulse_(legume)" class="mw-redirect" title="Pulse (legume)">pulses</a>, but exclude foods derived from some plants that are fruits, flowers, <a href="/wiki/Nut_(fruit)" title="Nut (fruit)">nuts</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Cereal" title="Cereal">cereal</a> grains.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Marketvegetables.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Marketvegetables.jpg/250px-Marketvegetables.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="375" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Marketvegetables.jpg/500px-Marketvegetables.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="2400"></a><figcaption>Vegetables separated with baskets in a <a href="/wiki/Market_(place)" class="mw-redirect" title="Market (place)">market</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Philippines" title="Philippines">Philippines</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Chinese potato" term="Chinese potato" wikidataID="Q2716687" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_potato" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Chinese potato<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_potato">Chinese potato</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><i><b>Coleus rotundifolius</b></i>, <a href="/wiki/Synonym_(taxonomy)" title="Synonym (taxonomy)">synonyms</a> <i><b>Plectranthus rotundifolius</b></i> and <i><b>Solenostemon rotundifolius</b></i>,<sup id="cite_ref-PatoMwanGovaSmit19_1-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-PatoMwanGovaSmit19-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> commonly known as <b>native potato</b> or <b>country potato</b> in Africa and called <b>Chinese potato</b> in <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>, is a <a href="/wiki/Perennial" title="Perennial">perennial</a> <a href="/wiki/Herbaceous_plant" title="Herbaceous plant">herbaceous plant</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Lamiaceae" title="Lamiaceae">mint family (Lamiaceae)</a> native to tropical Africa. It is cultivated for its edible <a href="/wiki/Tubers" class="mw-redirect" title="Tubers">tubers</a> primarily in <a href="/wiki/West_Africa" title="West Africa">West Africa</a>, as well as more recently in parts of <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a>, especially India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, and Indonesia.<sup id="cite_ref-NRC_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NRC-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Koorka_0124.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Koorka_0124.jpg/250px-Koorka_0124.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="333" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Koorka_0124.jpg/500px-Koorka_0124.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1536" data-file-height="2048"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="sponge gourd" term="sponge gourd" wikidataID="Q2308434" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge_gourd" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: sponge gourd<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge_gourd">Sponge gourd</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><i><b>Luffa aegyptiaca</b></i>, the <b>sponge gourd</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <b>Egyptian cucumber</b> or <b>Vietnamese luffa</b>,  is an <a href="/wiki/Annual_plant" title="Annual plant">annual</a> species of <a href="/wiki/Vine" title="Vine">vine</a> cultivated for its fruit, native to <a href="/wiki/South_Asia" title="South Asia">South</a> and <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Asia" title="Southeast Asia">Southeast Asia</a>.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Luffa_aegyptiaca_Blanco2.334-cropped.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Luffa_aegyptiaca_Blanco2.334-cropped.jpg/250px-Luffa_aegyptiaca_Blanco2.334-cropped.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="364" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Luffa_aegyptiaca_Blanco2.334-cropped.jpg/500px-Luffa_aegyptiaca_Blanco2.334-cropped.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1160" data-file-height="1690"></a><figcaption>Leaves, flower and fruit of a luffa</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="IC" term="IC" wikidataID="Q223987" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IC" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: IC<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IC">IC</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>IC</b>, <b>Ic</b>, <b>ic</b>, or <b>i.c.</b> may stand for:
</p>
<p></p></div><div name="Colletotrichum" term="Colletotrichum" wikidataID="Q10457032" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colletotrichum" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Colletotrichum<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colletotrichum">Colletotrichum</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><i><b>Colletotrichum</b></i> (sexual stage: <i><b>Glomerella</b></i>) is a <a href="/wiki/Genus" title="Genus">genus</a> of <a href="/wiki/Fungus" title="Fungus">fungi</a> that are symbionts to plants as <a href="/wiki/Endophyte" title="Endophyte">endophytes</a> (living within the plant) or <a href="/wiki/Phytopathogen" class="mw-redirect" title="Phytopathogen">phytopathogens</a>. Many of the species in this genus are <a href="/wiki/Plant_pathogen" class="mw-redirect" title="Plant pathogen">plant pathogens</a>, but some species may have a <a href="/wiki/Mutualism_(biology)" title="Mutualism (biology)">mutualistic</a> relationship with <a href="/wiki/Host_(biology)" title="Host (biology)">hosts</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Colletotrichum_lindemuthianum.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Colletotrichum_lindemuthianum.jpg/250px-Colletotrichum_lindemuthianum.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="230" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Colletotrichum_lindemuthianum.jpg/500px-Colletotrichum_lindemuthianum.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="767" data-file-height="706"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="IARI" term="IARI" wikidataID="Q3521333" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IARI" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: IARI<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IARI">IARI</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>Indian Agricultural Research Institute</b> (<b>IARI</b>), commonly known as the <b>Pusa Institute</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-abt_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-abt-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is India's national institute for agricultural research, education and <a href="/wiki/Agricultural_extension" title="Agricultural extension">extension</a>. The name Pusa Institute is derived from the fact that the institute was originally located in <a href="/wiki/Samastipur#Pusa" title="Samastipur">Pusa</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bihar" title="Bihar">Bihar</a> as the <b>Imperial Institute of Agricultural Research</b> in 1911. It was then renamed as the <b>Imperial Agricultural Research Institute</b> in 1919 and following a major earthquake in Pusa in 1934, it was relocated to <a href="/wiki/Delhi" title="Delhi">Delhi</a> in 1936. The current institute in Delhi is financed and administered by the <a href="/wiki/Indian_Council_of_Agricultural_Research" title="Indian Council of Agricultural Research"> Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)</a>. The IARI was responsible for the research leading to the "<a href="/wiki/Green_Revolution_in_India" title="Green Revolution in India">Green Revolution in India</a>" of the 1970s.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/IARI" class="mw-redirect" title="IARI">IARI</a> ranked First among Agriculture and Allied Universities in the National Institutional Ranking Framework <a href="/wiki/NIRF" class="mw-redirect" title="NIRF">NIRF</a> (India Rankings 2024).<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:IARILogo.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/IARILogo.jpg/250px-IARILogo.jpg" decoding="async" width="140" height="158" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/IARILogo.jpg/330px-IARILogo.jpg 2x" data-file-width="470" data-file-height="531"></a><figcaption>Logo of the Imperial Agricultural Research Institute</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Crop Production" term="Crop Production" wikidataID="Q11451" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crop_production" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Crop Production<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crop_production">Crop production</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Agriculture</b> is the practice of cultivating the soil, planting, raising, and harvesting both food and non-food crops, as well as <a href="/wiki/Livestock" title="Livestock">livestock</a> production. Broader definitions also include <a href="/wiki/Forestry" title="Forestry">forestry</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aquaculture" title="Aquaculture">aquaculture</a>. Agriculture was a key factor in the rise of <a href="/wiki/Sedentism" title="Sedentism">sedentary</a> human <a href="/wiki/Civilization" title="Civilization">civilization</a>, whereby farming of <a href="/wiki/Domestication" title="Domestication">domesticated</a> plants and animals created food <a href="/wiki/Economic_surplus" title="Economic surplus">surpluses</a> that enabled people to live in the cities. While humans started gathering grains at least 105,000 years ago, nascent farmers only began planting them around 11,500 years ago. Sheep, goats, pigs, and cattle were domesticated around 10,000 years ago. Plants were independently cultivated in at least 11 regions of the world. In the 20th century, <a href="/wiki/Industrial_agriculture" title="Industrial agriculture">industrial agriculture</a> based on large-scale <a href="/wiki/Monoculture" title="Monoculture">monocultures</a> came to dominate agricultural output.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:PivotWithDrops.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PivotWithDrops.JPG/250px-PivotWithDrops.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="179" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PivotWithDrops.JPG/500px-PivotWithDrops.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="2100" data-file-height="1500"></a><figcaption>Modern agriculture: a <a href="/wiki/Center_pivot_irrigation" class="mw-redirect" title="Center pivot irrigation">center pivot irrigation</a> system on a field</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Plant Breeding" term="Plant Breeding" wikidataID="Q788558" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_Breeding" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Plant Breeding<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_Breeding">Plant Breeding</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b><a href="/wiki/Plant" title="Plant">Plant</a> breeding</b> is the science of changing the traits of <a href="/wiki/Plants" class="mw-redirect" title="Plants">plants</a> in order to produce desired characteristics.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is used to improve the quality of plant products for use by humans and animals.<sup id="cite_ref-Hartung-2014_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hartung-2014-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The goals of plant breeding are to produce crop varieties that boast unique and superior traits for a variety of applications. The most frequently addressed agricultural traits are those related to biotic and abiotic stress tolerance, grain or biomass yield, end-use quality characteristics such as taste or the concentrations of specific biological molecules (proteins, sugars, lipids, vitamins, fibers) and ease of processing (harvesting, milling, baking, malting, blending, etc.).<sup id="cite_ref-Willy-2010_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Willy-2010-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Wheat_selection_k10183-1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/29/Wheat_selection_k10183-1.jpg" decoding="async" width="252" height="189" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="252" data-file-height="189"></a><figcaption>The Yecoro <a href="/wiki/Wheat" title="Wheat">wheat</a> (right) <a href="/wiki/Cultivar" title="Cultivar">cultivar</a> is sensitive to salinity, plants resulting from a hybrid cross with cultivar W4910 (left) show greater tolerance to high salinity</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="sunflower" term="sunflower" wikidataID="Q171497" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: sunflower<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower">Sunflower</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>common sunflower</b> (<i><b>Helianthus annuus</b></i>) is a species of large <a href="/wiki/Annual_plant" title="Annual plant">annual</a> <a href="/wiki/Forb" title="Forb">forb</a> of the daisy family <a href="/wiki/Asteraceae" title="Asteraceae">Asteraceae</a>. The common sunflower is harvested for its <a href="/wiki/Sunflower_seed" title="Sunflower seed">edible oily seeds</a>, which are often eaten as a <a href="/wiki/Snack_food" class="mw-redirect" title="Snack food">snack food</a>. They are also used in the production of cooking oil, as food for livestock, as <a href="/wiki/Bird_food" title="Bird food">bird food</a>, and as plantings in domestic gardens for aesthetics. Wild plants are known for their multiple flower heads, whereas the domestic sunflower often possesses a single large flower head atop an unbranched stem.
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Sunflower_sky_backdrop.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Sunflower_sky_backdrop.jpg/250px-Sunflower_sky_backdrop.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="277" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Sunflower_sky_backdrop.jpg/500px-Sunflower_sky_backdrop.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1404" data-file-height="1555"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="Biosecurity" term="Biosecurity" wikidataID="Q803874" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biosecurity" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Biosecurity<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biosecurity">Biosecurity</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Biosecurity</b> refers to measures aimed at preventing the introduction or spread of harmful <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organisms</a> (e.g. <a href="/wiki/Virus" title="Virus">viruses</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bacteria" title="Bacteria">bacteria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Plant" title="Plant">plants</a>, <a href="/wiki/Animal" title="Animal">animals</a> etc.) intentionally or unintentionally outside their native range or within new environments. In <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a>, these measures are aimed at protecting <a href="/wiki/Food_crop" class="mw-redirect" title="Food crop">food crops</a> and <a href="/wiki/Livestock" title="Livestock">livestock</a> from <a href="/wiki/Pest_(organism)" title="Pest (organism)">pests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Invasive_species" title="Invasive species">invasive species</a>, and other organisms not conducive to the welfare of the <a href="/wiki/Human_population" class="mw-redirect" title="Human population">human population</a>. The term includes <a href="/wiki/Biological_pest_control" title="Biological pest control">biological threats</a> to people, including those from <a href="/wiki/Pandemic" title="Pandemic">pandemic</a> diseases and <a href="/wiki/Bioterrorism" title="Bioterrorism">bioterrorism</a>. The definition has sometimes been broadened to embrace other concepts, and it is used for different purposes in different contexts.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Influenza_virus_research.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Influenza_virus_research.jpg/250px-Influenza_virus_research.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="354" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Influenza_virus_research.jpg/500px-Influenza_virus_research.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1966" data-file-height="2786"></a><figcaption>A <a href="/wiki/Microbiologist" title="Microbiologist">microbiologist</a> working on the reconstructed virus of the 1918 <a href="/wiki/Spanish_flu" title="Spanish flu">Spanish Flu</a>, using a <a href="/wiki/Fume_hood" title="Fume hood">fume hood</a> for <a href="/wiki/Biocontainment" title="Biocontainment">biocontainment</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Seed treatment" term="Seed treatment" wikidataID="Q252666" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed_treatment" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Seed treatment<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed_treatment">Seed treatment</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A seed treatment is a treatment of the <a href="/wiki/Seed" title="Seed">seed</a> with either chemical agents or biological or by physical methods, usually done to provide protection to the seed and improve the establishment of healthy crops. Although the term seed treatment is used often and indeed typically to mean seed coating, there are other methods of seed treatment.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> 
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Beize_zea_mays.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Corn kernels treated with taint, a fungicide. Sifering agents are provided with a dye for identification, since tainted goods are excluded from feeding." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Beize_zea_mays.JPG/250px-Beize_zea_mays.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Beize_zea_mays.JPG/500px-Beize_zea_mays.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="1200" data-file-height="800"></a><figcaption> Corn kernels treated with a fungicide. A dye is added to the coating, since seeds coated with chemicals cannot be used for food.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="vermicompost" term="vermicompost" wikidataID="Q900747" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermicompost" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: vermicompost<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermicompost">Vermicompost</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Vermicompost</b> (<b>vermi-compost</b>) is the product of the decomposition process using various species of <a href="/wiki/Worm" title="Worm">worms</a>, usually <a href="/wiki/Eisenia_foetida" class="mw-redirect" title="Eisenia foetida">red wigglers</a>, <a href="/wiki/Enchytraeus_buchholzi" title="Enchytraeus buchholzi">white worms</a>, and other <a href="/wiki/Earthworm" title="Earthworm">earthworms</a>, to create a mixture of decomposing vegetable or <a href="/wiki/Food_waste" class="mw-redirect" title="Food waste">food waste</a>, bedding materials, and vermicast. This process is called <b>vermicomposting</b>, with the rearing of worms for this purpose is called <b>vermiculture</b>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Lombri-compostage.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Lombri-compostage.JPG/330px-Lombri-compostage.JPG" decoding="async" width="300" height="209" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Lombri-compostage.JPG/500px-Lombri-compostage.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Lombri-compostage.JPG/960px-Lombri-compostage.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2657" data-file-height="1849"></a><figcaption>Vermicomposting uses worms to decompose waste and make nutrient-rich "worm manure".</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Andhra Pradesh" term="Andhra Pradesh" wikidataID="Q1159" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Andhra Pradesh<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh">Andhra Pradesh</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Andhra Pradesh</b><sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India" title="States and union territories of India">state</a> on the <a href="/wiki/East_Coast_of_India" class="mw-redirect" title="East Coast of India">east coast</a> of southern <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>. It is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_area" title="List of states and union territories of India by area">seventh-largest state</a> and the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_population" title="List of states and union territories of India by population">tenth-most populous</a> in the country. <a href="/wiki/Telugu_language" title="Telugu language">Telugu</a>, one of the <a href="/wiki/Classical_languages_of_India" title="Classical languages of India">classical languages of India</a>, is the most widely spoken language in the state, as well as its official language. <a href="/wiki/Amaravati" title="Amaravati">Amaravati</a> is the state capital, while the largest city is <a href="/wiki/Visakhapatnam" title="Visakhapatnam">Visakhapatnam</a>. <a href="/wiki/Amaravati" title="Amaravati">Amaravati</a> is a greenfield capital city developed near Vijayawada. Geographically  both Amaravati and Vijayawada can be seen as Twin cities. Andhra Pradesh shares borders with <a href="/wiki/Odisha" title="Odisha">Odisha</a> to the northeast, <a href="/wiki/Chhattisgarh" title="Chhattisgarh">Chhattisgarh</a> to the north, <a href="/wiki/Karnataka" title="Karnataka">Karnataka</a> to the west, <a href="/wiki/Tamil_Nadu" title="Tamil Nadu">Tamil Nadu</a> to the south, <a href="/wiki/Telangana" title="Telangana">Telangana</a> to northwest and the <a href="/wiki/Bay_of_Bengal" title="Bay of Bengal">Bay of Bengal</a> to the east. It has the <a href="/wiki/Coastline_of_Andhra_Pradesh" title="Coastline of Andhra Pradesh">longest coastline</a> in India (aerial distance between extreme ends) at about 1,000 kilometres (620&#160;mi).
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg" class="mw-file-description" title="Location of Andhra Pradesh in India"><img alt="The map of India showing Andhra Pradesh" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg/330px-India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="350" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg/500px-India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg/960px-India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1486" data-file-height="1734"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="red rot" term="red rot" wikidataID="Q7305380" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_rot" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: red rot<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_rot">Red rot</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Red rot</b> is a degradation process found in vegetable-tanned <a href="/wiki/Leather" title="Leather">leather</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

Diagnosis is used in a lot of different <a href="/wiki/Academic_discipline" title="Academic discipline">disciplines</a>, with variations in the use of <a href="/wiki/Logic" title="Logic">logic</a>, <a href="/wiki/Analytics" title="Analytics">analytics</a>, and experience, to determine "<a href="/wiki/Causality" title="Causality">cause and effect</a>". In <a href="/wiki/Systems_engineering" title="Systems engineering">systems engineering</a> and <a href="/wiki/Computer_science" title="Computer science">computer science</a>, it is typically used to determine the causes of symptoms, mitigations, and solutions.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
