</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Lite-Trac_Crop_Sprayer.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Lite-Trac_Crop_Sprayer.jpg/250px-Lite-Trac_Crop_Sprayer.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Lite-Trac_Crop_Sprayer.jpg/500px-Lite-Trac_Crop_Sprayer.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="900" data-file-height="675"></a><figcaption>A self-propelled crop sprayer spraying pesticide on a field</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="sugar mills" term="sugar mills" wikidataID="Q1820305" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_mills" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: sugar mills<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_mills">Sugar mills</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>sugar cane mill</b> is a factory that processes <a href="/wiki/Sugar_cane" class="mw-redirect" title="Sugar cane">sugar cane</a> to produce <a href="/wiki/Raw_sugar" class="mw-redirect" title="Raw sugar">raw sugar</a><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEAMSCL2023_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAMSCL2023-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> or plantation white sugar.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESteindl2005_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESteindl2005-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Some sugar mills are situated next to a back-end refinery, that turns raw sugar into (refined) <a href="/wiki/White_sugar" class="mw-redirect" title="White sugar">white sugar</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESMRI2023_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESMRI2023-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Inkerman_mill.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Inkerman_mill.jpg/330px-Inkerman_mill.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="180" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Inkerman_mill.jpg/500px-Inkerman_mill.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Inkerman_mill.jpg/960px-Inkerman_mill.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1000" data-file-height="600"></a><figcaption>Inkerman sugar mill in Australia</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="rice production" term="rice production" wikidataID="Q5090" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_production" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: rice production<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_production">Rice production</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Rice</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Cereal_grain" class="mw-redirect" title="Cereal grain">cereal grain</a> and in its <a href="/wiki/Domestication" title="Domestication">domesticated</a> form is the <a href="/wiki/Staple_food" title="Staple food">staple food</a> of over half of the <a href="/wiki/World%27s_population" class="mw-redirect" title="World's population">world's population</a>, particularly in <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Africa" title="Africa">Africa</a>. Rice is the seed of the grass species <i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_sativa" title="Oryza sativa">Oryza sativa</a></i> (Asian rice)&#8212;or, much less commonly, <i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_glaberrima" title="Oryza glaberrima">Oryza glaberrima</a></i> (African rice). Asian rice was domesticated in <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a> some 13,500 to 8,200 years ago; African rice was domesticated in Africa about 3,000 years ago. Rice has become commonplace in many cultures worldwide; in 2023, 800 million tons were produced, placing it third after <a href="/wiki/Sugarcane" title="Sugarcane">sugarcane</a> and <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">maize</a>. Only some 8% of rice is traded internationally. China, India, and Indonesia are the largest consumers of rice. A substantial amount of the rice produced in developing nations is lost after harvest through factors such as poor transport and storage. Rice yields can be reduced by pests including <a href="/wiki/Insect" title="Insect">insects</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rodent" title="Rodent">rodents</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Bird" title="Bird">birds</a>, as well as by <a href="/wiki/Weed" title="Weed">weeds</a>, and by <a href="/wiki/List_of_rice_diseases" title="List of rice diseases">diseases</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Rice_blast" class="mw-redirect" title="Rice blast">rice blast</a>. Traditional <a href="/wiki/Rice_polyculture" title="Rice polyculture">rice polycultures</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Rice-duck_farming" title="Rice-duck farming">rice-duck farming</a>, and modern <a href="/wiki/Integrated_pest_management" title="Integrated pest management">integrated pest management</a> seek to control damage from pests in a <a href="/wiki/Sustainable_agriculture" title="Sustainable agriculture">sustainable</a> way.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg/500px-20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg" decoding="async" width="340" height="191" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg/960px-20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="720"></a><figcaption>Rice plant (<i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_sativa" title="Oryza sativa">Oryza sativa</a></i>) with branched <a href="/wiki/Panicle" title="Panicle">panicles</a> containing many grains on each stem</figcaption></figure>

href="/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India" title="States and union territories of India">state</a> in <a href="/wiki/North_India" title="North India">northern India</a>. With over 241&#160;million inhabitants, it is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_population" title="List of states and union territories of India by population">most populated state</a> not just in India but <a href="/wiki/List_of_first-level_administrative_divisions_by_population" title="List of first-level administrative divisions by population">worldwide</a> &#8211; if it were a country, it would be the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population" title="List of countries and dependencies by population">sixth-largest</a> in the world<sup id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> &#8211; and accounting for 17% of the population of India and around 3% of the total world population. The state is bordered by <a href="/wiki/Rajasthan" title="Rajasthan">Rajasthan</a> to the west, <a href="/wiki/Haryana" title="Haryana">Haryana</a>, <a href="/wiki/Himachal_Pradesh" title="Himachal Pradesh">Himachal Pradesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Delhi" title="Delhi">Delhi</a> to the northwest, <a href="/wiki/Uttarakhand" title="Uttarakhand">Uttarakhand</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nepal" title="Nepal">Nepal</a> to the north, <a href="/wiki/Bihar" title="Bihar">Bihar</a> to the east, <a href="/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh" title="Madhya Pradesh">Madhya Pradesh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chhattisgarh" title="Chhattisgarh">Chhattisgarh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jharkhand" title="Jharkhand">Jharkhand</a> to the south. It is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_of_India_by_area" class="mw-redirect" title="List of states of India by area">fourth-largest Indian state by area</a> covering 243,286&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (93,933&#160;sq&#160;mi), accounting for 7.3 per cent of the total area of India. <a href="/wiki/Lucknow" title="Lucknow">Lucknow</a> serves as the <a href="/wiki/State_capital" class="mw-redirect" title="State capital">state capital</a>, with <a href="/wiki/Prayagraj" title="Prayagraj">Prayagraj</a> being the <a href="/wiki/Allahabad_High_Court" title="Allahabad High Court">judicial capital</a>. It is divided into 18 <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Uttar_Pradesh" title="Administrative divisions of Uttar Pradesh">divisions</a> and 75 <a href="/wiki/List_of_districts_of_Uttar_Pradesh" title="List of districts of Uttar Pradesh">districts</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Indo-Gangetic_Plain.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="The Indo-Gangetic Plain, also known as the Northern Plain or North Indian River Plain" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Indo-Gangetic_Plain.jpg/250px-Indo-Gangetic_Plain.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Indo-Gangetic_Plain.jpg/500px-Indo-Gangetic_Plain.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1200"></a><figcaption>A part of the Gangetic Plain</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="inoculation" term="inoculation" wikidataID="Q1664296" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inoculation" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: inoculation<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inoculation">Inoculation</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Inoculation</b> is the act of implanting a pathogen or other <a href="/wiki/Microbe" class="mw-redirect" title="Microbe">microbe</a> or <a href="/wiki/Virus" title="Virus">virus</a> into a person or other organism. It is a method of <a href="/wiki/Artificial_induction_of_immunity" title="Artificial induction of immunity">artificially inducing immunity</a> against various <a href="/wiki/Infectious_disease" class="mw-redirect" title="Infectious disease">infectious diseases</a>. The term "inoculation" is also used more generally to refer to intentionally depositing microbes into any <a href="/wiki/Growth_medium" title="Growth medium">growth medium</a>, as into a <a href="/wiki/Petri_dish" title="Petri dish">Petri dish</a> used to <a href="/wiki/Microbiological_culture" title="Microbiological culture">culture</a> the microbe, or into food ingredients for making cultured foods such as <a href="/wiki/Yoghurt" class="mw-redirect" title="Yoghurt">yoghurt</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fermentation" title="Fermentation">fermented</a> beverages such as beer and wine. This article is primarily about the use of inoculation for producing <a href="/wiki/Immunization" title="Immunization">immunity</a> against <a href="/wiki/Infection" title="Infection">infection</a>. Inoculation has been used to <a href="/wiki/Eradication_of_infectious_diseases" title="Eradication of infectious diseases">eradicate</a> <a href="/wiki/Smallpox" title="Smallpox">smallpox</a> and to markedly reduce other infectious diseases such as <a href="/wiki/Polio" title="Polio">polio</a>. Although the terms "inoculation", "<a href="/wiki/Vaccination" title="Vaccination">vaccination</a>", and "immunization" are often used interchangeably, there are important differences. Inoculation is the act of implanting a pathogen or microbe into a person or other recipient; vaccination is the act of implanting or giving someone a <a href="/wiki/Vaccine" title="Vaccine">vaccine</a> specifically; and immunization is the development of disease resistance that results from the <a href="/wiki/Immune_system" title="Immune system">immune system</a>'s response to a vaccine or natural infection.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Mary_Wortley_Montagu_by_Charles_Jervas,_after_1716.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Mary_Wortley_Montagu_by_Charles_Jervas%2C_after_1716.jpg/250px-Mary_Wortley_Montagu_by_Charles_Jervas%2C_after_1716.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="342" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Mary_Wortley_Montagu_by_Charles_Jervas%2C_after_1716.jpg/330px-Mary_Wortley_Montagu_by_Charles_Jervas%2C_after_1716.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Mary_Wortley_Montagu_by_Charles_Jervas%2C_after_1716.jpg/500px-Mary_Wortley_Montagu_by_Charles_Jervas%2C_after_1716.jpg 2x" data-file-width="789" data-file-height="1422"></a><figcaption>Mary Wortley Montagu, by <a href="/wiki/Charles_Jervas" title="Charles Jervas">Charles Jervas</a>, after 1716</figcaption></figure>

These minute <a href="/wiki/Insect" title="Insect">insects</a>, colloquially known as <b>hoppers</b>, are plant feeders that suck <a href="/wiki/Plant_sap" class="mw-redirect" title="Plant sap">plant sap</a> from grass, shrubs, or trees. Their hind legs are modified for jumping, and are covered with hairs that facilitate the spreading of a secretion over their bodies that acts as a water repellent and carrier of <a href="/wiki/Pheromone" title="Pheromone">pheromones</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Stiller_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Stiller-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> They undergo a partial <a href="/wiki/Metamorphosis" title="Metamorphosis">metamorphosis</a>, and have various host associations, varying from very generalized to very specific. Some species have a cosmopolitan distribution, or occur throughout the temperate and tropical regions. Some are pests or <a href="/wiki/Vector_(epidemiology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Vector (epidemiology)">vectors</a> of <a href="/wiki/Plant_virus" title="Plant virus">plant viruses</a> and <a href="/wiki/Phytoplasma" title="Phytoplasma">phytoplasmas</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Stiller_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Stiller-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The family is distributed  all over the world, and constitutes the second-largest hemipteran family, with at least 20,000 described species.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Two-lined_gum_treehopper03.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Two-lined_gum_treehopper03.jpg/250px-Two-lined_gum_treehopper03.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Two-lined_gum_treehopper03.jpg/500px-Two-lined_gum_treehopper03.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1067"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="Das Lipi" term="Das Lipi" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=Das%20Lipi" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Das Lipi<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=Das%20Lipi">Das Lipi</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

In more colloquial terms, the health of soil arises from favorable interactions of all soil components (living and non-living) that belong together, as in <a href="/wiki/Microbiota" title="Microbiota">microbiota</a>, plants and animals. It is possible that a soil can be healthy in terms of <a href="/wiki/Ecosystem" title="Ecosystem">ecosystem</a> functioning but not necessarily serve <a href="/wiki/Crop_production" class="mw-redirect" title="Crop production">crop production</a> or human nutrition directly, hence the scientific debate on terms and measurements.

The Institute established in 1963<sup id="cite_ref-ctcritvm-institute_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ctcritvm-institute-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> with its headquarters at <a href="/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram" title="Thiruvananthapuram">Thiruvananthapuram</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kerala" title="Kerala">Kerala</a> has with an area of 48.19 <a href="/wiki/Hectare" title="Hectare">hectares</a>. The headquarters of ICAR - CTCRI is located at <a href="/wiki/Sreekaryam" title="Sreekaryam">Sreekaryam</a> at a distance 12&#160;km away from <a href="/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_International_Airport" title="Thiruvananthapuram International Airport">Thiruvananthapuram International Airport</a> and 10&#160;km from <a href="/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Central_railway_station" title="Thiruvananthapuram Central railway station">Thiruvananthapuram Central railway station</a> as well as <a href="/wiki/Central_Bus_Station_Thiruvananthapuram" class="mw-redirect" title="Central Bus Station Thiruvananthapuram">Central Bus Station Thiruvananthapuram</a>. The Institute has a regional centre at <a href="/wiki/Bhubaneswar" title="Bhubaneswar">Bhubaneswar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Orissa,_India" class="mw-redirect" title="Orissa, India">Orissa</a> established in 1976 <sup id="cite_ref-ctcribbs-institute_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ctcribbs-institute-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  with an area of 20 <a href="/wiki/Hectare" title="Hectare">hectares</a> located 8&#160;km from <a href="/wiki/Bhubaneswar_Airport" class="mw-redirect" title="Bhubaneswar Airport">Bhubaneswar Airport</a> and 7&#160;km from <a href="/wiki/Bhubaneswar_railway_station" title="Bhubaneswar railway station">Bhubaneswar railway station</a> to cater the needs of <a href="/wiki/East_India" title="East India">Eastern India</a>.
</p>

Fertilizers may be distinct from <a href="/wiki/Liming_(soil)" title="Liming (soil)">liming materials</a> or other non-nutrient <a href="/wiki/Soil_amendments" class="mw-redirect" title="Soil amendments">soil amendments</a>. Many sources of fertilizer exist, both natural and <a href="/wiki/Agrochemical" title="Agrochemical">industrially</a> produced.<sup id="cite_ref-Scherer2009_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Scherer2009-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> For most modern agricultural practices, fertilization focuses on three main macro nutrients: <a href="/wiki/Nitrogen" title="Nitrogen">nitrogen</a> (N), <a href="/wiki/Phosphorus" title="Phosphorus">phosphorus</a> (P), and <a href="/wiki/Potassium" title="Potassium">potassium</a> (K) with occasional addition of supplements like <a href="/wiki/Rock_flour" title="Rock flour">rock flour</a> for micronutrients. Farmers apply these fertilizers in a variety of ways: through dry or <a href="/wiki/Pelletized" class="mw-redirect" title="Pelletized">pelletized</a> or liquid application processes, using large <a href="/wiki/Agricultural_equipment" class="mw-redirect" title="Agricultural equipment">agricultural equipment</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Hand_tool" title="Hand tool">hand-tool</a> methods.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Manure_spreading_Hlokozi_2007_11_29.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Manure_spreading_Hlokozi_2007_11_29.jpg/500px-Manure_spreading_Hlokozi_2007_11_29.jpg" decoding="async" width="340" height="275" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Manure_spreading_Hlokozi_2007_11_29.jpg/960px-Manure_spreading_Hlokozi_2007_11_29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1476" data-file-height="1194"></a><figcaption>A <a href="/wiki/Farmer" title="Farmer">farmer</a> spreading <a href="/wiki/Manure" title="Manure">manure</a> to improve <a href="/wiki/Soil_fertility" title="Soil fertility">soil fertility</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="rice straw" term="rice straw" wikidataID="Q160066" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_straw" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: rice straw<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_straw">Rice straw</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Straw</b> is an agricultural <a href="/wiki/Byproduct" class="mw-redirect" title="Byproduct">byproduct</a> consisting of the dry <a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/stalk" class="extiw" title="wikt:stalk">stalks</a> of <a href="/wiki/Cereal" title="Cereal">cereal</a> plants after the <a href="/wiki/Grain" title="Grain">grain</a> and <a href="/wiki/Chaff" title="Chaff">chaff</a> have been removed. It makes up about half of the <a href="/wiki/Crop_yield" title="Crop yield">yield</a> by weight of cereal crops such as <a href="/wiki/Barley" title="Barley">barley</a>, <a href="/wiki/Oat" title="Oat">oats</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rye" title="Rye">rye</a> and <a href="/wiki/Wheat" title="Wheat">wheat</a>. It has a number of different uses, including <a href="/wiki/Fuel" title="Fuel">fuel</a>, <a href="/wiki/Livestock_bedding" class="mw-redirect" title="Livestock bedding">livestock bedding</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fodder" title="Fodder">fodder</a>, <a href="/wiki/Thatching" title="Thatching">thatching</a> and <a href="/wiki/Basket_making" class="mw-redirect" title="Basket making">basket making</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Rice_straw.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Rice_straw.jpg/250px-Rice_straw.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Rice_straw.jpg/500px-Rice_straw.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="640" data-file-height="480"></a><figcaption>Bundles of <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a> straw</figcaption></figure>

Unlike early <a href="/wiki/Genetic_engineering_techniques" title="Genetic engineering techniques">genetic engineering techniques</a> that randomly insert genetic material into a host genome, genome editing targets the insertions to site-specific locations. The basic mechanism involved in genetic manipulations through programmable nucleases is the recognition of target genomic loci and binding of effector <a href="/wiki/DNA-binding_domain" title="DNA-binding domain">DNA-binding domain</a> (DBD), <a href="/wiki/Double-strand_break" class="mw-redirect" title="Double-strand break">double-strand breaks</a> (DSBs) in target DNA by the <a href="/wiki/Restriction_endonuclease" class="mw-redirect" title="Restriction endonuclease">restriction endonucleases</a> (<a href="/wiki/FokI" title="FokI">FokI</a> and <a href="/wiki/CRISPR_associated_protein" class="mw-redirect" title="CRISPR associated protein">Cas</a>), and the repair of DSBs through <a href="/wiki/Homology-directed_recombination" class="mw-redirect" title="Homology-directed recombination">homology-directed recombination</a> (HDR) or <a href="/wiki/Non-homologous_end_joining" title="Non-homologous end joining">non-homologous end joining</a> (NHEJ).<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

</div><p></p></div><div name="colour" term="colour" wikidataID="Q1075" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colour" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: colour<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colour">Colour</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Color</b> (or <b>colour</b> in <a href="/wiki/English_in_the_Commonwealth_of_Nations" title="English in the Commonwealth of Nations">Commonwealth English</a>) is the <a href="/wiki/Visual_perception" title="Visual perception">visual perception</a> produced by the activation of the different types of <a href="/wiki/Cone_cell" title="Cone cell">cone cells</a> in the eye caused by <a href="/wiki/Light" title="Light">light</a>. Though color is not an inherent property of <a href="/wiki/Matter" title="Matter">matter</a>, color perception is related to an object's <a href="/wiki/Light_absorption" class="mw-redirect" title="Light absorption">light absorption</a>, <a href="/wiki/Emission_spectra" class="mw-redirect" title="Emission spectra">emission</a>, <a href="/wiki/Reflection_(physics)" title="Reflection (physics)">reflection</a> and <a href="/wiki/Transmittance" title="Transmittance">transmission</a>. For most humans, visible wavelengths of light are the ones perceived in the <a href="/wiki/Visible_spectrum" title="Visible spectrum">visible light spectrum</a>, with three types of <a href="/wiki/Cone_cell" title="Cone cell">cone cells</a> (<a href="/wiki/Trichromacy" title="Trichromacy">trichromacy</a>). Other animals may have a different number of cone cell types or have eyes sensitive to different wavelengths, such as bees that can distinguish <a href="/wiki/Ultraviolet" title="Ultraviolet">ultraviolet</a>, and thus have a different color sensitivity range. Animal perception of color originates from different light <a href="/wiki/Wavelength" title="Wavelength">wavelength</a> or <a href="/wiki/Spectral_sensitivity" title="Spectral sensitivity">spectral sensitivity</a> in cone cell types, which is then processed by the <a href="/wiki/Brain" title="Brain">brain</a>.

</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:CPCRI_Main_Building.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/CPCRI_Main_Building.jpg/250px-CPCRI_Main_Building.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="148" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/CPCRI_Main_Building.jpg/500px-CPCRI_Main_Building.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2250" data-file-height="1331"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="safflower" term="safflower" wikidataID="Q156625" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safflower" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: safflower<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safflower">Safflower</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Safflower</b> (<i><b>Carthamus tinctorius</b></i>), also <b>false saffron</b>, is a highly branched, <a href="/wiki/Herbaceous" class="mw-redirect" title="Herbaceous">herbaceous</a>, <a href="/wiki/Thistle" title="Thistle">thistle</a>-like <a href="/wiki/Annual_plant" title="Annual plant">annual plant</a> in the family Asteraceae. It is one of the world's oldest crops; today, it is commercially cultivated for <a href="/wiki/Vegetable_oil" title="Vegetable oil">vegetable oil</a> extracted from the <a href="/wiki/Seed" title="Seed">seeds</a>. Plants are 30 to 150&#160;cm (12 to 59&#160;in) tall with globular <a href="/wiki/Flower_head" class="mw-redirect" title="Flower head">flower heads</a> having <a href="/wiki/Yellow" title="Yellow">yellow</a>, <a href="/wiki/Orange_(colour)" title="Orange (colour)">orange</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Red" title="Red">red</a> <a href="/wiki/Flower" title="Flower">flowers</a>. Each branch will usually have from one to five flower heads containing 15 to 20 seeds per head. Safflower is native to arid environments having <a href="/wiki/Wet_season" title="Wet season">seasonal rain</a>. It grows a deep <a href="/wiki/Taproot" title="Taproot">taproot</a> which enables it to thrive in such environments.
</p>

The term is applied to the <a href="/wiki/Sprouting" title="Sprouting">sprouting</a> of a <a href="/wiki/Seedling" title="Seedling">seedling</a> from a <a href="/wiki/Seed" title="Seed">seed</a> of an <a href="/wiki/Flowering_plant" title="Flowering plant">angiosperm</a> or <a href="/wiki/Gymnosperm" title="Gymnosperm">gymnosperm</a>, the growth of a <a href="/wiki/Sporeling" title="Sporeling">sporeling</a> from a <a href="/wiki/Spore" title="Spore">spore</a>, such as the spores of <a href="/wiki/Fungus" title="Fungus">fungi</a>, ferns, <a href="/wiki/Bacteria" title="Bacteria">bacteria</a>, and the growth of the <a href="/wiki/Pollen_tube" title="Pollen tube">pollen tube</a> from the <a href="/wiki/Pollen_grain" class="mw-redirect" title="Pollen grain">pollen grain</a> of a <a href="/wiki/Seed_plant" title="Seed plant">seed plant</a>.

It was founded in 1972 by a consortium of organisations convened by the <a href="/wiki/Ford_Foundation" title="Ford Foundation">Ford-</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Rockefeller_Foundation" title="Rockefeller Foundation">Rockefeller-</a> foundations. Its charter was signed by the <a href="/wiki/FAO" class="mw-redirect" title="FAO">FAO</a> and the <a href="/wiki/UNDP" class="mw-redirect" title="UNDP">UNDP</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:STNMTZ_20211006_2012.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/STNMTZ_20211006_2012.jpg/250px-STNMTZ_20211006_2012.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/STNMTZ_20211006_2012.jpg/500px-STNMTZ_20211006_2012.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="6008" data-file-height="4000"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="linseed" term="linseed" wikidataID="Q45108" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linseed" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: linseed<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linseed">Linseed</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Flax</b>, also known as <b>common flax</b> or <b>linseed</b>, is a <a href="/wiki/Flowering_plant" title="Flowering plant">flowering plant</a>, <i><b>Linum usitatissimum</b></i>, in the family <a href="/wiki/Linaceae" title="Linaceae">Linaceae</a>. It is cultivated as a food and <a href="/wiki/Fiber_crop" title="Fiber crop">fiber crop</a> in regions of the world with <a href="/wiki/Temperate_climate" title="Temperate climate">temperate climates</a>. In 2022, <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</a> produced 75% of the world's supply of flax.

</div><p></p></div><div name="Agricultural Research" term="Agricultural Research" wikidataID="Q3606845" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_research" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Agricultural Research<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_research">Agricultural research</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Agricultural science</b> (or <b>agriscience</b> for short<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>) is a broad multidisciplinary field of <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a> that encompasses the parts of exact, natural, economic and <a href="/wiki/Social_science" title="Social science">social sciences</a> that are used in the practice and understanding of <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a>. Professionals of the agricultural science are called agricultural scientists or <a href="/wiki/Agriculturists" class="mw-redirect" title="Agriculturists">agriculturists</a>.
</p>

</div><p></p></div><div name="moisture stress" term="moisture stress" wikidataID="Q6894868" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moisture_stress" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: moisture stress<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moisture_stress">Moisture stress</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Moisture stress</b> is a form of <a href="/wiki/Abiotic_stress" title="Abiotic stress">abiotic stress</a> that occurs when the moisture of plant tissues is reduced to suboptimal levels.  Water stress occurs in response to atmospheric and soil water availability when the <a href="/wiki/Transpiration" title="Transpiration">transpiration</a> rate exceeds the rate of water uptake by the roots and cells lose <a href="/wiki/Turgor_pressure" title="Turgor pressure">turgor pressure</a>. Moisture stress is described by two main metrics, <a href="/wiki/Water_potential" title="Water potential">water potential</a> and <a href="/wiki/Water_content" title="Water content">water content</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

<p></p></div><div name="grain quality" term="grain quality" wikidataID="Q16249780" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grain_quality" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: grain quality<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grain_quality">Grain quality</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">
In agriculture, <b>grain quality</b> judgement depends on the intended use of the <a href="/wiki/Grain" title="Grain">grain</a>. In <a href="/wiki/Ethanol" title="Ethanol">ethanol</a> production, aspects of the <a href="/wiki/Chemical_composition" title="Chemical composition">chemical composition</a> of grain&#8211;and specific aspects such as <a href="/wiki/Starch" title="Starch">starch</a> content&#8211;are considered important. In <a href="/wiki/Food_processing" title="Food processing">food processing</a> and <a href="/wiki/Feed_manufacturing" title="Feed manufacturing">feed manufacturing</a>, properties such as <a href="/wiki/Protein" title="Protein">protein</a>, oil, and <a href="/wiki/Sugar" title="Sugar">sugar</a> are significant. In the <a href="/wiki/Mill_(grinding)" title="Mill (grinding)">milling</a> industry, soundness is the most important factor. For grain farmers, high <a href="/wiki/Germination" title="Germination">germination</a> percentage and <a href="/wiki/Seed_dormancy" title="Seed dormancy">seed dormancy</a> are the main features to consider. For <a href="/wiki/Consumer" title="Consumer">consumers</a>, sensory properties such as color and flavor are most important.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Wheat_grains,_a_yellow_bean_among_vitreous_kernels.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Wheat_grains%2C_a_yellow_bean_among_vitreous_kernels.png/250px-Wheat_grains%2C_a_yellow_bean_among_vitreous_kernels.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="180" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2a/Wheat_grains%2C_a_yellow_bean_among_vitreous_kernels.png 1.5x" data-file-width="326" data-file-height="235"></a><figcaption>Red arrow points to a non-vitreous "yellow bean" among vitreous kernels of wheat</figcaption></figure>

It was <a href="/wiki/History_of_rice_cultivation" title="History of rice cultivation">first domesticated</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Yangtze_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Yangtze River">Yangtze River</a> basin in China 13,500 to 8,200 years ago.<sup id="cite_ref-Normile_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Normile-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Vaughanetal2008_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vaughanetal2008-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-harris_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-harris-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Zhang2012_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Zhang2012-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Mature_Rice_(India)_by_Augustus_Binu.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Mature_Rice_%28India%29_by_Augustus_Binu.jpg/250px-Mature_Rice_%28India%29_by_Augustus_Binu.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Mature_Rice_%28India%29_by_Augustus_Binu.jpg/500px-Mature_Rice_%28India%29_by_Augustus_Binu.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3020" data-file-height="2000"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="genetic diversity" term="genetic diversity" wikidataID="Q585259" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_diversity" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: genetic diversity<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_diversity">Genetic diversity</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Genetic diversity</b> is the total number of <a href="/wiki/Genetics" title="Genetics">genetic</a> characteristics in the genetic makeup of a species. It ranges widely, from the number of species to differences within <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a>, and can be correlated to the span of survival for a species.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is distinguished from <i><a href="/wiki/Genetic_variability" title="Genetic variability">genetic variability</a></i>, which describes the tendency of genetic characteristics to vary.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Human_karyotype.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Human_karyotype.svg/500px-Human_karyotype.svg.png" decoding="async" width="350" height="377" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Human_karyotype.svg/960px-Human_karyotype.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="1346" data-file-height="1449"></a><figcaption>A graphical representation of the typical human <a href="/wiki/Karyotype" title="Karyotype">karyotype</a>.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Kerala" term="Kerala" wikidataID="Q1186" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Kerala<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala">Kerala</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Kerala</b><sup id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India" title="States and union territories of India">state</a> of <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Malabar_Coast" title="Malabar Coast">Malabar Coast</a>. It was formed on 1 November 1956 under the <a href="/wiki/States_Reorganisation_Act" class="mw-redirect" title="States Reorganisation Act">States Reorganisation Act</a>, which unified the country's <a href="/wiki/Malayalam" title="Malayalam">Malayalam</a>-speaking regions into a single state. Covering 38,863&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (15,005&#160;sq&#160;mi), it is bordered by <a href="/wiki/Karnataka" title="Karnataka">Karnataka</a> to the north and northeast, <a href="/wiki/Tamil_Nadu" title="Tamil Nadu">Tamil Nadu</a> to the east and south, and the <a href="/wiki/Laccadive_Sea" title="Laccadive Sea">Laccadive Sea</a> to the west. With 33 million inhabitants according to the <a href="/wiki/2011_Census_of_India" class="mw-redirect" title="2011 Census of India">2011 census</a>, Kerala is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_of_India_by_population" class="mw-redirect" title="List of states of India by population">13th-most populous state in India</a>. It is divided into <a href="/wiki/List_of_districts_of_Kerala" title="List of districts of Kerala">14 districts</a>, with <a href="/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram" title="Thiruvananthapuram">Thiruvananthapuram</a> as the capital. Malayalam is the most widely spoken language and, along with English, serves as an official language of the state.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Boathouse_(7063399547).jpg" class="mw-file-description" title="A houseboat in the Kerala backwaters"><img alt="A collection of images of Kerala" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Boathouse_%287063399547%29.jpg/330px-Boathouse_%287063399547%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="270" height="155" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Boathouse_%287063399547%29.jpg/500px-Boathouse_%287063399547%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Boathouse_%287063399547%29.jpg/960px-Boathouse_%287063399547%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5103" data-file-height="2932"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="tubers" term="tubers" wikidataID="Q183319" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tubers" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: tubers<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tubers">Tubers</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Tubers</b> are a type of enlarged structure that <a href="/wiki/Plant" title="Plant">plants</a> use as <a href="/wiki/Storage_organ" title="Storage organ">storage organs</a> for <a href="/wiki/Nutrient" title="Nutrient">nutrients</a>, derived from stems or roots. </p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cairns_climate.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Cairns_climate.svg/250px-Cairns_climate.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Cairns_climate.svg/500px-Cairns_climate.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="600"></a><figcaption>The rainfall distribution by month in <a href="/wiki/Cairns" title="Cairns">Cairns</a>, Australia</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="food security" term="food security" wikidataID="Q1229911" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_security" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: food security<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_security">Food security</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Food security</b> is the state of having reliable access to a sufficient quantity of affordable, healthy <a href="/wiki/Human_food" title="Human food">food</a>. The availability of food for people of any class, gender, status, ethnicity, or religion is another element of food protection. Similarly, <a href="/wiki/Household" title="Household">household</a> food security is considered to exist when all the members of a family have consistent access to enough food for an active, <a href="/wiki/Health" title="Health">healthy</a> life.<sup id="cite_ref-usda_measuring_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-usda_measuring-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Food-secure individuals do not live in <a href="/wiki/Hunger" title="Hunger">hunger</a> or fear of <a href="/wiki/Starvation" title="Starvation">starvation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FAO_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FAO-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Food security includes resilience to future disruptions of food supply. Such a disruption could occur due to various risk factors such as <a href="/wiki/Drought" title="Drought">droughts</a> and <a href="/wiki/Flood" title="Flood">floods</a><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>, shipping disruptions, fuel shortages, economic instability, and wars.<sup id="cite_ref-FAO-2013_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FAO-2013-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <b>Food insecurity</b> is the opposite of food security: a state where there is only limited or uncertain availability of suitable food.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Africa_Food_Security_18_(10665134354).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg/250px-Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="376" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg/500px-Africa_Food_Security_18_%2810665134354%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1880" data-file-height="2825"></a><figcaption>Women selling <a href="/wiki/Produce" title="Produce">produce</a> at a market in <a href="/wiki/Lilongwe" title="Lilongwe">Lilongwe</a>, <a href="/wiki/Malawi" title="Malawi">Malawi</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Agronomy" term="Agronomy" wikidataID="Q173113" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agronomy" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Agronomy<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agronomy">Agronomy</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Agronomy</b> is the science and technology of producing and using <a href="/wiki/Plant" title="Plant">plants</a> by <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a> for <a href="/wiki/Food" title="Food">food</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fuel" title="Fuel">fuel</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fiber" title="Fiber">fiber</a>, chemicals, recreation, or land conservation. Agronomy has come to include research of <a href="/wiki/Plant_genetics" title="Plant genetics">plant genetics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Plant_physiology" title="Plant physiology">plant physiology</a>, <a href="/wiki/Meteorology" title="Meteorology">meteorology</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Soil_science" title="Soil science">soil science</a>. It is the application of a combination of sciences such as <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chemistry" title="Chemistry">chemistry</a>, <a href="/wiki/Economics" title="Economics">economics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ecology" title="Ecology">ecology</a>, <a href="/wiki/Earth_science" title="Earth science">earth science</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Genetics" title="Genetics">genetics</a>. Professionals in the field are known as <a href="/wiki/Agriculturist" title="Agriculturist">agronomists</a>.
</p>

(August 2024)">better&#160;source&#160;needed</span></a></i>]</sup>
</p><p></p></div><div name="Rock phosphate" term="Rock phosphate" wikidataID="Q1424327" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_phosphate" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Rock phosphate<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_phosphate">Rock phosphate</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Phosphorite</b>, <b>phosphate rock</b> or <b>rock phosphate</b> is a non-<a href="/wiki/Detrital" class="mw-redirect" title="Detrital">detrital</a> <a href="/wiki/Sedimentary_rock" title="Sedimentary rock">sedimentary rock</a> that contains high amounts of <a href="/wiki/Phosphate_minerals" class="mw-redirect" title="Phosphate minerals">phosphate minerals</a>. The phosphate content of phosphorite (or grade of phosphate rock) varies greatly, from 4%<sup id="cite_ref-fao_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fao-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> to 20% <a href="/wiki/Phosphorus_pentoxide" title="Phosphorus pentoxide">phosphorus pentoxide</a> (P<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>). Marketed phosphate rock is enriched ("beneficiated") to at least 28%, often more than 30% P<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>. This occurs through washing, screening, deliming, magnetic separation or flotation.<sup id="cite_ref-fao_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fao-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> By comparison, the average phosphorus content of sedimentary rocks is less than 0.2%.<sup id="cite_ref-Blatt_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Blatt-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Peloidal_phosphorite_Phosphoria_Formation_Simplot_Mine_Idaho.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Peloidal_phosphorite_Phosphoria_Formation_Simplot_Mine_Idaho.jpg/250px-Peloidal_phosphorite_Phosphoria_Formation_Simplot_Mine_Idaho.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="149" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Peloidal_phosphorite_Phosphoria_Formation_Simplot_Mine_Idaho.jpg/500px-Peloidal_phosphorite_Phosphoria_Formation_Simplot_Mine_Idaho.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1344" data-file-height="799"></a><figcaption>Peloidal phosphorite, <a href="/wiki/Phosphoria_Formation" title="Phosphoria Formation">Phosphoria Formation</a>, Simplot Mine, Idaho. 4.6 cm wide.</figcaption></figure>

Horticulture is commonly associated with the more professional and technical aspects of plant cultivation on a smaller and more controlled scale than <a href="/wiki/Agronomy" title="Agronomy">agronomy</a>. There are various divisions of horticulture because plants are grown for a variety of purposes.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> These divisions include, but are not limited to: <a href="/wiki/Plant_propagation" title="Plant propagation">propagation</a>, <a href="/wiki/Arboriculture" title="Arboriculture">arboriculture</a>, <a href="/wiki/Landscaping" title="Landscaping">landscaping</a>, <a href="/wiki/Floriculture" title="Floriculture">floriculture</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sod" title="Sod">turf</a> maintenance. For each of these, there are various professions, aspects, tools used and associated challenges -- each requiring highly specialized skills and knowledge on the part of the horticulturist.

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="shelf life" term="shelf life" wikidataID="Q1689021" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelf_life" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: shelf life<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelf_life">Shelf life</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Shelf life</b> is the length of time that a commodity may be stored without becoming unfit for use, consumption, or sale.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In other words, it might refer to whether a commodity should no longer be on a pantry shelf (unfit for use), or no longer on a supermarket shelf (unfit for sale, but not yet unfit for use). It applies to <a href="/wiki/Cosmetics" title="Cosmetics">cosmetics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Food" title="Food">foods</a> and <a href="/wiki/Drink" title="Drink">beverages</a>, <a href="/wiki/Medical_device" title="Medical device">medical devices</a>, <a href="/wiki/Medicine" title="Medicine">medicines</a>, <a href="/wiki/Explosive" title="Explosive">explosives</a>, <a href="/wiki/Medication" title="Medication">pharmaceutical drugs</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-:0_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Chemical_substance" class="mw-redirect" title="Chemical substance">chemicals</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tire" title="Tire">tyres</a>, <a href="/wiki/Electric_battery" title="Electric battery">batteries</a>, and many other <a href="/wiki/Decomposition" title="Decomposition">perishable</a> items. In some regions, an advisory <i>best before</i>, mandatory <i>use by</i> or <i>freshness date</i> is required on packaged perishable foods. The concept of <a href="/wiki/Expiration_date" title="Expiration date">expiration date</a> is related but legally distinct in some jurisdictions.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Expiration.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/Expiration.jpg/250px-Expiration.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="186" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/Expiration.jpg/500px-Expiration.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="662" data-file-height="493"></a><figcaption>This pack of diced pork says 'Display until' 7 May and 'Use by' 8 May.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="interspecific hybrids" term="interspecific hybrids" wikidataID="Q42621" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interspecific_hybrids" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: interspecific hybrids<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interspecific_hybrids">Interspecific hybrids</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a>, a <b>hybrid</b> is the offspring resulting from combining the qualities of two organisms of different <a href="/wiki/Variety_(botany)" title="Variety (botany)">varieties</a>, <a href="/wiki/Subspecies" title="Subspecies">subspecies</a>, <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> or <a href="/wiki/Genus" title="Genus">genera</a> through <a href="/wiki/Sexual_reproduction" title="Sexual reproduction">sexual reproduction</a>. Generally, it means that each cell has genetic material from two different organisms, whereas an individual where some cells are derived from a different organism is called a <a href="/wiki/Chimera_(genetics)" title="Chimera (genetics)">chimera</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Hybrids are not always intermediates between their parents such as in <a href="/wiki/Blending_inheritance" title="Blending inheritance">blending inheritance</a> (a now discredited theory in modern <a href="/wiki/Genetics" title="Genetics">genetics</a> by <a href="/wiki/Particulate_inheritance" title="Particulate inheritance">particulate inheritance</a>), but can show <a href="/wiki/Heterosis" title="Heterosis">hybrid vigor</a>, sometimes growing larger or taller than either parent. The concept of a hybrid is interpreted differently in animal and plant breeding, where there is interest in the individual parentage. In <a href="/wiki/Genetics" title="Genetics">genetics</a>, attention is focused on the numbers of <a href="/wiki/Chromosome" title="Chromosome">chromosomes</a>. In taxonomy, a key question is how closely related the parent <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> are.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="margin-left:0.1em; white-space:nowrap;">[<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify" title="Wikipedia:Please clarify"><span title="Why are these cases different or separate, and how are they related to different definitions of what a hybrid is? (August 2024)">clarification needed</span></a></i>]</sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Juancito.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Juancito.jpg/500px-Juancito.jpg" decoding="async" width="340" height="285" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Juancito.jpg/960px-Juancito.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1486" data-file-height="1245"></a><figcaption>A <a href="/wiki/Mule" title="Mule">mule</a> is a <a href="/wiki/Sterility_(physiology)" title="Sterility (physiology)">sterile</a> hybrid of a male <a href="/wiki/Donkey" title="Donkey">donkey</a> and a female <a href="/wiki/Horse" title="Horse">horse</a>. Mules are smaller than horses but stronger than donkeys, making them useful as <a href="/wiki/Pack_animal" title="Pack animal">pack animals</a>.</figcaption></figure>

Its many <a href="/wiki/Variety_(botany)" title="Variety (botany)">varieties</a> differ substantially in the shape and bitterness of the fruit.

</div><p></p></div><div name="training" term="training" wikidataID="Q918385" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: training<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training">Training</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Training</b> is <a href="/wiki/Teaching" title="Teaching">teaching</a>, or developing in oneself or others, any <a href="/wiki/Skill" title="Skill">skills</a> and <a href="/wiki/Knowledge" title="Knowledge">knowledge</a>  or <a href="/wiki/Physical_fitness" title="Physical fitness">fitness</a> that relate to specific <a href="/wiki/Practicality" class="mw-redirect" title="Practicality">useful</a> <a href="/wiki/Competence_(human_resources)" title="Competence (human resources)">competencies</a>. Training has specific goals of improving one's <a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/capability" class="extiw" title="wikt:capability">capability</a>, capacity, <a href="/wiki/Productivity" title="Productivity">productivity</a> and <a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/performance" class="extiw" title="wikt:performance">performance</a>. It forms the core of <a href="/wiki/Apprenticeship" title="Apprenticeship">apprenticeships</a> and provides the backbone of content at <a href="/wiki/Institute_of_technology" title="Institute of technology">institutes of technology</a> (also known as technical colleges or polytechnics). In addition to the basic training required for a <a href="/wiki/Trade_(profession)" class="mw-redirect" title="Trade (profession)">trade</a>, <a href="/wiki/Employment" title="Employment">occupation</a> or <a href="/wiki/Profession" title="Profession">profession</a>, training may continue beyond initial competence to maintain, upgrade and update skills throughout <a href="/wiki/Career" title="Career">working life</a>. People within some professions and occupations may refer to this sort of training as <a href="/wiki/Professional_development" title="Professional development">professional development</a>. Training also refers to the development of physical fitness related to a specific competence, such as sport, martial arts, military applications and some other occupations. Training methods of all types can be improved by setting specific, time-based, and difficult goals. This allows for the progressive mastery of a topic with a measured outcome.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

It is the most widely cultivated species of several plants in the family <a href="/wiki/Araceae" title="Araceae">Araceae</a> that are used as vegetables for their <a href="/wiki/Corm" title="Corm">corms</a>, leaves, stems and <a href="/wiki/Petiole_(botany)" title="Petiole (botany)">petioles</a>. The tubers are usually a vivid <a href="/wiki/Violet_(color)" title="Violet (color)">violet</a>-<a href="/wiki/Purple" title="Purple">purple</a> to bright <a href="/wiki/Lavender_(color)" title="Lavender (color)">lavender</a> (hence the common name), but some range from creamy-white to plain white. It is sometimes confused with <a href="/wiki/Taro" title="Taro">taro</a> and the Okinawa sweet potato <i>beniimo</i><span style="font-weight: normal"> (<span title="Japanese-language text"><span lang="ja">&#32005;&#33419;</span></span>)</span> (<i><a href="/wiki/Ipomoea_batatas" class="mw-redirect" title="Ipomoea batatas">Ipomoea batatas</a></i> '<a href="/wiki/List_of_sweet_potato_cultivars" title="List of sweet potato cultivars">Ayamurasaki</a>'), however <i>D. alata</i> is also grown in Okinawa. Its origins are in the Asian and Oceanian <a href="/wiki/Tropics" title="Tropics">tropics</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-grin_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-grin-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Some varieties attain to great size. A "Mambatap" greater yam grown in Maprik, East Sepik District, Papua New Guinea  around 1939 was 3.5&#160;m (11&#160;ft) in length.<sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="quantitative traits" term="quantitative traits" wikidataID="Q55608248" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantitative_traits" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: quantitative traits<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantitative_traits">Quantitative traits</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Complex traits</b>, also known as <a href="/wiki/Polygenic_traits" class="mw-redirect" title="Polygenic traits">polygenic</a> or <a href="/wiki/Multigenic_trait" class="mw-redirect" title="Multigenic trait">multigenic</a> traits, are <a href="/wiki/Phenotypes" class="mw-redirect" title="Phenotypes">phenotypes</a> determined by the <a href="/wiki/Gene%E2%80%93environment_interaction" title="Gene&#8211;environment interaction">interaction</a> of multiple genetic and environmental factors. A central goal of contemporary <a href="/wiki/Genetics" title="Genetics">genetics</a> research is to understand the <a href="/wiki/Mechanism_(biology)" title="Mechanism (biology)">molecular mechanisms</a> by which <a href="/wiki/Genetic_variation" title="Genetic variation">genetic variation</a> influences complex traits.<sup id="cite_ref-Fisher_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Fisher-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:1_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Examples of complex traits in humans include <a href="/wiki/Human_height" title="Human height">height</a>; <a href="/wiki/Intelligence" title="Intelligence">intelligence</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cognitive_skill" title="Cognitive skill">cognitive function</a>; <a href="/wiki/Body-mass_index" class="mw-redirect" title="Body-mass index">body-mass index</a>; <a href="/wiki/Blood_pressure" title="Blood pressure">blood pressure</a>; and <a href="/wiki/Statistical_risk" title="Statistical risk">risk</a> for <a href="/wiki/Complex_disease" class="mw-redirect" title="Complex disease">complex diseases</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Diabetes" title="Diabetes">diabetes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Heart_disease" class="mw-redirect" title="Heart disease">heart disease</a>, <a href="/wiki/Alzheimer%27s_disease" title="Alzheimer's disease">Alzheimer's disease</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Schizophrenia" title="Schizophrenia">schizophrenia</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:2013_09_10_Tomate.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/2013_09_10_Tomate.jpg/330px-2013_09_10_Tomate.jpg" decoding="async" width="265" height="182" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/2013_09_10_Tomate.jpg/500px-2013_09_10_Tomate.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/2013_09_10_Tomate.jpg/960px-2013_09_10_Tomate.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3151" data-file-height="2160"></a><figcaption>The size of a tomato is one example of a complex trait.</figcaption></figure>

Access to cheaper <a href="/wiki/Energy" title="Energy">energy</a> has become essential to the functioning of modern economies. However, the uneven distribution of <a href="/wiki/Energy_supplies" class="mw-redirect" title="Energy supplies">energy supplies</a> among countries has led to significant <a href="/wiki/Vulnerability" title="Vulnerability">vulnerabilities</a>. International energy relations have contributed to the <a href="/wiki/Globalization" title="Globalization">globalization</a> of the world leading to energy security and energy vulnerability at the same time.<sup id="cite_ref-overland-2016_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-overland-2016-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:US_Navy_100330-N-9565D-020_An_F-A-18_Super_Hornet_from_Air_Test_and_Evaluation_Squadron_(VX)_23_with_green_markings_and_the_U.S._Department_of_the_Navy_Energy_Security_logo.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/US_Navy_100330-N-9565D-020_An_F-A-18_Super_Hornet_from_Air_Test_and_Evaluation_Squadron_%28VX%29_23_with_green_markings_and_the_U.S._Department_of_the_Navy_Energy_Security_logo.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="201" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/US_Navy_100330-N-9565D-020_An_F-A-18_Super_Hornet_from_Air_Test_and_Evaluation_Squadron_%28VX%29_23_with_green_markings_and_the_U.S._Department_of_the_Navy_Energy_Security_logo.jpg/500px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/US_Navy_100330-N-9565D-020_An_F-A-18_Super_Hornet_from_Air_Test_and_Evaluation_Squadron_%28VX%29_23_with_green_markings_and_the_U.S._Department_of_the_Navy_Energy_Security_logo.jpg/960px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3872" data-file-height="2592"></a><figcaption>A <a href="/wiki/United_States_Navy" title="United States Navy">U.S. Navy</a> <a href="/wiki/Boeing_F/A-18E/F_Super_Hornet" title="Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet">F/A-18 Super Hornet</a> displaying an "Energy Security" logo.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Taiwan" term="Taiwan" wikidataID="Q865" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Taiwan<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan">Taiwan</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Taiwan</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-word2_35-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-word2-35"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>I<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ROC_territory_39-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ROC_territory-39"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>j<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> officially the <b>Republic of China</b> (<b>ROC</b>),<sup id="cite_ref-word1_40-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-word1-40"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>II<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a country<sup id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>29<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> in <a href="/wiki/East_Asia" title="East Asia">East Asia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Southeast_Asia_45-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Southeast_Asia-45"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>m<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The main <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Taiwan" title="Geography of Taiwan">island of Taiwan</a>, also known as <i>Formosa</i>, lies between the <a href="/wiki/East_China_Sea" title="East China Sea">East</a> and <a href="/wiki/South_China_Sea" title="South China Sea">South China Seas</a> in the northwestern <a href="/wiki/Pacific_Ocean" title="Pacific Ocean">Pacific Ocean</a>, with the <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">People's Republic of China</a> (PRC) to the northwest, <a href="/wiki/Japan" title="Japan">Japan</a> to the northeast, and the <a href="/wiki/Philippines" title="Philippines">Philippines</a> to the south. It has an area of 35,808 square kilometres (13,826 square miles), with mountain ranges dominating the eastern two-thirds and plains in the western third, where its <a href="/wiki/Urbanization_by_country" class="mw-redirect" title="Urbanization by country">highly urbanized</a> population is concentrated. The combined <a href="/wiki/Free_area_of_the_Republic_of_China" class="mw-redirect" title="Free area of the Republic of China">territories under ROC control</a> consist of <a href="/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Taiwan" title="List of islands of Taiwan">168 islands</a><sup id="cite_ref-Taiwan_Islands_56-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Taiwan_Islands-56"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>n<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> in total covering 36,193 square kilometres (13,974 square miles).<sup id="cite_ref-taiwansnapshot_26-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-taiwansnapshot-26"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NDC2021_57-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NDC2021-57"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Taipei%E2%80%93Keelung_metropolitan_area" title="Taipei&#8211;Keelung metropolitan area">largest metropolitan area</a> is formed by <a href="/wiki/Taipei" title="Taipei">Taipei</a> (the capital), <a href="/wiki/New_Taipei_City" title="New Taipei City">New Taipei City</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Keelung" title="Keelung">Keelung</a>. With around 23.9 million inhabitants, Taiwan is among the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population_density" title="List of countries and dependencies by population density">most densely populated countries</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:%E5%8D%91%E5%8D%97%E9%81%BA%E5%9D%80%E4%BA%BA%E7%8D%B8%E5%BD%A2%E7%8E%89%E7%8E%A6.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/%E5%8D%91%E5%8D%97%E9%81%BA%E5%9D%80%E4%BA%BA%E7%8D%B8%E5%BD%A2%E7%8E%89%E7%8E%A6.jpg/250px-%E5%8D%91%E5%8D%97%E9%81%BA%E5%9D%80%E4%BA%BA%E7%8D%B8%E5%BD%A2%E7%8E%89%E7%8E%A6.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="275" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/%E5%8D%91%E5%8D%97%E9%81%BA%E5%9D%80%E4%BA%BA%E7%8D%B8%E5%BD%A2%E7%8E%89%E7%8E%A6.jpg/330px-%E5%8D%91%E5%8D%97%E9%81%BA%E5%9D%80%E4%BA%BA%E7%8D%B8%E5%BD%A2%E7%8E%89%E7%8E%A6.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/%E5%8D%91%E5%8D%97%E9%81%BA%E5%9D%80%E4%BA%BA%E7%8D%B8%E5%BD%A2%E7%8E%89%E7%8E%A6.jpg/500px-%E5%8D%91%E5%8D%97%E9%81%BA%E5%9D%80%E4%BA%BA%E7%8D%B8%E5%BD%A2%E7%8E%89%E7%8E%A6.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1019" data-file-height="1475"></a><figcaption>2,300-year-old jade, unearthed at <a href="/wiki/Beinan_Cultural_Park" class="mw-redirect" title="Beinan Cultural Park">Beinan Cultural Park</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="buckwheat" term="buckwheat" wikidataID="Q132734" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckwheat" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: buckwheat<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckwheat">Buckwheat</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Buckwheat</b> (<i><b>Fagopyrum esculentum</b></i>) or <b>common buckwheat</b><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-USDA_GRIN_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-USDA_GRIN-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/Flowering_plant" title="Flowering plant">flowering plant</a> in the knotweed family <a href="/wiki/Polygonaceae" title="Polygonaceae">Polygonaceae</a> cultivated for its grain-like seeds and as a <a href="/wiki/Cover_crop" title="Cover crop">cover crop</a>. Buckwheat cultivation originated around the 6th millennium BC in the region of what is now <a href="/wiki/Yunnan" title="Yunnan">Yunnan Province</a> in southwestern <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a>. The name "buckwheat" is used for several other species, such as <i><a href="/wiki/Fagopyrum_tataricum" title="Fagopyrum tataricum">Fagopyrum tataricum</a></i>, a domesticated food plant raised in Asia.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Leiden_University_Library_-_Seikei_Zusetsu_vol._17,_page_027_-_%E8%95%8E%E9%BA%A6_-_Fagopyrum_esculentum_Moench,_1804.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Leiden_University_Library_-_Seikei_Zusetsu_vol._17%2C_page_027_-_%E8%95%8E%E9%BA%A6_-_Fagopyrum_esculentum_Moench%2C_1804.jpg/250px-Leiden_University_Library_-_Seikei_Zusetsu_vol._17%2C_page_027_-_%E8%95%8E%E9%BA%A6_-_Fagopyrum_esculentum_Moench%2C_1804.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="375" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Leiden_University_Library_-_Seikei_Zusetsu_vol._17%2C_page_027_-_%E8%95%8E%E9%BA%A6_-_Fagopyrum_esculentum_Moench%2C_1804.jpg/500px-Leiden_University_Library_-_Seikei_Zusetsu_vol._17%2C_page_027_-_%E8%95%8E%E9%BA%A6_-_Fagopyrum_esculentum_Moench%2C_1804.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="533" data-file-height="800"></a><figcaption>Buckwheat, illustration from the Japanese agricultural encyclopedia Seikei Zusetsu (1804)</figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="cabbage" term="cabbage" wikidataID="Q35051" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabbage" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: cabbage<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabbage">Cabbage</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Cabbage</b>, comprising several <a href="/wiki/Cultivar" title="Cultivar">cultivars</a> of <i><a href="/wiki/Brassica_oleracea" title="Brassica oleracea">Brassica oleracea</a></i>, is a leafy green, red (purple), or white (pale green) <a href="/wiki/Biennial_plant" title="Biennial plant">biennial plant</a> grown as an <a href="/wiki/Annual_plant" title="Annual plant">annual</a> vegetable crop for its dense-leaved heads. It is descended from the wild cabbage (<a href="/wiki/Brassica_oleracea" title="Brassica oleracea"><i>B.&#160;oleracea</i> var. <i>oleracea</i></a>), and belongs to the "<a href="/wiki/Cole_crops" class="mw-redirect" title="Cole crops">cole crops</a>" or <a href="/wiki/Brassica" title="Brassica">brassicas</a>, meaning it is closely related to <a href="/wiki/Broccoli" title="Broccoli">broccoli</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cauliflower" title="Cauliflower">cauliflower</a> (var. <i>botrytis</i>); <a href="/wiki/Brussels_sprouts" class="mw-redirect" title="Brussels sprouts">Brussels sprouts</a> (var. <i>gemmifera</i>); and <a href="/wiki/Savoy_cabbage" title="Savoy cabbage">Savoy cabbage</a> (var. <i>sabauda</i>).
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Brassica_oleracea_Helgoland1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Brassica_oleracea_Helgoland1.jpg/250px-Brassica_oleracea_Helgoland1.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="253" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Brassica_oleracea_Helgoland1.jpg/330px-Brassica_oleracea_Helgoland1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Brassica_oleracea_Helgoland1.jpg/500px-Brassica_oleracea_Helgoland1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1488" data-file-height="1984"></a><figcaption>The cabbage <a href="/wiki/Inflorescence" title="Inflorescence">inflorescence</a>, which appears in the plant's second year of growth, features white or yellow flowers, each with four perpendicularly arranged petals.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="aphids" term="aphids" wikidataID="Q183350" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aphids" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: aphids<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aphids">Aphids</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Aphids</b> are small <a href="/wiki/Sap" title="Sap">sap</a>-sucking <a href="/wiki/Insect" title="Insect">insects</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Taxonomic_rank" title="Taxonomic rank">family</a> <b>Aphididae</b>. Common names include <b>greenfly</b> and <b>blackfly</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> although individuals within a species can vary widely in color. The group includes the fluffy white <a href="/wiki/Eriosomatinae" title="Eriosomatinae">woolly aphids</a>. A typical life cycle involves flightless females giving <a href="/wiki/Viviparity" title="Viviparity">live birth</a> to female <a href="/wiki/Nymph_(biology)" title="Nymph (biology)">nymphs</a>&#8212;who may also be already <a href="/wiki/Pregnancy" title="Pregnancy">pregnant</a>, an adaptation scientists call <a href="/wiki/Telescoping_generations" title="Telescoping generations">telescoping generations</a>&#8212;without the involvement of males. <a href="/wiki/Developmental_biology" title="Developmental biology">Maturing</a> rapidly, females breed profusely so that the number of these insects multiplies quickly. <a href="/wiki/Alate" title="Alate">Winged females</a> may develop later in the season, allowing the insects to colonize new plants. In <a href="/wiki/Temperate_climate" title="Temperate climate">temperate</a> regions, a phase of <a href="/wiki/Sexual_reproduction" title="Sexual reproduction">sexual reproduction</a> occurs in the <a href="/wiki/Autumn" title="Autumn">autumn</a>, with the insects often overwintering as <a href="/wiki/Egg" title="Egg">eggs</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg/250px-Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="296" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg/500px-Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1914" data-file-height="2270"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="longistaminata" term="longistaminata" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=longistaminata" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: longistaminata<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=longistaminata">longistaminata</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">
