Crops are cultivated at scale to produce food, fiber, fuel, and other products. Crops have been central to human civilization since the <a href="/wiki/First_agricultural_revolution" class="mw-redirect" title="First agricultural revolution">first agricultural revolution</a>, a key stage in the broader <a href="/wiki/History_of_agriculture" title="History of agriculture">history of agriculture</a>, when early societies domesticated plants for food and trade.<sup id="cite_ref-lewin35_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lewin35-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Today, a small number of <a href="/wiki/Staple_food" title="Staple food">staple crops</a> such as rice, wheat, maize, and sugarcane account for the majority of global production. Because of their economic importance, crops are studied within several scientific disciplines, including <a href="/wiki/Agronomy" title="Agronomy">agronomy</a>, <a href="/wiki/Agricultural_science" title="Agricultural science">agricultural science</a>, <a href="/wiki/Horticulture" title="Horticulture">horticulture</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Forestry" title="Forestry">forestry</a>.
</p>

</div><p></p></div><div name="Germany" term="Germany" wikidataID="Q183" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Germany<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany">Germany</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Germany</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>d<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> officially the <b>Federal Republic of Germany</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>e<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a country in <a href="/wiki/Western_Europe" title="Western Europe">Western</a> and <a href="/wiki/Central_Europe" title="Central Europe">Central Europe</a>. It lies between the <a href="/wiki/Baltic_Sea" title="Baltic Sea">Baltic Sea</a> and the <a href="/wiki/North_Sea" title="North Sea">North Sea</a> to the north with the <a href="/wiki/Alps" title="Alps">Alps</a> to the south. Its sixteen <a href="/wiki/States_of_Germany" title="States of Germany">constituent states</a> have <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_Germany" title="Demographics of Germany">a total population</a> of over 82 million, making it the most populous <a href="/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union" title="Member state of the European Union">member state of the European Union</a>. Germany borders <a href="/wiki/Denmark" title="Denmark">Denmark</a> to the north; <a href="/wiki/Poland" title="Poland">Poland</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Czech_Republic" title="Czech Republic">Czech Republic</a> to the east; <a href="/wiki/Austria" title="Austria">Austria</a> and <a href="/wiki/Switzerland" title="Switzerland">Switzerland</a> to the south; and <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</a>, <a href="/wiki/Luxembourg" title="Luxembourg">Luxembourg</a>, <a href="/wiki/Belgium" title="Belgium">Belgium</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Netherlands" title="Netherlands">Netherlands</a> to the west. The <a href="/wiki/Capital_of_Germany" title="Capital of Germany">nation's capital</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Germany_by_population" title="List of cities in Germany by population">most populous city</a> is <a href="/wiki/Berlin" title="Berlin">Berlin</a> and its main financial centre is <a href="/wiki/Frankfurt" title="Frankfurt">Frankfurt</a>; the largest urban area is the <a href="/wiki/Ruhr" title="Ruhr">Ruhr</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Trier_012.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Trier_012.JPG/250px-Trier_012.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="172" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Trier_012.JPG/500px-Trier_012.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="4231" data-file-height="2904"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Aula_Palatina" title="Aula Palatina">Basilica of Constantine</a> in <a href="/wiki/Trier" title="Trier">Trier</a> (<i><a href="/wiki/Augusta_Treverorum" title="Augusta Treverorum">Augusta Treverorum</a></i>), built in the 4th century</figcaption></figure>

The  external examiner system originated in 1832 with the establishment of the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Durham" class="mw-redirect" title="University of Durham">University of Durham</a>, and was then adopted by other British universities in the 19th century before spreading to other countries.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:ExamInCosin.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8a/ExamInCosin.jpg/330px-ExamInCosin.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="209" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8a/ExamInCosin.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="492" data-file-height="342"></a><figcaption>Examination at <a href="/wiki/Durham_University" title="Durham University">Durham University</a> in 1842, where the external examiner system originated.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Quarantine" term="Quarantine" wikidataID="Q182899" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarantine" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Quarantine<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarantine">Quarantine</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>quarantine</b> is a restriction on the <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_movement" title="Freedom of movement">movement of people</a>, animals, and goods which is intended to prevent the spread of <a href="/wiki/Disease" title="Disease">disease</a> or <a href="/wiki/Pest_(organism)" title="Pest (organism)">pests</a>. It is often used in connection to disease and illness, preventing the movement of those who may have been exposed to a <a href="/wiki/Infection" title="Infection">communicable disease</a>, yet do not have a confirmed <a href="/wiki/Medical_diagnosis" title="Medical diagnosis">medical diagnosis</a>. It is distinct from <a href="/wiki/Isolation_(health_care)" title="Isolation (health care)">medical isolation</a>, in which those confirmed to be infected with a communicable disease are isolated from the healthy population.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Coat_of_arms_of_Great_Britain_(1707%E2%80%931714).svg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="coat of arms" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_Security">Health Security</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Health security</b> is a concept that encompasses activities and measures across <a href="/wiki/Sovereign_state" title="Sovereign state">sovereign</a> boundaries that mitigates <a href="/wiki/Public_health" title="Public health">public health</a> incidents to ensure the health of populations.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is an evolving paradigm within the fields of <a href="/wiki/International_relations" title="International relations">international relations</a> and <a href="/wiki/Security_studies" title="Security studies">security studies</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Proponents of health security posit that all <a href="/wiki/State_(polity)" title="State (polity)">states</a> have a responsibility to protect the health and wellbeing of their populations.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Opponents suggest health security impacts <a href="/wiki/Civil_liberties" title="Civil liberties">civil liberties</a> and the equal distribution of resources.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

Their intrinsic value mainly concerns agricultural crops (<a href="/wiki/Crop_biodiversity" class="mw-redirect" title="Crop biodiversity">crop biodiversity</a>).
</p><p></p></div><div name="SCSP" term="SCSP" wikidataID="Q120025030" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SCSP" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: SCSP<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SCSP">SCSP</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>Special Competitive Studies Project</b> (SCSP) is a non-partisan U.S. <a href="/wiki/Think_tank" title="Think tank">think tank</a> and private foundation focused on technology and security. Founded by former Google CEO <a href="/wiki/Eric_Schmidt" title="Eric Schmidt">Eric Schmidt</a> in October 2021,<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> SCSP's stated mission is to "make recommendations to strengthen America&#8217;s long-term competitiveness as artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies are reshaping our national security, economy, and society." It seeks to ensure that "America is positioned and organized to win the techno-economic competition between now and 2030."<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p></p></div><div name="downy mildew" term="downy mildew" wikidataID="Q1394849" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downy_mildew" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: downy mildew<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downy_mildew">Downy mildew</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Downy mildew</b> refers to any of several types of <a href="/wiki/Oomycete" title="Oomycete">oomycete</a> microbes that are <a href="/wiki/Obligate_parasite" title="Obligate parasite">obligate parasites</a> of plants. Downy mildews exclusively belong to the <a href="/wiki/Peronosporaceae" title="Peronosporaceae">Peronosporaceae</a> family. In <a href="/wiki/Commerce" title="Commerce">commercial</a> <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a>, they are a particular problem for growers of <a href="/wiki/Cruciferae" class="mw-redirect" title="Cruciferae">crucifers</a>, <a href="/wiki/Grape" title="Grape">grapes</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vegetable" title="Vegetable">vegetables</a> that grow on vines. The prime example is <i><a href="/wiki/Peronospora_farinosa" title="Peronospora farinosa">Peronospora farinosa</a></i> featured in NCBI-Taxonomy<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and HYP3.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This pathogen does not produce survival structures in the northern states of the United States, and overwinters as live mildew colonies in Gulf Coast states. It progresses northward with <a href="/wiki/Cucurbitaceae" title="Cucurbitaceae">cucurbit</a> production each spring. Yield loss associated with downy mildew is most likely related to soft rots that occur after plant canopies collapse and sunburn occurs on fruit. Cucurbit downy mildew only affects leaves of cucurbit plants.
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Downy_and_Powdery_mildew_on_grape_leaf.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Downy_and_Powdery_mildew_on_grape_leaf.JPG/250px-Downy_and_Powdery_mildew_on_grape_leaf.JPG" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b8/Downy_and_Powdery_mildew_on_grape_leaf.JPG 1.5x" data-file-width="384" data-file-height="288"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="Andhra" term="Andhra" wikidataID="Q1159" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andhra" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Andhra<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andhra">Andhra</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Andhra Pradesh</b><sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India" title="States and union territories of India">state</a> on the <a href="/wiki/East_Coast_of_India" class="mw-redirect" title="East Coast of India">east coast</a> of southern <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>. It is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_area" title="List of states and union territories of India by area">seventh-largest state</a> and the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_and_union_territories_of_India_by_population" title="List of states and union territories of India by population">tenth-most populous</a> in the country. <a href="/wiki/Telugu_language" title="Telugu language">Telugu</a>, one of the <a href="/wiki/Classical_languages_of_India" title="Classical languages of India">classical languages of India</a>, is the most widely spoken language in the state, as well as its official language. <a href="/wiki/Amaravati" title="Amaravati">Amaravati</a> is the state capital, while the largest city is <a href="/wiki/Visakhapatnam" title="Visakhapatnam">Visakhapatnam</a>. <a href="/wiki/Amaravati" title="Amaravati">Amaravati</a> is a greenfield capital city developed near Vijayawada. Geographically  both Amaravati and Vijayawada can be seen as Twin cities. Andhra Pradesh shares borders with <a href="/wiki/Odisha" title="Odisha">Odisha</a> to the northeast, <a href="/wiki/Chhattisgarh" title="Chhattisgarh">Chhattisgarh</a> to the north, <a href="/wiki/Karnataka" title="Karnataka">Karnataka</a> to the west, <a href="/wiki/Tamil_Nadu" title="Tamil Nadu">Tamil Nadu</a> to the south, <a href="/wiki/Telangana" title="Telangana">Telangana</a> to northwest and the <a href="/wiki/Bay_of_Bengal" title="Bay of Bengal">Bay of Bengal</a> to the east. It has the <a href="/wiki/Coastline_of_Andhra_Pradesh" title="Coastline of Andhra Pradesh">longest coastline</a> in India (aerial distance between extreme ends) at about 1,000 kilometres (620&#160;mi).
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg" class="mw-file-description" title="Location of Andhra Pradesh in India"><img alt="The map of India showing Andhra Pradesh" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg/330px-India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="350" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg/500px-India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg/960px-India_locator_map_Andhra_Pradesh.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1486" data-file-height="1734"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="Co 17001" term="Co 17001" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=Co%2017001" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Co 17001<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=Co%2017001">Co 17001</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="pulses" term="pulses" wikidataID="Q145909" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulses" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: pulses<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulses">Pulses</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Legumes</b> are <a href="/wiki/Plants" class="mw-redirect" title="Plants">plants</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Pea" title="Pea">pea</a> family <a href="/wiki/Fabaceae" title="Fabaceae">Fabaceae</a> (or Leguminosae), or the fruit or seeds of such plants. When used as a dry grain for human consumption, the seeds are also called <b>pulses</b>. Legumes are grown agriculturally, primarily for human consumption, but also as livestock forage and <a href="/wiki/Silage" title="Silage">silage</a>, and as soil-enhancing <a href="/wiki/Green_manure" title="Green manure">green manure</a>. Legumes produce a botanically unique type of <a href="/wiki/Fruit" title="Fruit">fruit</a> &#8211; a <a href="/wiki/Simple_fruit" title="Simple fruit">simple</a> <a href="/wiki/Dry_fruits" title="Dry fruits">dry fruit</a> that develops from a simple <a href="/wiki/Carpel" class="mw-redirect" title="Carpel">carpel</a> and usually <a href="/wiki/Dehiscence_(botany)" title="Dehiscence (botany)">dehisces</a> (opens along a seam) on two sides.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Various_legumes.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Various_legumes.jpg/250px-Various_legumes.jpg" decoding="async" width="230" height="344" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Various_legumes.jpg/500px-Various_legumes.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="640" data-file-height="957"></a><figcaption>A selection of dried pulses and fresh legumes</figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="rice pests" term="rice pests" wikidataID="Q5090" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_pests" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: rice pests<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_pests">Rice pests</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Rice</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Cereal_grain" class="mw-redirect" title="Cereal grain">cereal grain</a> and in its <a href="/wiki/Domestication" title="Domestication">domesticated</a> form is the <a href="/wiki/Staple_food" title="Staple food">staple food</a> of over half of the <a href="/wiki/World%27s_population" class="mw-redirect" title="World's population">world's population</a>, particularly in <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a> and <a href="/wiki/Africa" title="Africa">Africa</a>. Rice is the seed of the grass species <i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_sativa" title="Oryza sativa">Oryza sativa</a></i> (Asian rice)&#8212;or, much less commonly, <i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_glaberrima" title="Oryza glaberrima">Oryza glaberrima</a></i> (African rice). Asian rice was domesticated in <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a> some 13,500 to 8,200 years ago; African rice was domesticated in Africa about 3,000 years ago. Rice has become commonplace in many cultures worldwide; in 2023, 800 million tons were produced, placing it third after <a href="/wiki/Sugarcane" title="Sugarcane">sugarcane</a> and <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">maize</a>. Only some 8% of rice is traded internationally. China, India, and Indonesia are the largest consumers of rice. A substantial amount of the rice produced in developing nations is lost after harvest through factors such as poor transport and storage. Rice yields can be reduced by pests including <a href="/wiki/Insect" title="Insect">insects</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rodent" title="Rodent">rodents</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Bird" title="Bird">birds</a>, as well as by <a href="/wiki/Weed" title="Weed">weeds</a>, and by <a href="/wiki/List_of_rice_diseases" title="List of rice diseases">diseases</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Rice_blast" class="mw-redirect" title="Rice blast">rice blast</a>. Traditional <a href="/wiki/Rice_polyculture" title="Rice polyculture">rice polycultures</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Rice-duck_farming" title="Rice-duck farming">rice-duck farming</a>, and modern <a href="/wiki/Integrated_pest_management" title="Integrated pest management">integrated pest management</a> seek to control damage from pests in a <a href="/wiki/Sustainable_agriculture" title="Sustainable agriculture">sustainable</a> way.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg/500px-20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg" decoding="async" width="340" height="191" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg/960px-20201102.Hengnan.Hybrid_rice_Sanyou-1.6.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="720"></a><figcaption>Rice plant (<i><a href="/wiki/Oryza_sativa" title="Oryza sativa">Oryza sativa</a></i>) with branched <a href="/wiki/Panicle" title="Panicle">panicles</a> containing many grains on each stem</figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="cucumber" term="cucumber" wikidataID="Q23425" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cucumber" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: cucumber<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cucumber">Cucumber</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>cucumber</b> (<i><b>Cucumis sativus</b></i>) is a widely-cultivated <a href="/wiki/Vine#Horticultural_climbing_plants" title="Vine">creeping vine</a> plant in the family <a href="/wiki/Cucurbitaceae" title="Cucurbitaceae">Cucurbitaceae</a> that bears cylindrical to spherical <a href="/wiki/Fruit" title="Fruit">fruits</a>, which are used as <a href="/wiki/Culinary_vegetable" class="mw-redirect" title="Culinary vegetable">culinary vegetables</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Encyclopedia_Britannica_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Considered an annual plant,<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> there are three main types of cucumber&#8212;slicing, <a href="/wiki/Pickled_cucumber" title="Pickled cucumber">pickling</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Seedless_fruit" title="Seedless fruit">seedless</a>&#8212;within which several <a href="/wiki/Cultivar" title="Cultivar">cultivars</a> have been created. The cucumber originates in <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a> extending from <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nepal" title="Nepal">Nepal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh" title="Bangladesh">Bangladesh</a>, <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a> (<a href="/wiki/Yunnan" title="Yunnan">Yunnan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Guizhou" title="Guizhou">Guizhou</a>, <a href="/wiki/Guangxi" title="Guangxi">Guangxi</a>), and <a href="/wiki/Northern_Thailand" title="Northern Thailand">Northern Thailand</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Plant_Breeding_Reviews_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Plant_Breeding_Reviews-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-powo_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-powo-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-tandfonline.com_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tandfonline.com-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> but now grows on most <a href="/wiki/Continent" title="Continent">continents</a>, and many different types of cucumber are grown commercially and traded on the <a href="/wiki/Global_market" class="mw-redirect" title="Global market">global market</a>. In <a href="/wiki/North_America" title="North America">North America</a>, the term <i><a href="/wiki/Wild_cucumber" title="Wild cucumber">wild cucumber</a></i> refers to plants in the <a href="/wiki/Genus" title="Genus">genera</a> <i><a href="/wiki/Echinocystis" title="Echinocystis">Echinocystis</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Marah_(plant)" title="Marah (plant)">Marah</a></i>, though the two are not closely related.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Concombre_Fournier.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Concombre_Fournier.jpg/250px-Concombre_Fournier.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="310" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Concombre_Fournier.jpg/500px-Concombre_Fournier.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="686" data-file-height="850"></a><figcaption>Concombre Fournier in "Les plantes potag&#232;res" Vilmorin 1925</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="commercialization" term="commercialization" wikidataID="Q5152592" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercialization" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: commercialization<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercialization">Commercialization</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Commercialisation</b> or <b>commercialization </b>is the <a href="/wiki/Business_process" title="Business process">process</a> of introducing a new <a href="/wiki/Product_(business)" title="Product (business)">product</a> or <a href="/wiki/Methods_of_production" class="mw-redirect" title="Methods of production">production method</a> into <a href="/wiki/Commerce" title="Commerce">commerce</a>&#8212;making it available on the <a href="/wiki/Market_(economics)" title="Market (economics)">market</a>. The term often <a href="/wiki/Connotation" title="Connotation">connotes</a> especially entry into the <a href="/wiki/Mass_market" title="Mass market">mass market</a> (as opposed to entry into earlier <a href="/wiki/Niche_market" title="Niche market">niche markets</a>), but it also includes a move from the <a href="/wiki/Laboratory" title="Laboratory">laboratory</a> into (even limited) commerce. Many technologies begin in a <a href="/wiki/Research_and_development" title="Research and development">research and development</a> laboratory or in an inventor's workshop and may not be practical for commercial use in their infancy (as <a href="/wiki/Prototype" title="Prototype">prototypes</a>). The "development" segment of the "<a href="/wiki/Research_and_development" title="Research and development">research and development</a>" spectrum requires time and money as <a href="/wiki/Industrial_engineering" title="Industrial engineering">systems are engineered</a> with a view to making the product or method a paying <a href="/wiki/Commerce" title="Commerce">commercial</a> proposition. 
</p><p></p></div><div name="mealybug" term="mealybug" wikidataID="Q143569" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mealybug" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: mealybug<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mealybug">Mealybug</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Mealybugs</b> are insects in the <a href="/wiki/Family_(biology)" title="Family (biology)">family</a> <b>Pseudococcidae</b>, unarmored <a href="/wiki/Scale_insect" title="Scale insect">scale insects</a> found in moist, warm habitats. Of the more than 2,000 described species, many are considered <a href="/wiki/Pest_(animal)" class="mw-redirect" title="Pest (animal)">pests</a> as they feed on plant juices of <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse" title="Greenhouse">greenhouse</a> plants, house plants and subtropical trees and also act as a <a href="/wiki/Vector_(epidemiology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Vector (epidemiology)">vector</a> for several plant diseases. Some ants live in symbiotic <a href="/wiki/Ant#Relationships_with_other_organisms" title="Ant">relationships</a> with them, protecting them from predators and feeding off the <a href="/wiki/Honeydew_(secretion)" title="Honeydew (secretion)">honeydew</a> which they excrete.
</p>

Its large <a href="/wiki/Taproot" title="Taproot">taproot</a> is commonly used as a <a href="/wiki/Root_vegetable" title="Root vegetable">root vegetable</a>, although the entire plant is edible and its <a href="/wiki/Leaf" title="Leaf">leaves</a> are sometimes used as a <a href="/wiki/Leaf_vegetable" title="Leaf vegetable">leaf vegetable</a>. Originally domesticated in <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a>, radishes are now grown and consumed globally. The radish is sometimes considered to form a <a href="/wiki/Species_complex" title="Species complex">species complex</a> with the <a href="/wiki/Wild_radish" class="mw-redirect" title="Wild radish">wild radish</a> and instead treated as the subspecies <i>Raphanus raphanistrum</i> subsp. <i>sativus</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-u427_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-u427-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

</p><p></p></div><div name="Uzbekistan" term="Uzbekistan" wikidataID="Q265" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbekistan" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Uzbekistan<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbekistan">Uzbekistan</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Uzbekistan</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> officially the <b>Republic of Uzbekistan</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>b<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/Landlocked_country#Doubly_landlocked" title="Landlocked country">doubly landlocked</a> country located in <a href="/wiki/Central_Asia" title="Central Asia">Central Asia</a>. It is surrounded by five countries: <a href="/wiki/Kazakhstan" title="Kazakhstan">Kazakhstan</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Kazakhstan%E2%80%93Uzbekistan_border" title="Kazakhstan&#8211;Uzbekistan border">north</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kyrgyzstan" title="Kyrgyzstan">Kyrgyzstan</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Kyrgyzstan%E2%80%93Uzbekistan_border" title="Kyrgyzstan&#8211;Uzbekistan border">northeast</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tajikistan" title="Tajikistan">Tajikistan</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Tajikistan%E2%80%93Uzbekistan_border" title="Tajikistan&#8211;Uzbekistan border">southeast</a>, <a href="/wiki/Afghanistan" title="Afghanistan">Afghanistan</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Afghanistan%E2%80%93Uzbekistan_border" title="Afghanistan&#8211;Uzbekistan border">south</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Turkmenistan" title="Turkmenistan">Turkmenistan</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Turkmenistan%E2%80%93Uzbekistan_border" title="Turkmenistan&#8211;Uzbekistan border">southwest</a>, making it one of only two doubly landlocked countries on Earth, the other being <a href="/wiki/Liechtenstein" title="Liechtenstein">Liechtenstein</a>. The country has a population of more than 38.2 million, making it the most populous country in Central Asia. Uzbekistan is a member of the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_Turkic_States" title="Organization of Turkic States">Organization of Turkic States</a>. <a href="/wiki/Uzbek_language" title="Uzbek language">Uzbek</a>, spoken by the <a href="/wiki/Uzbeks" title="Uzbeks">Uzbek people</a>, is the official language and is spoken by the majority of its inhabitants, while <a href="/wiki/Russian_language" title="Russian language">Russian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tajik_language" title="Tajik language">Tajik</a> are significant minority languages. <a href="/wiki/Islam" title="Islam">Islam</a> is the predominant religion, and most Uzbeks are <a href="/wiki/Sunni_Islam" title="Sunni Islam">Sunni Muslims</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Kaunakes_Bactria_Louvre_AO31917.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Kaunakes_Bactria_Louvre_AO31917.jpg/250px-Kaunakes_Bactria_Louvre_AO31917.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="211" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Kaunakes_Bactria_Louvre_AO31917.jpg/330px-Kaunakes_Bactria_Louvre_AO31917.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Kaunakes_Bactria_Louvre_AO31917.jpg/500px-Kaunakes_Bactria_Louvre_AO31917.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1170" data-file-height="1300"></a><figcaption>Female statuette wearing the <a href="/wiki/Kaunakes" title="Kaunakes">kaunakes</a>. Landraces are distinct from <a href="/wiki/Cultivars" class="mw-redirect" title="Cultivars">cultivars</a> and from standard <a href="/wiki/Breed" title="Breed">breeds</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Journal.pbio.2006352.g002_cropped.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Journal.pbio.2006352.g002_cropped.png/330px-Journal.pbio.2006352.g002_cropped.png" decoding="async" width="280" height="209" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Journal.pbio.2006352.g002_cropped.png/500px-Journal.pbio.2006352.g002_cropped.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/44/Journal.pbio.2006352.g002_cropped.png 2x" data-file-width="694" data-file-height="519"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Aerial_root" title="Aerial root">Aerial roots</a> of a <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">maize</a> landrace, <a href="/wiki/Sierra_Mixe_corn" title="Sierra Mixe corn">Sierra Mixe corn</a>, grown in nitrogen-depleted soils in the <a href="/wiki/Sierra_Mixe" title="Sierra Mixe">Sierra Mixe</a>, known for aerial roots with a <a href="/wiki/Bacteria" title="Bacteria">bacterial</a> gel that contributes substantially to the plant's nitrogen supply<sup id="cite_ref-nitrogen-maize_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nitrogen-maize-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>

It was described by <a href="/wiki/Francis_Walker_(entomologist)" title="Francis Walker (entomologist)">Francis Walker</a> in 1863. It is found in <a href="/wiki/Afghanistan" title="Afghanistan">Afghanistan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nepal" title="Nepal">Nepal</a>, north-eastern <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sri_Lanka" title="Sri Lanka">Sri Lanka</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh" title="Bangladesh">Bangladesh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Myanmar" title="Myanmar">Myanmar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vietnam" title="Vietnam">Vietnam</a>, <a href="/wiki/Thailand" title="Thailand">Thailand</a>, <a href="/wiki/Malaysia" title="Malaysia">Malaysia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Singapore" title="Singapore">Singapore</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sumatra" title="Sumatra">Sumatra</a>, <a href="/wiki/Java" title="Java">Java</a>, <a href="/wiki/Borneo" title="Borneo">Borneo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sumba" title="Sumba">Sumba</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sulawesi" title="Sulawesi">Sulawesi</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Philippines" title="Philippines">Philippines</a>, <a href="/wiki/Taiwan" title="Taiwan">Taiwan</a>, <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a> and <a href="/wiki/Japan" title="Japan">Japan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

Cryopreservation is an effective way to transport biological samples over long distances, store samples for prolonged periods of time, and create a bank of samples for users. 
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg/330px-Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg" decoding="async" width="280" height="420" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg/500px-Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/95/Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg 2x" data-file-width="864" data-file-height="1296"></a><figcaption>Cryogenically preserved samples being removed from a <a href="/wiki/Cryogenic_storage_dewar" title="Cryogenic storage dewar">dewar</a> of <a href="/wiki/Liquid_nitrogen" title="Liquid nitrogen">liquid nitrogen</a></figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="leaf sheath" term="leaf sheath" wikidataID="Q33971" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf_sheath" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: leaf sheath<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf_sheath">Leaf sheath</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>leaf</b> (<abbr title="plural">pl.</abbr>: <b>leaves</b>) is a principal appendage of the <a href="/wiki/Plant_stem" title="Plant stem">stem</a> of a <a href="/wiki/Vascular_plant" title="Vascular plant">vascular plant</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEsau2006_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEsau2006-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> usually borne laterally above ground and specialized for <a href="/wiki/Photosynthesis" title="Photosynthesis">photosynthesis</a>. Leaves are collectively called <b>foliage</b>, as in "autumn foliage",<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHaupt1953_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaupt1953-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMauseth2009_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMauseth2009-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> while the leaves, stem, <a href="/wiki/Flower" title="Flower">flower</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Fruit" title="Fruit">fruit</a> collectively form the <a href="/wiki/Shoot_(botany)" title="Shoot (botany)">shoot</a> system.<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In most leaves, the primary <a href="/wiki/Photosynthesis" title="Photosynthesis">photosynthetic</a> <a href="/wiki/Tissue_(biology)" title="Tissue (biology)">tissue</a> is the <a href="/wiki/Palisade_mesophyll" class="mw-redirect" title="Palisade mesophyll">palisade mesophyll</a> and is located on the upper side of the blade or lamina of the leaf,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEsau2006_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEsau2006-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> but in some species, including the mature foliage of <i><a href="/wiki/Eucalyptus" title="Eucalyptus">Eucalyptus</a></i>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEJames_et_al1999_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJames_et_al1999-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> palisade mesophyll is present on both sides and the leaves are said to be isobilateral. The leaf is an integral part of the stem system, and most leaves are flattened and have distinct upper (<a href="/wiki/Glossary_of_botanical_terms#adaxial" title="Glossary of botanical terms">adaxial</a>) and lower (<a href="/wiki/Glossary_of_botanical_terms#abaxial" title="Glossary of botanical terms">abaxial</a>) surfaces that differ in color, <a href="/wiki/Trichome" title="Trichome">hairiness</a>, the number of <a href="/wiki/Stomata" class="mw-redirect" title="Stomata">stomata</a> (pores that intake and output gases), the amount and structure of <a href="/wiki/Epicuticular_wax" title="Epicuticular wax">epicuticular wax</a>, and other features. Leaves are mostly green in color due to the presence of a compound called <a href="/wiki/Chlorophyll" title="Chlorophyll">chlorophyll</a> which is essential for photosynthesis as it absorbs light energy from the <a href="/wiki/Sun" title="Sun">Sun</a>. A leaf with lighter-colored or white patches or edges is called a <a href="/wiki/Variegation" title="Variegation">variegated leaf</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Leaf_Varieties_(15_sp).png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Leaf_Varieties_%2815_sp%29.png/500px-Leaf_Varieties_%2815_sp%29.png" decoding="async" width="400" height="401" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Leaf_Varieties_%2815_sp%29.png/960px-Leaf_Varieties_%2815_sp%29.png 1.5x" data-file-width="8160" data-file-height="8189"></a><figcaption>The diversity of leaves, including <i><a href="/wiki/Bismarckia" title="Bismarckia">Bismarckia</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Araucaria" title="Araucaria">Araucaria</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Euphorbia" title="Euphorbia">Euphorbia</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Nymphaea" title="Nymphaea">Nymphaea</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Colocasia" title="Colocasia">Colocasia</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Hildegardia_(plant)" title="Hildegardia (plant)"><i>Hildegardia</i></a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Picea" class="mw-redirect" title="Picea">Picea</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Melocactus" title="Melocactus">Melocactus</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Cycas" title="Cycas">Cycas</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Acer_(genus)" class="mw-redirect" title="Acer (genus)"><i>Acer</i></a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Yucca" title="Yucca">Yucca</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Ferocactus" title="Ferocactus">Ferocactus</a></i>, and <i><a href="/wiki/Ocimum" title="Ocimum">Ocimum</a></i>.</figcaption></figure>

Rust consists of <a href="/wiki/Hydrous_ferric_oxides" class="mw-redirect" title="Hydrous ferric oxides">hydrous iron(III) oxides</a> (Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>&#183;nH<sub>2</sub>O) and <a href="/wiki/Iron(III)_oxide-hydroxide" title="Iron(III) oxide-hydroxide">iron(III) oxide-hydroxide</a> (FeO(OH), Fe(OH)<sub>3</sub>), and is typically associated with the <a href="/wiki/Corrosion" title="Corrosion">corrosion</a> of <a href="/wiki/Refined_iron" class="mw-redirect" title="Refined iron">refined iron</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Rust_on_iron.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Rust_on_iron.jpg/500px-Rust_on_iron.jpg" decoding="async" width="340" height="227" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Rust_on_iron.jpg/960px-Rust_on_iron.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="5616" data-file-height="3744"></a><figcaption>Colors and porous surface texture of rust</figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="drip irrigation" term="drip irrigation" wikidataID="Q746694" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drip_irrigation" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: drip irrigation<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drip_irrigation">Drip irrigation</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

<b>Drip irrigation</b> or <b>trickle irrigation</b> is a type of <a href="/wiki/Micro-irrigation" title="Micro-irrigation">micro-irrigation</a> system that has the potential to save water and nutrients by allowing water to drip slowly to the roots of plants, either from above the soil surface or buried below the surface.  The goal is to place water directly into the <a href="/wiki/Rhizosphere" title="Rhizosphere">root zone</a> and minimize evaporation.  Drip irrigation systems distribute water through a network of <a href="/wiki/Valve" title="Valve">valves</a>, pipes, tubing, and emitters. Depending on how well designed, installed, maintained, and operated it is, a drip irrigation system can be more efficient than other types of irrigation systems, such as <a href="/wiki/Surface_irrigation" title="Surface irrigation">surface irrigation</a> or sprinkler irrigation.
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Button_dripper.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Button_dripper.JPG/330px-Button_dripper.JPG" decoding="async" width="261" height="196" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Button_dripper.JPG/500px-Button_dripper.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Button_dripper.JPG/960px-Button_dripper.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1536"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Netafim" title="Netafim">Israeli Netafim</a>, drip irrigation</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Agricultural University" term="Agricultural University" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=Agricultural%20University" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Agricultural University<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=Agricultural%20University">Agricultural University</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Genetics" term="Genetics" wikidataID="Q7162" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Genetics<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics">Genetics</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Genetics</b> is the study of <a href="/wiki/Gene" title="Gene">genes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Genetic_variation" title="Genetic variation">genetic variation</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Heredity" title="Heredity">heredity</a> in <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organisms</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-griffiths2000sect60_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-griffiths2000sect60-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Hartl_and_Jones_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hartl_and_Jones-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is an important branch in <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a> because heredity is vital to organisms' <a href="/wiki/Evolution" title="Evolution">evolution</a>. <a href="/wiki/Gregor_Mendel" title="Gregor Mendel">Gregor Mendel</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Moravia" title="Moravia">Moravian</a> <a href="/wiki/Augustinians" title="Augustinians">Augustinian</a> friar working in the 19th century in <a href="/wiki/Brno" title="Brno">Brno</a>, was the first to study genetics scientifically. Mendel studied "trait inheritance", patterns in the way traits are handed down from parents to offspring over time. He observed that organisms (pea plants) inherit traits by way of discrete "units of inheritance". This term, still used today, is a somewhat ambiguous definition of what is referred to as a gene.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Festetics_Imre-Oelenhainz.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Festetics_Imre-Oelenhainz.jpg/250px-Festetics_Imre-Oelenhainz.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="356" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Festetics_Imre-Oelenhainz.jpg/500px-Festetics_Imre-Oelenhainz.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1056" data-file-height="1504"></a><figcaption>Portrait of <a href="/wiki/Imre_Festetics" title="Imre Festetics">Imre Festetics</a>, the first <a href="/wiki/Geneticist" title="Geneticist">geneticist</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ethology" title="Ethology">ethologist</a>. His concepts of <a href="/wiki/Selection_(biology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Selection (biology)">selection</a> and <a href="/wiki/Evolution" title="Evolution">evolution</a> were later formulated in <a href="/wiki/Natural_selection" title="Natural selection">Charles Darwin's theory of evolution</a>.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="composting" term="composting" wikidataID="Q212254" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composting" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: composting<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composting">Composting</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Compost</b> is a mixture of ingredients used as plant fertilizer and to improve <a href="/wiki/Soil" title="Soil">soil</a>'s physical, chemical, and biological properties. It is commonly prepared by <a href="/wiki/Decomposition" title="Decomposition">decomposing</a> plant and food waste, recycling organic materials, and manure. The resulting mixture is rich in plant nutrients and <a href="/wiki/Beneficial_organism" title="Beneficial organism">beneficial organisms</a>, such as bacteria, protozoa, nematodes, and fungi. Compost improves soil fertility in <a href="/wiki/Garden" title="Garden">gardens</a>, <a href="/wiki/Landscaping" title="Landscaping">landscaping</a>, <a href="/wiki/Horticulture" title="Horticulture">horticulture</a>, <a href="/wiki/Urban_agriculture" title="Urban agriculture">urban agriculture</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Organic_farming" title="Organic farming">organic farming</a>, reducing dependency on commercial chemical fertilizers.<sup id="cite_ref-:4_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The benefits of compost include providing nutrients to crops as <a href="/wiki/Fertilizer" title="Fertilizer">fertilizer</a>, acting as a <a href="/wiki/Soil_conditioner" title="Soil conditioner">soil conditioner</a>, increasing the <a href="/wiki/Humus" title="Humus">humus</a> or <a href="/wiki/Humic_acids" class="mw-redirect" title="Humic acids">humic acid</a> contents of the soil, and introducing beneficial microbes that help to suppress pathogens in the soil and reduce soil-borne diseases.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Compost_site_germany.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Compost_site_germany.JPG/330px-Compost_site_germany.JPG" decoding="async" width="330" height="248" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Compost_site_germany.JPG/500px-Compost_site_germany.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Compost_site_germany.JPG/960px-Compost_site_germany.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2592" data-file-height="1944"></a><figcaption>Community-level composting in a rural area in <a href="/wiki/Germany" title="Germany">Germany</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="horticultural crops" term="horticultural crops" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=horticultural%20crops" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: horticultural crops<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=horticultural%20crops">horticultural crops</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

</p><div title="figure"><a href="https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q27286608#P2566" title="Edit this at Wikidata"><img alt="Edit this at Wikidata" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/8/8a/OOjs_UI_icon_edit-ltr-progressive.svg/20px-OOjs_UI_icon_edit-ltr-progressive.svg.png" decoding="async" width="10" height="10" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="20" data-file-height="20"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="pumpkin" term="pumpkin" wikidataID="Q165308" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pumpkin" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: pumpkin<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pumpkin">Pumpkin</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>pumpkin</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Cultivar" title="Cultivar">cultivated</a> <a href="/wiki/Winter_squash" title="Winter squash">winter squash</a> in the genus <i><a href="/wiki/Cucurbita" title="Cucurbita">Cucurbita</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-Ferriol_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ferriol-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-USARS_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-USARS-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The term is most commonly applied to round, orange-colored squash varieties, but does not possess a scientific definition. It may be used in reference to many different squashes of varied appearance and belonging to multiple species in the <i>Cucurbita</i> genus.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:FrenchMarketPumpkinsB.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/FrenchMarketPumpkinsB.jpg/500px-FrenchMarketPumpkinsB.jpg" decoding="async" width="350" height="263" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/FrenchMarketPumpkinsB.jpg/960px-FrenchMarketPumpkinsB.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2816" data-file-height="2112"></a><figcaption>A pile of pumpkins at the <a href="/wiki/French_Market" title="French Market">French Market</a> in New Orleans, Louisiana</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="PFMS" term="PFMS" wikidataID="Q5061665" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFMS" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: PFMS<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFMS">PFMS</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>Central Plan Scheme Monitoring System</b> (<b>CPSMS</b>) (now called <b>Public Finance Management System</b> or <b>PFMS</b>)<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/Government_of_India" title="Government of India">Government of India</a> public financial management reforms initiative which monitors programs in the social sector and tracks funds disbursed.  Given the large number of programs on which the money is spent, the CPSMS is an initiative by the Indian Central Government to ensure that the money is spent according to its intended purpose, and provide an accounting of same.
</p>
<p></p></div><div name="Brazil" term="Brazil" wikidataID="Q155" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Brazil<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil">Brazil</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Brazil</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>c<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> officially the <b>Federative Republic of Brazil</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>d<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is the largest country in <a href="/wiki/South_America" title="South America">South America</a>. It is also the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area" title="List of countries and dependencies by area">fifth-largest country by area</a> and the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population" title="List of countries and dependencies by population">seventh-largest by population</a>, with over 213 million people. The country is a <a href="/wiki/Federation" title="Federation">federation</a> composed of 26 <a href="/wiki/Federative_units_of_Brazil" title="Federative units of Brazil">states</a> and a <a href="/wiki/Federal_District_(Brazil)" title="Federal District (Brazil)">Federal District</a>, which hosts the capital, <a href="/wiki/Bras%C3%ADlia" title="Bras&#237;lia">Bras&#237;lia</a>. Its <a href="/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Brazil_by_population" title="List of municipalities in Brazil by population">most populous city</a> is <a href="/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo" title="S&#227;o Paulo">S&#227;o Paulo</a>, followed by <a href="/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro" title="Rio de Janeiro">Rio de Janeiro</a>. Brazil has the most <a href="/wiki/Community_of_Portuguese_Language_Countries" title="Community of Portuguese Language Countries">Portuguese speakers</a> in the world and is the only country in the <a href="/wiki/Americas" title="Americas">Americas</a> where <a href="/wiki/Portuguese_language" title="Portuguese language">Portuguese</a> is an <a href="/wiki/Portuguese-speaking_world" title="Portuguese-speaking world">official language</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Philander2012_21-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Philander2012-21"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-CrocittiVallance2011_22-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CrocittiVallance2011-22"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

There are several species of grain called rice.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Oryza_sativa" title="Oryza sativa">Asian rice</a> (<i>Oryza sativa)</i> is most widely known and most widely grown, with two major subspecies (<i>indica</i> and <i>japonica</i>) and over 40,000 varieties.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Also included in this list are varieties of <a href="/wiki/Oryza_glaberrima" title="Oryza glaberrima">African rice</a> (<i>Oryza glaberrima</i>) and <a href="/wiki/Wild_rice" title="Wild rice">wild rice</a> (genus <i>Zizania</i>).
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Rice_grains_(IRRI).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Rice_grains_%28IRRI%29.jpg/250px-Rice_grains_%28IRRI%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/ba/Rice_grains_%28IRRI%29.jpg/500px-Rice_grains_%28IRRI%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3600" data-file-height="2400"></a><figcaption>Rice can come in many shapes, colours and sizes.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Africa" term="Africa" wikidataID="Q15" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Africa<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa">Africa</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Africa</b> is the world's second-largest and second-most populous <a href="/wiki/Continent" title="Continent">continent</a> after <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a>. At about 30.3&#160;million km<sup>2</sup> (11.7&#160;million square&#160;miles) including adjacent islands, it covers around 20% of <a href="/wiki/Earth" title="Earth">Earth</a>'s land area and 6% of its total surface area.<sup id="cite_ref-Sayre_9-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sayre-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> With nearly 1.4 billion people as of 2021, it accounts for about <span data-sort-value="7001176207413858337&#9824;" style="display:none"></span>18% of the world's <a href="/wiki/Human_population" class="mw-redirect" title="Human population">human population</a>. <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_Africa" title="Demographics of Africa">Africa's population</a> is the youngest among all the continents;<sup id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-10"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Median" title="Median">median</a> age in 2012 was 19.7, when the worldwide median age was 30.4.<sup id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Based on 2024 projections, Africa's population will exceed 3.8 billion people by 2100.<sup id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Africa is the least wealthy inhabited continent <a href="/wiki/Per_capita" title="Per capita">per capita</a> and second-least wealthy by total wealth, ahead of <a href="/wiki/Oceania" title="Oceania">Oceania</a>. Scholars have attributed this to different factors including <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Africa" title="Geography of Africa">geography</a>, <a href="/wiki/Climate_of_Africa" title="Climate of Africa">climate</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Africa_Slow_14-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Africa_Slow-14"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Corruption" title="Corruption">corruption</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Africa_Slow_14-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Africa_Slow-14"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Scramble_for_Africa" title="Scramble for Africa">colonialism</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Cold_War" title="Cold War">Cold War</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Neocolonialism" title="Neocolonialism">neocolonialism</a>. Despite this low concentration of wealth, recent economic expansion and a large and young population make Africa an important economic market in the broader global context, and Africa has a large quantity of <a href="/wiki/Natural_resources_of_Africa" title="Natural resources of Africa">natural resources</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ancient_Egypt_map-en.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Ancient_Egypt_map-en.svg/250px-Ancient_Egypt_map-en.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="510" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Ancient_Egypt_map-en.svg/500px-Ancient_Egypt_map-en.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="1577" data-file-height="3219"></a><figcaption>Map of <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Egypt" title="Ancient Egypt">Ancient Egypt</a>, showing its major cities and sites, <abbr title="circa">c.</abbr><span style="white-space:nowrap;">&#8201;3150 BC to 30 BC</span></figcaption></figure>

Plant genomes can be engineered by physical methods or by use of <i><a href="/wiki/Agrobacterium" title="Agrobacterium">Agrobacterium</a></i> for the delivery of sequences hosted in <a href="/wiki/Transfer_DNA_binary_system" title="Transfer DNA binary system">T-DNA binary vectors</a>. Many plant cells are <a href="/wiki/Pluripotent" class="mw-redirect" title="Pluripotent">pluripotent</a>, meaning that a single cell from a mature plant can be harvested and then under the right conditions form a new plant. This ability is most often taken advantage by genetic engineers through selecting cells that can successfully be transformed into an adult plant which can then be grown into multiple new plants containing transgene in every cell through a process known as <a href="/wiki/Tissue_culture" title="Tissue culture">tissue culture</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:9_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:9-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Blue_Rose_APPLAUSE.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Blue_Rose_APPLAUSE.jpg/250px-Blue_Rose_APPLAUSE.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Blue_Rose_APPLAUSE.jpg/500px-Blue_Rose_APPLAUSE.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="3000"></a><figcaption>Suntory "blue" rose</figcaption></figure> </div><p></p></div><div name="Farm Income" term="Farm Income" wikidataID="Q5435555" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farm_income" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Farm Income<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farm_income">Farm income</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Farm income</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Community_indicators" title="Community indicators">statistical indicator</a> of the income from <a href="/wiki/Farming" class="mw-redirect" title="Farming">farming</a> for a particular country per year or some other period. This statistic is used by governments to determine agricultural policy and performance of the agricultural sector by financial markets.

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="direct seeded rice" term="direct seeded rice" wikidataID="Q119163392" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_seeded_rice" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: direct seeded rice<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_seeded_rice">Direct seeded rice</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><br>
<b>Direct seeded rice (DSR)</b><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a practice of <a href="/wiki/Sowing" title="Sowing">sowing</a> <a href="/wiki/Paddy_field" title="Paddy field">paddy</a> which involves planting <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a> seeds directly into the field, instead of the traditional method of growing <a href="/wiki/Seedling" title="Seedling">seedlings</a> in <a href="/wiki/Plant_nursery" title="Plant nursery">nurseries</a> and then transplanting them into the fields. This method significantly reduces the demand for labor, one of the major costs associated with rice farming. By eliminating the need for <a href="/wiki/Transplanting" title="Transplanting">transplanting</a>, farmers can cut down on labor costs and effectively manage the workforce during peak periods. It also provides flexibility in timing the planting, helping farmers to adapt to changing climate conditions. Moreover, DSR offers water efficiency. Traditional rice farming involves flooding fields, which is water-intensive and often unsustainable. Direct seeding of rice, on the other hand, requires less water during the establishment period, making it an attractive solution in regions experiencing <a href="/wiki/Water_scarcity" title="Water scarcity">water scarcity</a>. Reduced water usage in DSR systems can help lower <a href="/wiki/Methane_emissions" title="Methane emissions">methane emissions</a>, a potent <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_gas" title="Greenhouse gas">greenhouse gas</a> significantly produced in flooded rice paddies.<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Direct_Seeder_for_Rice_(DSR).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/Direct_Seeder_for_Rice_%28DSR%29.jpg/250px-Direct_Seeder_for_Rice_%28DSR%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="152" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/Direct_Seeder_for_Rice_%28DSR%29.jpg/500px-Direct_Seeder_for_Rice_%28DSR%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1200" data-file-height="729"></a><figcaption>Direct Seeder for Rice<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>

It includes five or species of herbs and subshrubs native to the tropical and subtropical Americas, ranging from northern <a href="/wiki/Mexico" title="Mexico">Mexico</a> to northwestern Argentina. Typical habitat is seasonally-dry tropical forest and thicket, often at forest margins, in scrub vegetation, and in open grassy areas.<sup id="cite_ref-powo_2-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-powo-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Plants in the genus grow from large, often edible <a href="/wiki/Taproot" title="Taproot">taproots</a>.
</p>

It is consumed as a beverage in many places, especially where sugarcane is commercially grown, such as <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Asia" title="Southeast Asia">Southeast Asia</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Indian_subcontinent" title="Indian subcontinent">Indian subcontinent</a>, <a href="/wiki/North_Africa" title="North Africa">North Africa</a>, mainly <a href="/wiki/Egypt" title="Egypt">Egypt</a>, and also in <a href="/wiki/South_America" title="South America">South America</a>, especially <a href="/wiki/Brazil" title="Brazil">Brazil</a>. 
Sugarcane juice is obtained by crushing peeled sugarcane in a mill and is one of the main precursors of <a href="/wiki/Rum" title="Rum">rum</a>.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Sugarcanejuice.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/Sugarcanejuice.jpg/250px-Sugarcanejuice.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/63/Sugarcanejuice.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="500" data-file-height="375"></a><figcaption>Sugarcane juice</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="pest management" term="pest management" wikidataID="Q2306047" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pest_management" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: pest management<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pest_management">Pest management</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Pest control</b> is the regulation or management of a <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> defined as a <a href="/wiki/Pest_(organism)" title="Pest (organism)">pest</a>; such as any animal, plant or fungus that impacts adversely on human activities or environment.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The human response depends on the importance of the damage done and will range from tolerance, through deterrence and management, to attempts to completely eradicate the pest. Pest control measures may be performed as part of an <a href="/wiki/Integrated_pest_management" title="Integrated pest management">integrated pest management</a> strategy.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Crop_Duster.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Crop_Duster.jpg/500px-Crop_Duster.jpg" decoding="async" width="340" height="432" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Crop_Duster.jpg/960px-Crop_Duster.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1739" data-file-height="2212"></a><figcaption>An <a href="/wiki/Agricultural_aircraft" title="Agricultural aircraft">agricultural aircraft</a> applies low-insecticide bait against <a href="/wiki/Western_corn_rootworm" title="Western corn rootworm">western corn rootworm</a>.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="South Asia" term="South Asia" wikidataID="Q771405" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asia" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: South Asia<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asia">South Asia</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>South Asia</b> is the southern <a href="/wiki/Subregion#Asia" title="Subregion">subregion</a> of <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a> that is defined in both geographical and <a href="/wiki/Ethnicity" title="Ethnicity">ethnic</a>-<a href="/wiki/Culture" title="Culture">cultural</a> terms. South Asia, with a population of 2.04 billion, contains a quarter (25%) of the world's population. As commonly conceptualised, the modern <a href="/wiki/State_(polity)" title="State (polity)">states</a> of South Asia include <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh" title="Bangladesh">Bangladesh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bhutan" title="Bhutan">Bhutan</a>, <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Maldives" title="Maldives">Maldives</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nepal" title="Nepal">Nepal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pakistan" title="Pakistan">Pakistan</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Sri_Lanka" title="Sri Lanka">Sri Lanka</a>, with <a href="/wiki/Afghanistan" title="Afghanistan">Afghanistan</a> also often included, which may otherwise be classified as part of <a href="/wiki/Central_Asia" title="Central Asia">Central Asia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTESaez201258_7-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTESaez201258-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> South Asia borders <a href="/wiki/East_Asia" title="East Asia">East Asia</a> to the northeast, Central Asia to the northwest, <a href="/wiki/West_Asia" title="West Asia">West Asia</a> to the west and <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Asia" title="Southeast Asia">Southeast Asia</a> to the east. Southeast Asia and <a href="/wiki/Littoral_South_Asia" title="Littoral South Asia">Maritime South Asia</a> are the only subregions of Asia that lie partly within the <a href="/wiki/Southern_Hemisphere" title="Southern Hemisphere">Southern Hemisphere</a>. The <a href="/wiki/British_Indian_Ocean_Territory" title="British Indian Ocean Territory">British Indian Ocean Territory</a> and two out of <a href="/wiki/Atolls_of_Maldives" class="mw-redirect" title="Atolls of Maldives">26 atolls</a> of the Maldives in South Asia lie entirely within the <a href="/wiki/Southern_Hemisphere" title="Southern Hemisphere">Southern Hemisphere</a>. Topographically, it is dominated by the <a href="/wiki/Indian_subcontinent" title="Indian subcontinent">Indian subcontinent</a> and is bounded by the <a href="/wiki/Indian_Ocean" title="Indian Ocean">Indian Ocean</a> in the south, and the <a href="/wiki/Himalayas" title="Himalayas">Himalayas</a>, <a href="/wiki/Karakoram" title="Karakoram">Karakoram</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Pamir_Mountains" title="Pamir Mountains">Pamir Mountains</a> in the north.<sup id="cite_ref-Chapman,_Graham_P._p._10_9-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chapman,_Graham_P._p._10-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:South_Asia_(orthographic_projection)_without_national_boundaries.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/South_Asia_%28orthographic_projection%29_without_national_boundaries.svg/250px-South_Asia_%28orthographic_projection%29_without_national_boundaries.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="250" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/South_Asia_%28orthographic_projection%29_without_national_boundaries.svg/500px-South_Asia_%28orthographic_projection%29_without_national_boundaries.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="550" data-file-height="550"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="whitefly" term="whitefly" wikidataID="Q815617" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitefly" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: whitefly<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitefly">Whitefly</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><a href="/wiki/Aleurodicinae" class="mw-redirect" title="Aleurodicinae">Aleurodicinae</a><br>
