You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="root knot nematode" term="root knot nematode" wikidataID="Q2215256" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root_knot_nematode" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: root knot nematode<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root_knot_nematode">Root knot nematode</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Root-knot nematodes</b> are plant-<a href="/wiki/Parasitism" title="Parasitism">parasitic</a> <a href="/wiki/Nematode" title="Nematode">nematodes</a> from the genus <i><b>Meloidogyne</b></i>. They exist in <a href="/wiki/Soil" title="Soil">soil</a> in areas with hot climates or short winters. About 2000 species of plants worldwide are susceptible to infection by root-knot nematodes and they cause approximately 5% of global <a href="/wiki/Crop_loss" class="mw-redirect" title="Crop loss">crop loss</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Root-knot nematode <a href="/wiki/Larva" title="Larva">larvae</a> infect plant <a href="/wiki/Root" title="Root">roots</a>, causing the development of root-knot <a href="/wiki/Gall" title="Gall">galls</a> that drain the plant's photosynthate and nutrients. Infection of young plants may be lethal, while infection of mature plants causes decreased yield.
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:A_juvenile_root-knot_nematode_(Meloidogyne_incognita)_penetrates_a_tomato_root_-_USDA-ARS.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/A_juvenile_root-knot_nematode_%28Meloidogyne_incognita%29_penetrates_a_tomato_root_-_USDA-ARS.jpg/250px-A_juvenile_root-knot_nematode_%28Meloidogyne_incognita%29_penetrates_a_tomato_root_-_USDA-ARS.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="305" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/A_juvenile_root-knot_nematode_%28Meloidogyne_incognita%29_penetrates_a_tomato_root_-_USDA-ARS.jpg/500px-A_juvenile_root-knot_nematode_%28Meloidogyne_incognita%29_penetrates_a_tomato_root_-_USDA-ARS.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2216" data-file-height="2700"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="smut" term="smut" wikidataID="Q3487079" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smut" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: smut<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smut">Smut</a></p><p></p></div><div name="rice cultivation" term="rice cultivation" wikidataID="Q106611631" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_cultivation" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: rice cultivation<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_cultivation">Rice cultivation</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>history of rice cultivation</b> is an interdisciplinary subject that studies archaeological and documentary evidence to explain how rice was first domesticated and cultivated by humans, the spread of cultivation to different regions of the planet, and the technological changes that have impacted cultivation over time. 
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:KITLV_40091_-_Kassian_C%C3%A9phas_-_Relief_of_the_hidden_base_of_Borobudur_-_1890-1891.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/KITLV_40091_-_Kassian_C%C3%A9phas_-_Relief_of_the_hidden_base_of_Borobudur_-_1890-1891.jpg/330px-KITLV_40091_-_Kassian_C%C3%A9phas_-_Relief_of_the_hidden_base_of_Borobudur_-_1890-1891.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="135" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/KITLV_40091_-_Kassian_C%C3%A9phas_-_Relief_of_the_hidden_base_of_Borobudur_-_1890-1891.jpg/500px-KITLV_40091_-_Kassian_C%C3%A9phas_-_Relief_of_the_hidden_base_of_Borobudur_-_1890-1891.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/KITLV_40091_-_Kassian_C%C3%A9phas_-_Relief_of_the_hidden_base_of_Borobudur_-_1890-1891.jpg/960px-KITLV_40091_-_Kassian_C%C3%A9phas_-_Relief_of_the_hidden_base_of_Borobudur_-_1890-1891.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4210" data-file-height="1889"></a><figcaption>Bas-relief at <a href="/wiki/Karmawibhangga_Museum" title="Karmawibhangga Museum">Karmawibhanga Museum in Central Java</a> of 9th century <a href="/wiki/Borobudur" title="Borobudur">Borobudur</a> describes <a href="/wiki/Rice_barn" title="Rice barn">rice barn</a> and rice plants being infested by mouse pestilence. <a href="/wiki/Rice_production_in_Indonesia" title="Rice production in Indonesia">Rice farming</a> has a long history in Indonesia.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Cuttack district" term="Cuttack district" wikidataID="Q2022256" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuttack_district" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Cuttack district<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuttack_district">Cuttack district</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Cuttack district</b> is one of the 30 <a href="/wiki/Districts_of_Odisha" class="mw-redirect" title="Districts of Odisha">districts of Odisha</a> state in <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>. It is located in the coastal part of the state and its administrative headquarters are located in the city of <a href="/wiki/Cuttack" title="Cuttack">Cuttack</a>. As of 2011 Census, after <a href="/wiki/Ganjam_district" title="Ganjam district">Ganjam</a>, it is the second most populous district of Odisha, with a population of 2,624,470.<sup id="cite_ref-districtcensus_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-districtcensus-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The name is an anglicized form of <i>Kataka</i> or <i>Katak</i> meaning Fort &#8211; referring to the <a href="/wiki/Barabati_Fort" class="mw-redirect" title="Barabati Fort">Barabati Fort</a>. The district is bisected by the river <a href="/wiki/Mahanadi" title="Mahanadi">Mahanadi</a> and its numerous distributaries and occupies a large portion of the river's delta. It is bounded by the <a href="/wiki/Angul" title="Angul">Angul</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dhenkanal" title="Dhenkanal">Dhenkanal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nayagarh" title="Nayagarh">Nayagarh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Khurda" class="mw-redirect" title="Khurda">Khurda</a> districts to the west while its southern and eastern boundaries touch <a href="/wiki/Puri" title="Puri">Puri</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jagatsinghpur" title="Jagatsinghpur">Jagatsinghpur</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kendrapara" title="Kendrapara">Kendrapara</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jajpur" title="Jajpur">Jajpur</a> districts.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Sketch_Map_Showing_Provincial_and_District_Divisions_to_Accompany_the_Administration_Report,_1872%E2%80%9373_(Cropped_to_Bihar,_Chota_Nagpur,_and_Odisha).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/The_Sketch_Map_Showing_Provincial_and_District_Divisions_to_Accompany_the_Administration_Report%2C_1872%E2%80%9373_%28Cropped_to_Bihar%2C_Chota_Nagpur%2C_and_Odisha%29.jpg/250px-The_Sketch_Map_Showing_Provincial_and_District_Divisions_to_Accompany_the_Administration_Report%2C_1872%E2%80%9373_%28Cropped_to_Bihar%2C_Chota_Nagpur%2C_and_Odisha%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="333" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/The_Sketch_Map_Showing_Provincial_and_District_Divisions_to_Accompany_the_Administration_Report%2C_1872%E2%80%9373_%28Cropped_to_Bihar%2C_Chota_Nagpur%2C_and_Odisha%29.jpg/500px-The_Sketch_Map_Showing_Provincial_and_District_Divisions_to_Accompany_the_Administration_Report%2C_1872%E2%80%9373_%28Cropped_to_Bihar%2C_Chota_Nagpur%2C_and_Odisha%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3000" data-file-height="4000"></a><figcaption>Cuttack District as part of the Orissa Division, <a href="/wiki/Bengal_Presidency" title="Bengal Presidency">Bengal Presidency</a>, 1872</figcaption></figure>

Variation in stomatal conductance is driven primarily by variation in the width (aperture) of the stomatal pores and the number of stomata per unit leaf area (stomatal density), and to a lesser extent by variation in the depth of the stomatal pore; temperature also has a small direct effect, independent of these other factors.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

Dual-beam experiment with epidermal peels of <i>Commelina.</i> Peels were irradiated with 0.2 mmol m<sup>&#8722;2</sup> s<sup>&#8722;1</sup> of red light; 0.01 mmol m<sup>&#8722;2</sup> s<sup>&#8722;1</sup> of blue light was added as indicated by the <i>arrow</i>. <i>Dashed lines</i> at the bottom of figure = aperture values at the end of 4h incubation in darkness, under normal and CO<sub>2</sub>-free air. The incubation media were aerated with CO<sub>2</sub>-free air throughout the experiment. (Schwartz and Zieger, 1984)<sup id="cite_ref-:0_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure></div><p></p></div><div name="crop wild relatives" term="crop wild relatives" wikidataID="Q1141015" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crop_wild_relatives" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: crop wild relatives<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crop_wild_relatives">Crop wild relatives</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>crop wild relative</b> (<b>CWR</b>) is a wild plant closely related to a <a href="/wiki/Domesticated_plant" class="mw-redirect" title="Domesticated plant">domesticated plant</a>. It may be a wild ancestor of the domesticated (cultivated) plant or another closely related <a href="/wiki/Taxon" title="Taxon">taxon</a>.
</p>

Cryopreservation is an effective way to transport biological samples over long distances, store samples for prolonged periods of time, and create a bank of samples for users. 
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg/330px-Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg" decoding="async" width="280" height="420" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg/500px-Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/95/Cryopreservation_USDA_Gene_Bank.jpg 2x" data-file-width="864" data-file-height="1296"></a><figcaption>Cryogenically preserved samples being removed from a <a href="/wiki/Cryogenic_storage_dewar" title="Cryogenic storage dewar">dewar</a> of <a href="/wiki/Liquid_nitrogen" title="Liquid nitrogen">liquid nitrogen</a></figcaption></figure>

The term was formerly used to refer to the field of <a href="/wiki/Sociology" title="Sociology">sociology</a>, the original "science of society", established in the 18th century. <p></p></div><div name="Branch Office" term="Branch Office" wikidataID="Q1880737" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch_office" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Branch Office<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch_office">Branch office</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>branch office</b> is an outlet of a company or, more generally, an organization that &#8211; unlike a <a href="/wiki/Subsidiary" title="Subsidiary">subsidiary</a> &#8211; does not constitute a separate legal entity, while being physically separated from the organization's main office.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Branching is particularly widespread in <a href="/wiki/Branch_(banking)" title="Branch (banking)">banking</a> and other financial institutions, where the products' complexity requires local offices to act more like an agency than as a separate company. A branch structure exposes the owning company to full <a href="/wiki/Taxable_income" title="Taxable income">taxability</a> and <a href="/wiki/Legal_liability" title="Legal liability">legal liability</a> in regard to the branch office's operations.

<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Latin_letter_D.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Latin_letter_D.svg/250px-Latin_letter_D.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Latin_letter_D.svg/500px-Latin_letter_D.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="450" data-file-height="300"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="Crops Research Institute" term="Crops Research Institute" wikidataID="Q5187985" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crops_Research_Institute" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Crops Research Institute<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crops_Research_Institute">Crops Research Institute</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>CSIR - Crops Research Institute (CRI)</b> is one of the thirteen (13) research Institutes of the <a href="/wiki/Council_for_Scientific_and_Industrial_Research_%E2%80%93_Ghana" title="Council for Scientific and Industrial Research &#8211; Ghana"><b>Council for Scientific and Industrial Research of Ghana (CSIR)</b></a>. CSIR-CRI evolved from the Specialists' branch of the <a href="/wiki/Gold_Coast_(British_colony)" title="Gold Coast (British colony)">Gold Coast</a> Department of Agriculture. In 1959, the Specialists' branch and the Soil and Land Use Survey Department were merged to form the Scientific Services Division of the then <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Food_and_Agriculture_(Ghana)" title="Ministry of Food and Agriculture (Ghana)">Ministry of Agriculture (MOFA)</a>. The Scientific Services Division was transferred to the National Research Council in 1962 and then to the <a href="/wiki/Ghana_Academy_of_Arts_and_Sciences" title="Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences">Ghana Academy of Sciences</a> in 1963 and renamed the Agriculture Research Institute (ARI). 
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Council_for_Scientific_and_Industrial_Research_%E2%80%93_Ghana_logo.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Council_for_Scientific_and_Industrial_Research_%E2%80%93_Ghana_logo.jpg/120px-Council_for_Scientific_and_Industrial_Research_%E2%80%93_Ghana_logo.jpg" decoding="async" width="100" height="100" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Council_for_Scientific_and_Industrial_Research_%E2%80%93_Ghana_logo.jpg/250px-Council_for_Scientific_and_Industrial_Research_%E2%80%93_Ghana_logo.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="336" data-file-height="336"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="rice moth" term="rice moth" wikidataID="Q2629584" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_moth" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: rice moth<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_moth">Rice moth</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>rice moth</b> (<i>Corcyra cephalonica</i>) is a <a href="/wiki/Moth" title="Moth">moth</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Family_(biology)" title="Family (biology)">family</a> <a href="/wiki/Pyralidae" title="Pyralidae">Pyralidae</a>. This small moth can become a significant <a href="/wiki/Pest_(organism)" title="Pest (organism)">pest</a>. Its <a href="/wiki/Caterpillar" title="Caterpillar">caterpillars</a> feed on dry plantstuffs such as <a href="/wiki/Seed" title="Seed">seeds</a>, including <a href="/wiki/Cereals" class="mw-redirect" title="Cereals">cereals</a> (e.g. <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a>). Other recorded<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> foods are <a href="/wiki/Flour" title="Flour">flour</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dried_fruits" class="mw-redirect" title="Dried fruits">dried fruits</a>.
</p>

The oil extracted from copra is rich in <a href="/wiki/Lauric_acid" title="Lauric acid">lauric acid</a>, making it an important commodity in the preparation of <a href="/wiki/Lauryl_alcohol" class="mw-redirect" title="Lauryl alcohol">lauryl alcohol</a>, soaps, fatty acids, cosmetics, etc. and thus a lucrative product for many coconut-producing countries. The palatable oil cake, known as copra cake, obtained as a residue in the production of copra oil is used in animal feeds. The ground cake is known as coconut or copra meal.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

using observable characteristics of organisms (or genes), which is known as <a href="/wiki/Computational_phylogenetics" title="Computational phylogenetics">phylogenetic inference</a>. It infers the relationship among <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organisms</a> based on empirical data and observed <a href="/wiki/Heritable" class="mw-redirect" title="Heritable">heritable</a> traits of <a href="/wiki/DNA" title="DNA">DNA</a> sequences, <a href="/wiki/Protein" title="Protein">protein</a> <a href="/wiki/Amino_acid" title="Amino acid">amino acid</a> sequences, and <a href="/wiki/Morphology_(biology)" title="Morphology (biology)">morphology</a>. The results are a <a href="/wiki/Phylogenetic_tree" title="Phylogenetic tree">phylogenetic tree</a>&#8212;a diagram depicting the <a href="/wiki/Hypothesis" title="Hypothesis">hypothetical</a> relationships among the organisms, reflecting their inferred evolutionary history.<sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

O. Wilson">E. O. Wilson</a> characterised parasites' way of feeding as "predators that eat prey in units of less than one".<sup id="cite_ref-Wilson2014_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Wilson2014-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Parasites include single-celled <a href="/wiki/Protozoa" title="Protozoa">protozoans</a> such as the agents of <a href="/wiki/Malaria" title="Malaria">malaria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sleeping_sickness" class="mw-redirect" title="Sleeping sickness">sleeping sickness</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Amoebic_dysentery" class="mw-redirect" title="Amoebic dysentery">amoebic dysentery</a>; animals such as <a href="/wiki/Hookworm" title="Hookworm">hookworms</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lice" class="mw-redirect" title="Lice">lice</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mosquito" title="Mosquito">mosquitoes</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Vampire_bat" title="Vampire bat">vampire bats</a>; <a href="/wiki/Fungi" class="mw-redirect" title="Fungi">fungi</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Armillaria_mellea" title="Armillaria mellea">honey fungus</a> and the agents of <a href="/wiki/Ringworm" class="mw-redirect" title="Ringworm">ringworm</a>; and plants such as <a href="/wiki/Mistletoe" title="Mistletoe">mistletoe</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dodder" class="mw-redirect" title="Dodder">dodder</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Orobanchaceae" title="Orobanchaceae">broomrapes</a>.

It preserves their <a href="/wiki/Genetic_information" class="mw-redirect" title="Genetic information">genetic information</a> in the form of reproductive material like seeds, sperm, eggs, <a href="/wiki/Embryo" title="Embryo">embryos</a>, cells and other kinds of DNA. Oftentimes, these banks house the genetic material of species that are <a href="/wiki/Endangered" class="mw-redirect" title="Endangered">endangered</a> or <a href="/wiki/Extinction" title="Extinction">close to extinction.</a>They are also used for the preservation of major crop species and cultivars, in order to preserve <a href="/wiki/Crop_diversity" title="Crop diversity">crop diversity</a>.This protects the organism from threats like <a href="/wiki/Extinction" title="Extinction">extinction</a>, <a href="/wiki/Disease" title="Disease">diseases</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">climate change</a>.

Mexico covers 1,972,550&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (761,610 sq mi),<sup id="cite_ref-cia.gov_15-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia.gov-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_area" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by area">thirteenth-largest country</a> in the world by land area. With a population exceeding 130 million, Mexico is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_population" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by population">tenth-most populous country</a> in the world and is home to the <a href="/wiki/Hispanophone#Countries" title="Hispanophone">largest number of native Spanish speakers</a> as of 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-2020_Census_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2020_Census-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Mexico_City" title="Mexico City">Mexico City</a> is the capital and <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Mexico" title="List of cities in Mexico">largest city</a>, which ranks among the <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_by_population" class="mw-redirect" title="List of cities by population">most populous metropolitan areas</a> in the world.

It was originally named for its first discovery in <a href="/wiki/Feces" title="Feces">feces</a>, but was later found to be common in soil, water, and environments in association with humans. While <a href="/wiki/Opportunistic_infection" title="Opportunistic infection">opportunistic infections</a> do occur, the <a href="/wiki/Bacterium" class="mw-redirect" title="Bacterium">bacterium</a> is generally considered nonpathogenic. When an opportunistic infection does occur, it is usually observed in the form of a urinary tract infection.

href="/wiki/Southeast_Europe" title="Southeast Europe">Southeast</a> and <a href="/wiki/Central_Europe" title="Central Europe">Central Europe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-unece.org_16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-unece.org-16"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Located in the <a href="/wiki/Balkans" title="Balkans">Balkans</a>, it borders <a href="/wiki/Hungary" title="Hungary">Hungary</a> to the north, <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a> to the northeast, <a href="/wiki/Bulgaria" title="Bulgaria">Bulgaria</a> to the southeast, <a </div><p></p></div><div name="Nutrition" term="Nutrition" wikidataID="Q2138622" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrition" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Nutrition<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrition">Nutrition</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Nutrition</b> is the <a href="/wiki/Biochemistry" title="Biochemistry">biochemical</a> and <a href="/wiki/Physiology" title="Physiology">physiological</a> process by which an <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organism</a> uses <a href="/wiki/Food" title="Food">food</a> and <a href="/wiki/Water" title="Water">water</a> to support its <a href="/wiki/Life" title="Life">life</a>. The intake of these substances provides organisms with <a href="/wiki/Nutrient" title="Nutrient">nutrients</a> (divided into <a href="/wiki/Macronutrient" class="mw-redirect" title="Macronutrient">macro-</a> and <a href="/wiki/Micronutrient" title="Micronutrient">micro-</a>) which can be <a href="/wiki/Metabolism" title="Metabolism">metabolized</a> to create <a href="/wiki/Food_energy" title="Food energy">energy</a> and chemical structures; too much or too little of an essential nutrient can cause <a href="/wiki/Malnutrition" title="Malnutrition">malnutrition</a>. <a href="/wiki/Nutritional_science" title="Nutritional science">Nutritional science</a>, the study of nutrition as a <a href="/wiki/Hard_science" class="mw-redirect" title="Hard science">hard science</a>, typically emphasizes <a href="/wiki/Human_nutrition" title="Human nutrition">human nutrition</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Close_wing_posture_of_Amblypodia_anita_(Hewitson,_1862)_-_Purple_Leaf_Blue_(Male)_gathering_nutrients_from_bird_dropping_WLB.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="see caption" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Close_wing_posture_of_Amblypodia_anita_%28Hewitson%2C_1862%29_-_Purple_Leaf_Blue_%28Male%29_gathering_nutrients_from_bird_dropping_WLB.jpg/500px-Close_wing_posture_of_Amblypodia_anita_%28Hewitson%2C_1862%29_-_Purple_Leaf_Blue_%28Male%29_gathering_nutrients_from_bird_dropping_WLB.jpg" decoding="async" width="380" height="253" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Close_wing_posture_of_Amblypodia_anita_%28Hewitson%2C_1862%29_-_Purple_Leaf_Blue_%28Male%29_gathering_nutrients_from_bird_dropping_WLB.jpg/960px-Close_wing_posture_of_Amblypodia_anita_%28Hewitson%2C_1862%29_-_Purple_Leaf_Blue_%28Male%29_gathering_nutrients_from_bird_dropping_WLB.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="6000" data-file-height="4000"></a><figcaption>A purple leaf blue butterfly (<i><a href="/wiki/Amblypodia_anita" title="Amblypodia anita">Amblypodia anita</a></i>) gathering <a href="/wiki/Nutrient" title="Nutrient">nutrients</a> from <a href="/wiki/Guano" title="Guano">guano</a></figcaption></figure>

It is a close <a href="/wiki/Chemical_analog" class="mw-redirect" title="Chemical analog">chemical analog</a> of <a href="/wiki/Methamphetamine" title="Methamphetamine">methamphetamine</a>, which has been sold as a <a href="/wiki/Designer_drug" title="Designer drug">designer drug</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It was originally patented by Knoll Pharma as one of several analogs for pharmaceutical applications. In animal models these analogs showed properties of cognitive enhancement and increased pain tolerance.<sup id="cite_ref-Korea2_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Korea2-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nevertheless, this class of compounds was never developed into a medicine.
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:N,%CE%B1-Diethylphenylethylamine.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/N%2C%CE%B1-Diethylphenylethylamine.svg/250px-N%2C%CE%B1-Diethylphenylethylamine.svg.png" decoding="async" width="200" height="103" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/N%2C%CE%B1-Diethylphenylethylamine.svg/330px-N%2C%CE%B1-Diethylphenylethylamine.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/N%2C%CE%B1-Diethylphenylethylamine.svg/500px-N%2C%CE%B1-Diethylphenylethylamine.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="445" data-file-height="230"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="advance lines" term="advance lines" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=advance%20lines" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: advance lines<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=advance%20lines">advance lines</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Indian Society" term="Indian Society" wikidataID="Q668" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_society" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Indian Society<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_society">Indian society</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>India</b>, officially the <b>Republic of India</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>j<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-30" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-30"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a country in <a href="/wiki/South_Asia" title="South Asia">South Asia</a>.  It is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area" title="List of countries and dependencies by area">seventh-largest country by area</a>; the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_population_(United_Nations)" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by population (United Nations)">most populous country</a> since 2023;<sup id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and, since its independence in 1947, the world's most populous democracy.<sup id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-stein-arnold_33-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-stein-arnold-33"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEFisher2018184&#8211;185_34-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFisher2018184%E2%80%93185-34"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Bounded by the <a href="/wiki/Indian_Ocean" title="Indian Ocean">Indian Ocean</a> on the south, the <a href="/wiki/Arabian_Sea" title="Arabian Sea">Arabian Sea</a> on the southwest, and the <a href="/wiki/Bay_of_Bengal" title="Bay of Bengal">Bay of Bengal</a> on the southeast, it shares land borders with <a href="/wiki/Pakistan" title="Pakistan">Pakistan</a> to the west;<sup id="cite_ref-36" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-36"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>k<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nepal" title="Nepal">Nepal</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Bhutan" title="Bhutan">Bhutan</a> to the north; and <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh" title="Bangladesh">Bangladesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Myanmar" title="Myanmar">Myanmar</a> to the east. In the <a href="/wiki/Indian_Ocean" title="Indian Ocean">Indian Ocean</a>, India is near <a href="/wiki/Sri_Lanka" title="Sri Lanka">Sri Lanka</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Maldives" title="Maldives">Maldives</a>; its <a href="/wiki/Andaman_and_Nicobar_Islands" title="Andaman and Nicobar Islands">Andaman and Nicobar Islands</a> share a <a href="/wiki/Maritime_boundary" title="Maritime boundary">maritime border</a> with Myanmar, <a href="/wiki/Thailand" title="Thailand">Thailand</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Indonesia" title="Indonesia">Indonesia</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:India_(orthographic_projection).svg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Image of a globe centred on India, with India highlighted." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/250px-India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="250" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/500px-India_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="541" data-file-height="541"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="leaf spot disease" term="leaf spot disease" wikidataID="Q6508875" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf_spot_disease" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: leaf spot disease<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf_spot_disease">Leaf spot disease</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>leaf spot</b> is a limited, discoloured, diseased area of a leaf that is caused by <a href="/wiki/Fungus" title="Fungus">fungal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bacteria" title="Bacteria">bacterial</a> or viral plant diseases, or by injuries from <a href="/wiki/Nematode" title="Nematode">nematodes</a>, insects, environmental factors, <a href="/wiki/Toxicity" title="Toxicity">toxicity</a> or <a href="/wiki/Herbicide" title="Herbicide">herbicides</a>. These discoloured spots or lesions often have a centre of <a href="/wiki/Necrosis" title="Necrosis">necrosis</a> (cell death).<sup id="cite_ref-:0_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Symptoms can overlap across causal agents, however differing signs and symptoms of certain pathogens can lead to the diagnosis of the type of leaf spot disease. Prolonged wet and humid conditions promote leaf spot disease and most pathogens are spread by wind, splashing rain or <a href="/wiki/Irrigation" title="Irrigation">irrigation</a> that carry the disease to other leaves.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:%27Cercospora_capsici.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/%27Cercospora_capsici.jpg/250px-%27Cercospora_capsici.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="163" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/%27Cercospora_capsici.jpg/500px-%27Cercospora_capsici.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="768" data-file-height="502"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="Laxminarayana" term="Laxminarayana" wikidataID="Q6479899" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxminarayana" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Laxminarayana<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxminarayana">Laxminarayana</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Lakshmi Narayana</b> (<a href="/wiki/Sanskrit_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Sanskrit language">Sanskrit</a>: <span lang="sa">&#2354;&#2325;&#2381;&#2359;&#2381;&#2350;&#2368;-&#2344;&#2366;&#2352;&#2366;&#2351;&#2339;</span>, <a href="/wiki/IAST" class="mw-redirect" title="IAST">IAST</a>: <span title="International Alphabet of Sanskrit transliteration"><i lang="sa-Latn">Lak&#7779;m&#299;n&#257;r&#257;ya&#7751;a</i></span>) or <b>Lakshmi Narayan</b> is the dual representation of the <a href="/wiki/Hinduism" title="Hinduism">Hindu deities</a> <a href="/wiki/Vishnu" title="Vishnu">Vishnu</a>, also known as <a href="/wiki/Narayana" title="Narayana">Narayana</a>, and his consort, <a href="/wiki/Lakshmi" title="Lakshmi">Lakshmi</a>, traditionally featured in their abode, <a href="/wiki/Vaikuntha" title="Vaikuntha">Vaikuntha</a>. The goddess of wealth and prosperity, Lakshmi, is depicted as standing next to Vishnu, who holds the <a href="/wiki/Panchajanya" title="Panchajanya">Panchajanya</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kaumodaki" title="Kaumodaki">Kaumodaki</a>, <a href="/wiki/Padma_(Vishnu)" title="Padma (Vishnu)">Padma</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Sudarshana_Chakra" title="Sudarshana Chakra">Sudarshana Chakra</a>. Another depiction of Lakshmi Narayana portrays Lakshmi in service of Narayana, who reclines on serpent <a href="/wiki/Sesha" class="mw-redirect" title="Sesha">Shesha</a>, floating in <a href="/wiki/Kshira_Sagara" title="Kshira Sagara">Kshira Sagara</a>, the ocean of milk.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Lakshmi_Narayana_at_Temple_Devi_Jagdambi_(Khajur%C3%A2ho).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Lakshmi_Narayana_at_Temple_Devi_Jagdambi_%28Khajur%C3%A2ho%29.jpg/250px-Lakshmi_Narayana_at_Temple_Devi_Jagdambi_%28Khajur%C3%A2ho%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="272" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Lakshmi_Narayana_at_Temple_Devi_Jagdambi_%28Khajur%C3%A2ho%29.jpg/500px-Lakshmi_Narayana_at_Temple_Devi_Jagdambi_%28Khajur%C3%A2ho%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="744" data-file-height="808"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="sustainability" term="sustainability" wikidataID="Q219416" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainability" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: sustainability<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainability">Sustainability</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Sustainability</b> (from the latin <i>sustinere</i> - hold up, hold upright; furnish with means of support; bear, undergo, endure) is the ability to continue over a long period of time.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In modern usage it generally refers to a state in which the environment, economy, and society will continue to exist over a long period of time.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Many definitions emphasize the environmental dimension.<sup id="cite_ref-Kotze-2022_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kotze-2022-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Bosselmann-2010_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bosselmann-2010-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This can include addressing key <a href="/wiki/Environmental_issues" title="Environmental issues">environmental problems</a>, such as <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">climate change</a> and <a href="/wiki/Biodiversity_loss" title="Biodiversity loss">biodiversity loss</a>. The idea of sustainability can guide decisions at the global, national, organizational, and individual levels.<sup id="cite_ref-Berg-2020_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Berg-2020-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A related concept is that of <a href="/wiki/Sustainable_development" title="Sustainable development">sustainable development</a>, and the terms are often used to mean the same thing.<sup id="cite_ref-EB-2022_7-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EB-2022-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> distinguishes the two like this: "<i>Sustainability</i> is often thought of as a long-term goal (i.e. a more sustainable world), while <i>sustainable development</i> refers to the many processes and pathways to achieve it."<sup id="cite_ref-UNESCO-2015_8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UNESCO-2015-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp/250px-Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="159" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp/500px-Visualization_of_pillars_of_sustainability.webp.png 1.5x" data-file-width="869" data-file-height="553"></a><figcaption>Three visual representations of sustainability and its three dimensions. The left image shows sustainability as three intersecting circles. The top right is a nested approach where social and economic sustainability are contained within environmental sustainability. The bottom right shows pillars with the different components holding up sustainability.</figcaption></figure>

With an area of about 331,000 square kilometres (128,000&#160;sq&#160;mi) and a population of over 102&#160;million, it is the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population" title="List of countries and dependencies by population">16th-most populous country</a>. One of two <a href="/wiki/Communist_state" title="Communist state">communist states</a> in <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Asia" title="Southeast Asia">Southeast Asia</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>i<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Vietnam is bordered by <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a> to the north, and <a href="/wiki/Laos" title="Laos">Laos</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cambodia" title="Cambodia">Cambodia</a> to the west; it lies along the <a href="/wiki/Gulf_of_Thailand" title="Gulf of Thailand">Gulf of Thailand</a> to the southwest and the <a href="/wiki/South_China_Sea" title="South China Sea">South China Sea</a> to the east, where it has shared and <a href="/wiki/Territorial_disputes_in_the_South_China_Sea" title="Territorial disputes in the South China Sea">disputed maritime borders</a> with other countries. Its capital is <a href="/wiki/Hanoi" title="Hanoi">Hanoi</a>, while its <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Vietnam#Largest_cities_by_population" title="List of cities in Vietnam">largest city</a> is <a href="/wiki/Ho_Chi_Minh_City" title="Ho Chi Minh City">Ho Chi Minh City</a>.

</div><p></p></div><div name="Molecular Biology" term="Molecular Biology" wikidataID="Q7202" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_Biology" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Molecular Biology<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_Biology">Molecular Biology</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Molecular biology</b> <span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="'m' in 'my'">m</span><span title="/&#601;/: 'a' in 'about'">&#601;</span><span title="/&#712;/: primary stress follows">&#712;</span><span title="'l' in 'lie'">l</span><span title="/&#603;/: 'e' in 'dress'">&#603;</span><span title="'k' in 'kind'">k</span><span title="/j/: 'y' in 'yes'">j</span><span title="/&#650;/: 'u' in 'push'">&#650;</span><span title="'l' in 'lie'">l</span><span title="/&#601;r/: 'er' in 'letter'">&#601;r</span></span>/</a></span></span> is a branch of <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a> that seeks to understand the <a href="/wiki/Molecule" title="Molecule">molecular</a> structures and chemical processes that are the basis of biological activity within and between <a href="/wiki/Cell_(biology)" title="Cell (biology)">cells</a>. It is centered largely on the study of <a href="/wiki/Nucleic_acid" title="Nucleic acid">nucleic acids</a> (such as <a href="/wiki/DNA" title="DNA">DNA</a> and <a href="/wiki/RNA" title="RNA">RNA</a>) and <a href="/wiki/Protein" title="Protein">proteins</a>. It examines the structure, function, and interactions of these <a href="/wiki/Macromolecule" title="Macromolecule">macromolecules</a> as they orchestrate processes such as <a href="/wiki/DNA_replication" title="DNA replication">replication</a>, <a href="/wiki/Transcription_(biology)" title="Transcription (biology)">transcription</a>, <a href="/wiki/Translation_(biology)" title="Translation (biology)">translation</a>, <a href="/wiki/Protein_biosynthesis" title="Protein biosynthesis">protein synthesis</a>, and complex <a href="/wiki/Biomolecule" title="Biomolecule">biomolecular</a> interactions. The field of molecular biology is <a href="/wiki/Multi-disciplinary" class="mw-redirect" title="Multi-disciplinary">multi-disciplinary</a>, relying on principles from <a href="/wiki/Genetics" title="Genetics">genetics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Biochemistry" title="Biochemistry">biochemistry</a>, physics, mathematics, and more recently computer science (<a href="/wiki/Bioinformatics" title="Bioinformatics">bioinformatics</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-cell2_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cell2-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Gannon-2002_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gannon-2002-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Extended_Central_Dogma_with_Enzymes.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Extended_Central_Dogma_with_Enzymes.jpg/250px-Extended_Central_Dogma_with_Enzymes.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="128" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Extended_Central_Dogma_with_Enzymes.jpg/500px-Extended_Central_Dogma_with_Enzymes.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="762" data-file-height="389"></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Central_dogma_of_molecular_biology" title="Central dogma of molecular biology">central dogma of molecular biology</a> showing the flow of genetic information within a biological system.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="conventional tillage" term="conventional tillage" wikidataID="Q5166322" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conventional_tillage" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: conventional tillage<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conventional_tillage">Conventional tillage</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Conventional tillage</b> refers to <a href="/wiki/Tillage" title="Tillage">tillage</a> operations considered standard for a specific location and crop and that tend to bury the <a href="/wiki/Crop_residue" title="Crop residue">crop residues</a>; usually considered as a base for determining the cost effectiveness of <a href="/wiki/Erosion_control" title="Erosion control">erosion control</a> practices.

</span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honey_bees">Honey bees</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>honey bee</b> (also spelled <b>honeybee</b>) is a <a href="/wiki/Eusocial" class="mw-redirect" title="Eusocial">eusocial</a> <a href="/wiki/Flying_insect" class="mw-redirect" title="Flying insect">flying insect</a> from the <a href="/wiki/Genus" title="Genus">genus</a> <i><b>Apis</b></i> of the largest <a href="/wiki/Bee" title="Bee">bee</a> <a href="/wiki/Family_(biology)" title="Family (biology)">family</a>, <a href="/wiki/Apidae" title="Apidae">Apidae</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Honey bees are known for their construction of <a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/perennial" class="extiw" title="wiktionary:perennial">perennial</a> <a href="/wiki/Nest" title="Nest">nests</a> within cavities (i.e. <a href="/wiki/Beehive" title="Beehive">beehives</a>) containing <a href="/wiki/Honeycomb" title="Honeycomb">hexagonal cells</a> made of <a href="/wiki/Beeswax" title="Beeswax">secreted wax</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> their large <a href="/wiki/Colony_(biology)" title="Colony (biology)">colony</a> sizes, and their routine <a href="/wiki/Regurgitation_(digestion)" title="Regurgitation (digestion)">regurgitation</a> of digested <a href="/wiki/Carbohydrate" title="Carbohydrate">carbohydrates</a> as surplus <a href="/wiki/Food_storage" title="Food storage">food storage</a> in the form of <a href="/wiki/Honey" title="Honey">honey</a>, the lattermost of which distinguishes their hives as a prized <a href="/wiki/Foraging" title="Foraging">foraging</a> target of many <a href="/wiki/Mellivorous" class="mw-redirect" title="Mellivorous">mellivorous</a> animals including <a href="/wiki/Honey_badger" title="Honey badger">honey badgers</a>, bears and human <a href="/wiki/Hunter-gatherer" title="Hunter-gatherer">hunter-gatherers</a>.

Cereals are the world's largest <a href="/wiki/Crop" title="Crop">crops</a>, and are therefore <a href="/wiki/Staple_food" title="Staple food">staple foods</a>. They include <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a>, <a href="/wiki/Wheat" title="Wheat">wheat</a> (UK: corn), <a href="/wiki/Rye" title="Rye">rye</a>, <a href="/wiki/Oat" title="Oat">oats</a>, <a href="/wiki/Barley" title="Barley">barley</a>, <a href="/wiki/Millet" title="Millet">millet</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">maize</a> (US: corn). Edible grains from other plant families, such as <a href="/wiki/Amaranth" title="Amaranth">amaranth</a>, <a href="/wiki/Buckwheat" title="Buckwheat">buckwheat</a> and <a href="/wiki/Quinoa" title="Quinoa">quinoa</a>, are <a href="/wiki/Pseudocereal" title="Pseudocereal">pseudocereals</a>. Most cereals are <a href="/wiki/Annual_plant" title="Annual plant">annuals</a>, producing one crop from each planting, though rice is sometimes grown as a <a href="/wiki/Perennial" title="Perennial">perennial</a>. Winter varieties are hardy enough to be planted in the autumn, becoming dormant in the winter, and harvested in spring or early summer; spring varieties are planted in spring and harvested in late summer. The term cereal is derived from the name of the <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Rome" title="Ancient Rome">Roman</a> goddess of grain crops and fertility, <a href="/wiki/Ceres_(mythology)" title="Ceres (mythology)">Ceres</a>.

In a civil <a href="/wiki/State_(polity)" title="State (polity)">state</a>, <i>authority</i> may be practiced by <a href="/wiki/Legislature" title="Legislature">legislative</a>, <a href="/wiki/Executive_(government)" title="Executive (government)">executive</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Judiciary" title="Judiciary">judicial</a> branches of <a href="/wiki/Government" title="Government">government</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-:0_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> each of which has authority and <em>is</em> an authority.<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
The term "authority" has multiple nuances and distinctions within various academic fields ranging from <a href="/wiki/Sociology" title="Sociology">sociology</a> to <a href="/wiki/Political_science" title="Political science">political science</a>.

It is generally caused by <a href="/wiki/Phytoplasma" title="Phytoplasma">phytoplasma</a> or <a href="/wiki/Virus" title="Virus">virus</a> infections,<sup id="cite_ref-mor_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mor-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> though it may also be because of <a href="/wiki/Physiological_plant_disorders" class="mw-redirect" title="Physiological plant disorders">environmental factors</a> that result in an imbalance in <a href="/wiki/Plant_hormone" title="Plant hormone">plant hormones</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-sim2004_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sim2004-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Phyllody causes the affected plant to become partially or entirely sterile, as it is unable to produce normal <a href="/wiki/Flower" title="Flower">flowers</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-mor_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mor-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-triv_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-triv-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

Other sources of beekeeping income include <a href="/wiki/Pollination" title="Pollination">pollination</a> of crops, raising <a href="/wiki/Queen_bee" title="Queen bee">queens</a>, and production of package bees for sale. Bee hives are kept in an <a href="/wiki/Apiary" title="Apiary">apiary</a> or "bee yard".

TOC determinations are made in a variety of application areas. For example, TOC may be used as  a non-specific indicator of water quality, or TOC of <a href="/wiki/Source_rock" title="Source rock">source rock</a> may be used as one factor in evaluating a <a href="/wiki/Petroleum_play" title="Petroleum play">petroleum play</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-EIAJune2013_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EIAJune2013-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> For marine surface sediments average TOC content is 0.5% in the deep ocean, and 2% along the eastern margins.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

The adult beetles are relatively large, ranging between <style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1154941027">.mw-parser-output .frac{white-space:nowrap}.mw-parser-output .frac .num,.mw-parser-output .frac .den{font-size:80%;line-height:0;vertical-align:super}.mw-parser-output .frac .den{vertical-align:sub}.mw-parser-output .sr-only{border:0;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);clip-path:polygon(0px 0px,0px 0px,0px 0px);height:1px;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:absolute;width:1px}</style>2 and 4 centimetres (1 and <span class="frac">1<span class="sr-only">+</span><span class="num">1</span>&#8260;<span class="den">2</span></span> inches) long, and are usually a rusty red colour&#8212;but many colour variants exist and have often been classified as different species (e.g., <i><a href="/wiki/Rhynchophorus_vulneratus" title="Rhynchophorus vulneratus">R. vulneratus</a></i>). Weevil larvae can excavate holes in the trunks of <a href="/wiki/Palm_tree" class="mw-redirect" title="Palm tree">palm trees</a> up to 1 metre (3.3&#160;ft) long, thereby weakening and eventually killing the host plant. As a result, the weevil is considered a major pest in palm plantations, including the <a href="/wiki/Coconut_palm" class="mw-redirect" title="Coconut palm">coconut palm</a>, <a href="/wiki/Date_palm" title="Date palm">date palm</a> and <a href="/wiki/Oil_palm" class="mw-redirect" title="Oil palm">oil palm</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-NAPPO-PestAlert_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NAPPO-PestAlert-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Rhynchophorus_ferrugineus_MHNT.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Rhynchophorus_ferrugineus_MHNT.jpg/250px-Rhynchophorus_ferrugineus_MHNT.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="331" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Rhynchophorus_ferrugineus_MHNT.jpg/500px-Rhynchophorus_ferrugineus_MHNT.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2955" data-file-height="3918"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="IOPEPC" term="IOPEPC" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=IOPEPC" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: IOPEPC<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=IOPEPC">IOPEPC</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

It preserves their <a href="/wiki/Genetic_information" class="mw-redirect" title="Genetic information">genetic information</a> in the form of reproductive material like seeds, sperm, eggs, <a href="/wiki/Embryo" title="Embryo">embryos</a>, cells and other kinds of DNA. Oftentimes, these banks house the genetic material of species that are <a href="/wiki/Endangered" class="mw-redirect" title="Endangered">endangered</a> or <a href="/wiki/Extinction" title="Extinction">close to extinction.</a>They are also used for the preservation of major crop species and cultivars, in order to preserve <a href="/wiki/Crop_diversity" title="Crop diversity">crop diversity</a>.This protects the organism from threats like <a href="/wiki/Extinction" title="Extinction">extinction</a>, <a href="/wiki/Disease" title="Disease">diseases</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">climate change</a>.
</p>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="coconut rhinoceros beetle" term="coconut rhinoceros beetle" wikidataID="Q1188841" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut_rhinoceros_beetle" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: coconut rhinoceros beetle<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut_rhinoceros_beetle">Coconut rhinoceros beetle</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><i><b>Oryctes rhinoceros</b></i>, also known as <b>coconut rhinoceros beetle</b>, <b>Asiatic rhinoceros beetle</b>, and <b>coconut palm rhinoceros beetle</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-CABI37974_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CABI37974-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a large species of beetle (typically 4&#8211;5 cm long), belonging to the rhinoceros beetles subfamily <a href="/wiki/Dynastinae" title="Dynastinae">Dynastinae</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-gbif4995642_1-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gbif4995642-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  <i>Oryctes rhinoceros</i> attacks <a href="/wiki/Coconut" title="Coconut">coconut palms</a> and other palms such as the economically important <a href="/wiki/Elaeis_guineensis" title="Elaeis guineensis">oil palm</a>. It can cause serious damage to the developing <a href="/wiki/Frond" title="Frond">fronds</a> (leaves) up to death of the palm. The beetle breeds in decaying palm trunks or other organic matter like sawdust or compost heaps.<sup id="cite_ref-Bedford1980_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bedford1980-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Bedford2013_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bedford2013-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Oryctes_rhinoceros_male.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Oryctes_rhinoceros_male.jpg/250px-Oryctes_rhinoceros_male.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Oryctes_rhinoceros_male.jpg/500px-Oryctes_rhinoceros_male.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1200"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="silicon" term="silicon" wikidataID="Q670" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: silicon<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silicon">Silicon</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Silicon</b> (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/&#712;/: primary stress follows">&#712;</span><span title="'s' in 'sigh'">s</span><span title="/&#618;/: 'i' in 'kit'">&#618;</span><span title="'l' in 'lie'">l</span><span title="/./: syllable break">.</span><span title="/&#618;/: 'i' in 'kit'">&#618;</span><span title="/./: syllable break">.</span><span title="'k' in 'kind'">k</span><span title="/&#601;/: 'a' in 'about'">&#601;</span><span title="'n' in 'nigh'">n</span></span>/</a></span></span>, <a href="/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key" title="Help:Pronunciation respelling key"><i title="English pronunciation respelling"><span style="font-size:90%">SILL</span>-ih-k&#601;n</i></a>)<sup id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/Chemical_element" title="Chemical element">chemical element</a>; it has <a href="/wiki/Symbol_(chemistry)" class="mw-redirect" title="Symbol (chemistry)">symbol</a> <b>Si</b> and <a href="/wiki/Atomic_number" title="Atomic number">atomic number</a> 14. It is a hard, brittle crystalline solid with a blue-grey metallic lustre, and is a <a href="/wiki/Tetravalence" class="mw-redirect" title="Tetravalence">tetravalent</a> <a href="/wiki/Non-metal" class="mw-redirect" title="Non-metal">non-metal</a> (sometimes considered as a <a href="/wiki/Metalloid" title="Metalloid">metalloid</a>) and <a href="/wiki/Semiconductor" title="Semiconductor">semiconductor</a>. It is a member of <a href="/wiki/Carbon_group" title="Carbon group">group 14</a> in the periodic table: <a href="/wiki/Carbon" title="Carbon">carbon</a> is above it; and <a href="/wiki/Germanium" title="Germanium">germanium</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tin" title="Tin">tin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lead" title="Lead">lead</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Flerovium" title="Flerovium">flerovium</a> are below it. It is relatively unreactive. Silicon is a significant element that is essential for several physiological and metabolic processes in plants. Silicon is widely used as a semiconductor material in various electrical devices such as transistors, solar cells, and integrated circuits. It dominates semiconductor applications due to its low cost, excellent electronic properties, and adaptable physical characteristics. 
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:SiliconCroda.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="A lump of black reflective metal" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/SiliconCroda.jpg/250px-SiliconCroda.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="174" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/SiliconCroda.jpg/500px-SiliconCroda.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1046" data-file-height="727"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="oxysporum" term="oxysporum" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=oxysporum" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: oxysporum<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=oxysporum">oxysporum</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="random mating" term="random mating" wikidataID="Q967880" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_mating" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: random mating<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_mating">Random mating</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Panmixia</b> (or <b>panmixis</b>) means uniform random fertilization, which means individuals do not select a mate based on physical traits.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A panmictic population is one where all potential parents may contribute equally to the gamete pool, and that these gametes are uniformly distributed within the gamete population (gamodeme). This assumes that there are no hybridising restrictions within the parental population: neither <a href="/wiki/Genetics" title="Genetics">genetics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cytogenetics" title="Cytogenetics">cytogenetics</a> nor <a href="/wiki/Behavioural" class="mw-redirect" title="Behavioural">behavioural</a>; and neither spatial nor temporal (see also <a href="/wiki/Quantitative_genetics" title="Quantitative genetics">Quantitative genetics</a> for further discussion). True panmixia is rarely, if ever, observed in natural populations. It is a theoretical model used as a null hypothesis in population genetics. It serves as a point of comparison to understand how deviations from random mating affect allele and genotype frequencies.<a rel="nofollow" class="external autonumber" href="https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ece3.1149.">[1]</a> Therefore, all gamete recombination (fertilization) is uniformly possible. Both the <a href="/wiki/Wahlund_effect" title="Wahlund effect">Wahlund effect</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Hardy_Weinberg_equilibrium" class="mw-redirect" title="Hardy Weinberg equilibrium">Hardy Weinberg equilibrium</a> assume that the overall population is panmictic.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Pantala_flavescens-Kadavoor-2017-05-04-002.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Pantala_flavescens-Kadavoor-2017-05-04-002.jpg/250px-Pantala_flavescens-Kadavoor-2017-05-04-002.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Pantala_flavescens-Kadavoor-2017-05-04-002.jpg/500px-Pantala_flavescens-Kadavoor-2017-05-04-002.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4072" data-file-height="2715"></a><figcaption><i><a href="/wiki/Pantala_flavescens" title="Pantala flavescens">Pantala flavescens</a></i> is considered as a global panmictic population.</figcaption></figure>

<i> </i><span lang="grc"><a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%CE%BA%CF%85%CE%AC%CE%BD%CE%B5%CE%BF%CF%82#Ancient_Greek" class="extiw" lang="grc-Latn"><i>ku&#225;neos/kuano&#251;s</i></span>)</i>&#160;<span class="gloss-quot">'</span><span class="gloss-text">dark blue</span><span class="gloss-quot">'</span>), also called <b>anthocyans</b>, are <a href="/wiki/Solubility" title="Solubility">water-soluble</a> <a href="/wiki/Vacuole" title="Vacuole">vacuolar</a> <a href="/wiki/Pigment" title="Pigment">pigments</a> that, depending on their <a href="/wiki/PH" title="PH">pH</a>, may appear red, pink, purple, blue, or black. In 1835, the German pharmacist <a href="/wiki/Ludwig_Clamor_Marquart" title="Ludwig Clamor Marquart">Ludwig Clamor Marquart</a> named a chemical compound that gives flowers a blue color, Anthokyan, in his treatise <i>Die Farben der Bl&#252;then</i> (English: The Colors of Flowers). Food plants rich in anthocyanins include the blueberry, raspberry, <a href="/wiki/Black_rice" title="Black rice">black rice</a>, and black soybean, among many others that are red, pink, blue, purple, or black. Some of the colors of autumn leaves are derived from anthocyanins.<sup id="cite_ref-davies2004_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-davies2004-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-archetti2011_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-archetti2011-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

</div><p></p></div><div name="coconut oil" term="coconut oil" wikidataID="Q216235" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut_oil" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: coconut oil<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconut_oil">Coconut oil</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Coconut oil</b> (or <b>coconut fat</b>) is an edible oil derived from the meat of the <a href="/wiki/Coconut_palm" class="mw-redirect" title="Coconut palm">coconut palm</a> fruit.<sup id="cite_ref-tis_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tis-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-harv_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-harv-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Coconut oil is a white solid <a href="/wiki/Fat" title="Fat">fat</a> below around 25&#160;&#176;C (77&#160;&#176;F), and a clear thin liquid oil at higher temperatures. Unrefined varieties have a distinct coconut aroma.<sup id="cite_ref-harv_2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-harv-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Coconut oil is used as a food oil, and in industrial applications for <a href="/wiki/Cosmetics" title="Cosmetics">cosmetics</a> and <a href="/wiki/Detergent" title="Detergent">detergent</a> production.<sup id="cite_ref-tis_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tis-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-harv_2-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-harv-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The oil is rich in <a href="/wiki/Medium-chain_fatty_acid" class="mw-redirect" title="Medium-chain fatty acid">medium-chain fatty acids</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> 
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:9129Processing_and_cooking_of_coconut_healing_oil_in_the_Philippines_43.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/9129Processing_and_cooking_of_coconut_healing_oil_in_the_Philippines_43.jpg/250px-9129Processing_and_cooking_of_coconut_healing_oil_in_the_Philippines_43.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/9129Processing_and_cooking_of_coconut_healing_oil_in_the_Philippines_43.jpg/500px-9129Processing_and_cooking_of_coconut_healing_oil_in_the_Philippines_43.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4608" data-file-height="3456"></a><figcaption> Traditional (<span title="Tagalog-language text"><i lang="tl">lana</i></span>) extraction directly from <a href="/wiki/Coconut_milk" title="Coconut milk">the milk</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Philippines" title="Philippines">Philippines</a>. The process also produces <i><a href="/wiki/Latik" title="Latik">latik</a></i> (curds), used as a <a href="/wiki/Garnish_(food)" class="mw-redirect" title="Garnish (food)">garnish</a> in Filipino desserts. </figcaption></figure>

</p><p></p></div><div name="human health" term="human health" wikidataID="Q12147" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_health" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: human health<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_health">Human health</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">
<b>Health</b> has a variety of definitions, which have been used for different purposes over time. In general, it refers to physical and emotional <a href="/wiki/Well-being" title="Well-being">well-being</a>, especially that associated with normal functioning of the <a href="/wiki/Human_body" title="Human body">human body</a>, absent of <a href="/wiki/Disease" title="Disease">disease</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pain" title="Pain">pain</a> (including <a href="/wiki/Mental_pain" class="mw-redirect" title="Mental pain">mental pain</a>), or <a href="/wiki/Injury" title="Injury">injury</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Smallpox_eradication_team.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Smallpox_eradication_team.jpg/250px-Smallpox_eradication_team.jpg" decoding="async" width="240" height="233" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Smallpox_eradication_team.jpg/500px-Smallpox_eradication_team.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="700" data-file-height="681"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Donald_Henderson" title="Donald Henderson">Donald Henderson</a> as part of the CDC's <a href="/wiki/Smallpox" title="Smallpox">smallpox</a> eradication team in 1966</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="organic system" term="organic system" wikidataID="Q712378" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_system" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: organic system<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_system">Organic system</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In a multicellular <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organism</a>, an <b>organ</b> is a collection of <a href="/wiki/Tissue_(biology)" title="Tissue (biology)">tissues</a> joined in a structural unit to serve a common <a href="/wiki/Function_(biology)" title="Function (biology)">function</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In the <a href="/wiki/Biological_organization" class="mw-redirect" title="Biological organization">hierarchy of life</a>, an organ lies between <a href="/wiki/Tissue_(biology)" title="Tissue (biology)">tissue</a> and an <a href="/wiki/Organ_system" title="Organ system">organ system</a>. Tissues are formed from same type <a href="/wiki/Cell_(biology)" title="Cell (biology)">cells</a> to act together in a function. Tissues of different types combine to form an organ which has a specific function. The <a href="/wiki/Gastrointestinal_tract" title="Gastrointestinal tract">intestinal wall</a> for example is formed by <a href="/wiki/Epithelial_tissue" class="mw-redirect" title="Epithelial tissue">epithelial tissue</a> and <a href="/wiki/Smooth_muscle_tissue" class="mw-redirect" title="Smooth muscle tissue">smooth muscle tissue</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Kent_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kent-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Two or more organs working together in the execution of a specific body function form an organ system, also called a <a href="/wiki/Biological_system" title="Biological system">biological system</a> or body system.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Internal_organs.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Internal_organs.png/330px-Internal_organs.png" decoding="async" width="290" height="258" class="mw-file-element" term="organic farming" wikidataID="Q165647" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_farming" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: organic farming<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_farming">Organic farming</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Organic farming</b>, also known as <b>organic agriculture</b> or <b>ecological farming</b>, or <b>biological farming</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-eu_organic_labelling_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-eu_organic_labelling-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is an agricultural system that emphasizes the use of naturally occurring, non-synthetic inputs, such as compost <a href="/wiki/Manure" title="Manure">manure</a>, <a href="/wiki/Green_manure" title="Green manure">green manure</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Bone_meal" title="Bone meal">bone meal</a> and places emphasis on techniques such as <a href="/wiki/Crop_rotation" title="Crop rotation">crop rotation</a>, <a href="/wiki/Companion_planting" title="Companion planting">companion planting</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Mixed_farming" title="Mixed farming">mixed cropping</a>. <a href="/wiki/Biological_pest_control" title="Biological pest control">Biological pest control</a> methods, such as the fostering of insect predators, are also encouraged.<sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Organic agriculture can be defined as "an <a href="/wiki/Integrated_farming" title="Integrated farming">integrated farming</a> system that strives for <a href="/wiki/Sustainability" title="Sustainability">sustainability</a>, the enhancement of <a href="/wiki/Soil_fertility" title="Soil fertility">soil fertility</a> and <a href="/wiki/Biological_diversity" class="mw-redirect" title="Biological diversity">biological diversity</a> while, with rare exceptions, prohibiting synthetic pesticides, <a href="/wiki/Antibiotics" class="mw-redirect" title="Antibiotics">antibiotics</a>, synthetic fertilizers, <a href="/wiki/Genetically_modified_organisms" class="mw-redirect" title="Genetically modified organisms">genetically modified organisms</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Growth_hormones" class="mw-redirect" title="Growth hormones">growth hormones</a>".<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-10"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It originated early in the 20th century in reaction to rapidly changing farming practices. In 2019, the global area dedicated to certified organic agriculture amounted to 70&#160;million hectares (170&#160;million acres), with more than half of this area being in Australia.<sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
