Covering an area of 75,000&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (29,000&#160;sq&#160;mi), it traverses the <a href="/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India" title="States and union territories of India">states</a> of <a href="/wiki/Odisha" title="Odisha">Odisha</a>, <a href="/wiki/Telangana" title="Telangana">Telangana</a>, <a href="/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh" title="Andhra Pradesh">Andhra Pradesh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Karnataka" title="Karnataka">Karnataka</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Tamil_Nadu" title="Tamil Nadu">Tamil Nadu</a>. The range forms a discontinuous chain of mountains along the eastern edge of the <a href="/wiki/Deccan_Plateau" title="Deccan Plateau">Deccan Plateau</a>, stretching from north of the <a href="/wiki/Mahanadi_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Mahanadi River">Mahanadi River</a> in Odisha to <a href="/wiki/Vaigai_River" title="Vaigai River">Vaigai River</a> in Tamil Nadu at the southern end of the peninsula. The Eastern Ghats meet the <a href="/wiki/Western_Ghats" title="Western Ghats">Western Ghats</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Nilgiris" class="mw-redirect" title="Nilgiris">Nilgiris</a>. The average elevation is around 600&#160;m (2,000&#160;ft) and <a href="/wiki/Arma_Konda" title="Arma Konda">Arma Konda</a> is the highest peak in the mountains at 1,680&#160;m (5,510&#160;ft).
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Andhra_Pradesh_-_Landscapes_from_Andhra_Pradesh,_views_from_Indias_South_Central_Railway_(83).JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Andhra_Pradesh_-_Landscapes_from_Andhra_Pradesh%2C_views_from_Indias_South_Central_Railway_%2883%29.JPG/330px-Andhra_Pradesh_-_Landscapes_from_Andhra_Pradesh%2C_views_from_Indias_South_Central_Railway_%2883%29.JPG" decoding="async" width="272" height="58" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Andhra_Pradesh_-_Landscapes_from_Andhra_Pradesh%2C_views_from_Indias_South_Central_Railway_%2883%29.JPG/500px-Andhra_Pradesh_-_Landscapes_from_Andhra_Pradesh%2C_views_from_Indias_South_Central_Railway_%2883%29.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Andhra_Pradesh_-_Landscapes_from_Andhra_Pradesh%2C_views_from_Indias_South_Central_Railway_%2883%29.JPG/960px-Andhra_Pradesh_-_Landscapes_from_Andhra_Pradesh%2C_views_from_Indias_South_Central_Railway_%2883%29.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2880" data-file-height="610"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="East Indian arrowroot" term="East Indian arrowroot" wikidataID="Q3596013" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Indian_arrowroot" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: East Indian arrowroot<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Indian_arrowroot">East Indian arrowroot</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><i><b>Curcuma angustifolia</b></i> is one of over 80 species belonging to the genus <i><a href="/wiki/Curcuma" title="Curcuma">Curcuma</a></i> ,<sup id="cite_ref-paper3_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-paper3-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> in the family <a href="/wiki/Zingiberaceae" title="Zingiberaceae">Zingiberaceae</a>. This species is native to the <a href="/wiki/Indian_subcontinent" title="Indian subcontinent">Indian subcontinent</a> and is more commonly known as <b>East Indian arrowroot</b><sup id="cite_ref-grin_2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-grin-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> or <b>narrow-leaved turmeric</b> in <a href="/wiki/English_language" title="English language">English</a>, and is called "yaipan" in <a href="/wiki/Meiteilon" class="mw-redirect" title="Meiteilon">Manipuri</a>,  "Aipah" in <a href="/wiki/Thadou_language" title="Thadou language">Thadou-Kuki</a>, "tikhur" in <a href="/wiki/Bhojpuri_language" title="Bhojpuri language">Bhojpuri</a>, and "Koova" &#3349;&#3394;&#3381; in <a href="/wiki/Malayalam" title="Malayalam">Malayalam</a>/<a href="/wiki/Tamil_language" title="Tamil language">Tamil</a>, and is called "Kutupah" in <a href="/wiki/Poumai_Naga_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Poumai Naga language">Poula</a>. In the Eastern hemisphere, the plant plays an integral role in many cultures.<sup id="cite_ref-gbook_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gbook-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Indian_Medicinal_Plants_and_Drugs_Wellcome_L0032802.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Indian_Medicinal_Plants_and_Drugs_Wellcome_L0032802.jpg/250px-Indian_Medicinal_Plants_and_Drugs_Wellcome_L0032802.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="468" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Indian_Medicinal_Plants_and_Drugs_Wellcome_L0032802.jpg/500px-Indian_Medicinal_Plants_and_Drugs_Wellcome_L0032802.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2386" data-file-height="4470"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="Plant Biotechnology" term="Plant Biotechnology" wikidataID="Q788558" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_biotechnology" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Plant Biotechnology<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_biotechnology">Plant biotechnology</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b><a href="/wiki/Plant" title="Plant">Plant</a> breeding</b> is the science of changing the traits of <a href="/wiki/Plants" class="mw-redirect" title="Plants">plants</a> in order to produce desired characteristics.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is used to improve the quality of plant products for use by humans and animals.<sup id="cite_ref-Hartung-2014_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hartung-2014-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The goals of plant breeding are to produce crop varieties that boast unique and superior traits for a variety of applications. The most frequently addressed agricultural traits are those related to biotic and abiotic stress tolerance, grain or biomass yield, end-use quality characteristics such as taste or the concentrations of specific biological molecules (proteins, sugars, lipids, vitamins, fibers) and ease of processing (harvesting, milling, baking, malting, blending, etc.).<sup id="cite_ref-Willy-2010_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Willy-2010-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Wheat_selection_k10183-1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/29/Wheat_selection_k10183-1.jpg" decoding="async" width="252" height="189" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="252" data-file-height="189"></a><figcaption>The Yecoro <a href="/wiki/Wheat" title="Wheat">wheat</a> (right) <a href="/wiki/Cultivar" title="Cultivar">cultivar</a> is sensitive to salinity, plants resulting from a hybrid cross with cultivar W4910 (left) show greater tolerance to high salinity</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Eastern Uttar Pradesh" term="Eastern Uttar Pradesh" wikidataID="Q7261660" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Uttar_Pradesh" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Eastern Uttar Pradesh<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Uttar_Pradesh">Eastern Uttar Pradesh</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Purvanchal</b> (<abbr style="font-size:85%" title="literal translation">lit.</abbr><span style="white-space: nowrap;">&#8201;</span><span class="gloss-quot">'</span><span class="gloss-text">Eastern region</span><span class="gloss-quot">'</span>) is the region of eastern <a href="/wiki/Uttar_Pradesh" title="Uttar Pradesh">Uttar Pradesh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Purvanchal is also a proposed state in India, encompassing 32 eastern districts of Uttar Pradesh.&#160; The proposal, introduced in the <a href="/wiki/Uttar_Pradesh_Legislative_Assembly" title="Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly">Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly</a> in 2011 by then Chief Minister <a href="/wiki/Mayawati" title="Mayawati">Mayawati</a>, aimed to divide Uttar Pradesh into four smaller states for improved administration and governance.&#160; The proposal was rejected by the central government.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> 
</p>
<p></p></div><div name="Plant Health" term="Plant Health" wikidataID="Q30715232" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_health" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Plant Health<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_health">Plant health</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Plant health</b> includes the protection of plants, as well as scientific and regulatory frameworks for controlling plant pests or pathogens.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Plant health is concerned with:
</p>
<p></p></div><div name="Emamectin benzoate" term="Emamectin benzoate" wikidataID="Q5368875" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emamectin_benzoate" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Emamectin benzoate<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emamectin_benzoate">Emamectin benzoate</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Emamectin</b> is the 4&#8243;-deoxy-4&#8243;-methylamino derivative of <a href="/wiki/Abamectin" title="Abamectin">abamectin</a>, a 16-membered macrocyclic <a href="/wiki/Lactone" title="Lactone">lactone</a> produced by the fermentation of the soil <a href="/wiki/Actinomycete" class="mw-redirect" title="Actinomycete">actinomycete</a> <i>Streptomyces avermitilis</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ref7_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ref7-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
It is generally prepared as the <a href="/wiki/Salt_(chemistry)" title="Salt (chemistry)">salt</a> with <a href="/wiki/Benzoic_acid" title="Benzoic acid">benzoic acid</a>, emamectin benzoate, which is a white or faintly yellow powder.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  Emamectin is widely used in the US and Canada as an insecticide because of its chloride channel activation properties.<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

Those who study entomology are known as entomologists. In the past, the term <i>insect</i> was less specific, and historically the definition of entomology would also include the study of <a href="/wiki/Animal" title="Animal">animals</a> in other <a href="/wiki/Arthropod" title="Arthropod">arthropod</a> groups, such as <a href="/wiki/Arachnid" title="Arachnid">arachnids</a>, <a href="/wiki/Myriapod" class="mw-redirect" title="Myriapod">myriapods</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Crustaceans" class="mw-redirect" title="Crustaceans">crustaceans</a>. The field is also referred to as insectology in American English, while in British English insectology implies the study of the relationships between insects and humans.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

<p></p></div><div name="stem rust" term="stem rust" wikidataID="Q1342327" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_rust" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: stem rust<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stem_rust">Stem rust</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Stem rust</b>, also known as <b>cereal rust</b>, <b>black rust</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-Singh08_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Singh08-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Schumann00_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Schumann00-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <b>red rust</b> or <b>red dust</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-vincent2011_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-vincent2011-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is caused by the <a href="/wiki/Fungus" title="Fungus">fungus</a> <i><b>Puccinia graminis</b></i>, which causes significant disease in <a href="/wiki/Cereal" title="Cereal">cereal</a> crops. Crop species that are affected by the disease include <a href="/wiki/Bread_wheat" class="mw-redirect" title="Bread wheat">bread wheat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Durum" class="mw-redirect" title="Durum">durum wheat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Barley" title="Barley">barley</a> and <a href="/wiki/Triticale" title="Triticale">triticale</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Singh08_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Singh08-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> These diseases have affected cereal farming throughout history. The annual recurrence of stem rust of wheat in North Indian plains was discovered by K. C. Mehta.<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Since the 1950s, wheat strains bred to be resistant to stem rust have become available.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Fungicide" title="Fungicide">Fungicides</a> effective against stem rust are available as well.<sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Stem_rust_close_up.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Stem_rust_close_up.jpg/250px-Stem_rust_close_up.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="166" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Stem_rust_close_up.jpg/500px-Stem_rust_close_up.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2700" data-file-height="1795"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="DSMS" term="DSMS" wikidataID="Q281674" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DSMS" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: DSMS<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DSMS">DSMS</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">
A <b>data stream management system</b> (DSMS) is a computer <a href="/wiki/Software_system" title="Software system">software system</a> to manage continuous <a href="/wiki/Data_stream" title="Data stream">data streams</a>. It is similar to a <a href="/wiki/Database_management_system" class="mw-redirect" title="Database management system">database management system</a> (DBMS), which is, however, designed for static data in conventional <a href="/wiki/Database" title="Database">databases</a>. A DBMS also offers a flexible query processing so that the information needed can be expressed using queries. However, in contrast to a DBMS, a DSMS executes a <i>continuous query</i> that is not only performed once, but is permanently installed. Therefore, the query is continuously executed until it is explicitly uninstalled. Since most DSMS are data-driven, a continuous query produces new results as long as new data arrive at the system. This basic concept is similar to <a href="/wiki/Complex_event_processing" title="Complex event processing">complex event processing</a> so that both technologies are partially coalescing.
</p>

Some species are known by variants of the <a href="/wiki/Common_name" title="Common name">common name</a> "<a href="/wiki/Pigweed" title="Pigweed">pigweed</a>".<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Some members are <a href="/wiki/Annual_plant" title="Annual plant">annual</a> and others are <a href="/wiki/Perennial" title="Perennial">perennial</a>. The plant can grow from 1 to 2.5 metres (3 to 8 feet) tall with a <a href="/wiki/Succulent" class="mw-redirect" title="Succulent">succulent</a>, hollow stem. Parts of the plant vary from green to reddish. <a href="/wiki/Catkin" title="Catkin">Catkin</a>-like <a href="/wiki/Cymes" class="mw-redirect" title="Cymes">cymes</a> of densely packed flowers grow in the summer or fall.

There were no results matching the query.</p><p></p></div><div name="tribals" term="tribals" wikidataID="Q133311" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribals" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: tribals<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribals">Tribals</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The term <b>tribe</b> is used in many different contexts to refer to a category of <a href="/wiki/Human" title="Human">human</a> <a href="/wiki/Social_group" title="Social group">social group</a>. The predominant worldwide use of the term in <a href="/wiki/English_language" title="English language">English</a> is in the discipline of <a href="/wiki/Anthropology" title="Anthropology">anthropology</a>. The definition is contested, in part due to conflicting theoretical understandings of social and kinship structures, and also reflecting the problematic application of this concept to extremely diverse human societies. Its concept is often contrasted by anthropologists with other social and <a href="/wiki/Kinship" title="Kinship">kinship</a> groups, being hierarchically larger than a <a href="/wiki/Lineage_(anthropology)" title="Lineage (anthropology)">lineage</a> or <a href="/wiki/Clan" title="Clan">clan</a>, but smaller than a <a href="/wiki/Chiefdom" title="Chiefdom">chiefdom</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ethnicity" title="Ethnicity">ethnicity</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nation" title="Nation">nation</a> or <a href="/wiki/State_(polity)" title="State (polity)">state</a>. These terms are similarly disputed. In some cases tribes have legal recognition and some degree of political autonomy  from national or federal government, but this legalistic usage of the term may conflict with anthropological definitions.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:War_on_the_Plains_Comanche_vs_Osage_by_George_Catlin_1834.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/War_on_the_Plains_Comanche_vs_Osage_by_George_Catlin_1834.png/250px-War_on_the_Plains_Comanche_vs_Osage_by_George_Catlin_1834.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/War_on_the_Plains_Comanche_vs_Osage_by_George_Catlin_1834.png/500px-War_on_the_Plains_Comanche_vs_Osage_by_George_Catlin_1834.png 1.5x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1352"></a><figcaption>Tribal war on the plains. <a href="/wiki/Comanche" title="Comanche">Comanche</a> (right) trying to lance an <a href="/wiki/Osage_Nation" title="Osage Nation">Osage</a> warrior. </div><p></p></div><div name="borer" term="borer" wikidataID="Q893499" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borer" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: borer<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borer">Borer</a></p><p></p></div><div name="branch office" term="branch office" wikidataID="Q1880737" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch_office" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: branch office<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch_office">Branch office</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>branch office</b> is an outlet of a company or, more generally, an organization that &#8211; unlike a <a href="/wiki/Subsidiary" title="Subsidiary">subsidiary</a> &#8211; does not constitute a separate legal entity, while being physically separated from the organization's main office.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Branching is particularly widespread in <a href="/wiki/Branch_(banking)" title="Branch (banking)">banking</a> and other financial institutions, where the products' complexity requires local offices to act more like an agency than as a separate company. A branch structure exposes the owning company to full <a href="/wiki/Taxable_income" title="Taxable income">taxability</a> and <a href="/wiki/Legal_liability" title="Legal liability">legal liability</a> in regard to the branch office's operations.
</p>

The notion of particle size applies to particles in <a href="/wiki/Colloid" title="Colloid">colloids</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Particle_(ecology)" title="Particle (ecology)">ecology</a>, in <a href="/wiki/Granular_material" title="Granular material">granular material</a> (whether <a href="/wiki/Particulates" class="mw-redirect" title="Particulates">airborne</a> or not), and to particles that form a granular material (see also <a href="/wiki/Grain_size" title="Grain size">grain size</a>).

Founded in 1936,<sup id="cite_ref-Milestones_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Milestones-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> it operates under the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Information_and_Broadcasting_(India)" title="Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (India)">Ministry of Information and Broadcasting</a> and is one of the two divisions of <a href="/wiki/Prasar_Bharati" title="Prasar Bharati">Prasar Bharati</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Headquartered at the <i>Akashvani Bhavan</i> in New Delhi, it houses the Drama Section, FM Section, and National Service. It also serves as the home of the Indian television station Doordarshan Kendra.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Akhashvani_logo.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/7/7b/Akhashvani_logo.png/250px-Akhashvani_logo.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="221" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/7/7b/Akhashvani_logo.png 1.5x" data-file-width="336" data-file-height="297"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="parasitoids" term="parasitoids" wikidataID="Q595663" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitoids" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: parasitoids<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitoids">Parasitoids</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Evolutionary_ecology" title="Evolutionary ecology">evolutionary ecology</a>, a <b>parasitoid</b> is an <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organism</a> that lives in close association with its <a href="/wiki/Host_(biology)" title="Host (biology)">host</a> at the host's expense, eventually resulting in the death of the host. Parasitoidism is one of six major <a href="/wiki/Evolutionarily_stable_strategy" title="Evolutionarily stable strategy">evolutionary strategies</a> within <a href="/wiki/Parasitism" title="Parasitism">parasitism</a>, distinguished by the fatal <a href="/wiki/Prognosis" title="Prognosis">prognosis</a> for the host, which makes the strategy close to <a href="/wiki/Predation" title="Predation">predation</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:CSIRO_ScienceImage_2357_Spotted_alfalfa_aphid_being_attacked_by_parasitic_wasp.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/CSIRO_ScienceImage_2357_Spotted_alfalfa_aphid_being_attacked_by_parasitic_wasp.jpg/330px-CSIRO_ScienceImage_2357_Spotted_alfalfa_aphid_being_attacked_by_parasitic_wasp.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="206" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/CSIRO_ScienceImage_2357_Spotted_alfalfa_aphid_being_attacked_by_parasitic_wasp.jpg/500px-CSIRO_ScienceImage_2357_Spotted_alfalfa_aphid_being_attacked_by_parasitic_wasp.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/CSIRO_ScienceImage_2357_Spotted_alfalfa_aphid_being_attacked_by_parasitic_wasp.jpg/960px-CSIRO_ScienceImage_2357_Spotted_alfalfa_aphid_being_attacked_by_parasitic_wasp.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1772" data-file-height="1219"></a><figcaption>A <a href="/wiki/Parasitoid_wasp" title="Parasitoid wasp">parasitoid wasp</a> (<i>Trioxys complanatus</i>, <a href="/wiki/Aphidiinae" title="Aphidiinae">Aphidiinae</a>) <a href="/wiki/Ovipositing" class="mw-redirect" title="Ovipositing">ovipositing</a> into the body of a spotted alfalfa <a href="/wiki/Aphid" title="Aphid">aphid</a> (<i>Therioaphis maculata</i>, <a href="/wiki/Calaphidinae" title="Calaphidinae">Calaphidinae</a>), a behaviour that is used in <a href="/wiki/Biological_pest_control" title="Biological pest control">biological pest control</a><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>

The  external examiner system originated in 1832 with the establishment of the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Durham" class="mw-redirect" title="University of Durham">University of Durham</a>, and was then adopted by other British universities in the 19th century before spreading to other countries.

The term is sometimes written with a subscript, as <b>F<sub>1</sub> hybrid</b>.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Subsequent generations are called <b>F<sub>2</sub></b>, <b>F<sub>3</sub></b>, etc.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Kissing_Savannahs.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Kissing_Savannahs.jpg/250px-Kissing_Savannahs.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="259" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Kissing_Savannahs.jpg/500px-Kissing_Savannahs.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="695" data-file-height="720"></a><figcaption>Two <a href="/wiki/Savannah_cat" title="Savannah cat">savannah cats</a>, a hybrid between the <a href="/wiki/Domestic_cat" class="mw-redirect" title="Domestic cat">domestic cat</a> (<i>Felis catus</i>) and the <a href="/wiki/Serval" title="Serval">serval</a> (<i>Leptailurus serval</i>). </div><p></p></div><div name="genetic variability" term="genetic variability" wikidataID="Q1374271" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variability" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: genetic variability<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_variability">Genetic variability</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">
<b>Genetic variability</b> is either the presence of, or the generation of, genetic differences. It is defined as "the formation of individuals differing in <a href="/wiki/Genotype" title="Genotype">genotype</a>, or the presence of genotypically different individuals, in contrast to environmentally induced differences which, as a rule, cause only temporary, nonheritable changes of the <a href="/wiki/Phenotype" title="Phenotype">phenotype</a>."<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Genetic variability in a <a href="/wiki/Population" title="Population">population</a> promotes <a href="/wiki/Biodiversity" title="Biodiversity">biodiversity</a>, as it ensures that no two living things are exactly alike.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> While many factors can cause genetic variability, some factors can also decrease genetic variability.
</p><p></p></div><div name="GP" term="GP" wikidataID="Q223811" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GP" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: GP<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GP">GP</a></p><p></p></div><div name="Orchids" term="Orchids" wikidataID="Q25308" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchids" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Orchids<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchids">Orchids</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Orchids</b> are plants that belong to the <a href="/wiki/Family_(biology)" title="Family (biology)">family</a> <b>Orchidaceae</b> (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/&#716;/: secondary stress follows">&#716;</span><span title="/&#596;&#720;r/: 'ar' in 'war'">&#596;&#720;r</span><span title="'k' in 'kind'">k</span><span title="/&#618;/: 'i' in 'kit'">&#618;</span><span title="/&#712;/: primary stress follows">&#712;</span><span title="'d' in 'dye'">d</span><span title="/e&#618;/: 'a' in 'face'">e&#618;</span><span title="'s' in 'sigh'">s</span><span title="/i/: 'y' in 'happy'">i</span><span title="/./: syllable break">.</span><span title="/i&#720;/: 'ee' in 'fleece'">i&#720;</span></span>,<span class="wrap"> </span>-<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="'s' in 'sigh'">s</span><span title="/i/: 'y' in 'happy'">i</span><span title="/./: syllable break">.</span><span title="/a&#618;/: 'i' in 'tide'">a&#618;</span></span>/</a></span></span>),<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> a diverse and widespread group of <a href="/wiki/Flowering_plant" title="Flowering plant">flowering plants</a> with blooms that are often colourful and fragrant. Orchids are <a href="/wiki/Cosmopolitan_distribution" title="Cosmopolitan distribution">cosmopolitan</a> plants, living in diverse habitats on every continent except Antarctica. The world's <a href="/wiki/Species_richness" title="Species richness">richest</a> diversity of orchid genera and species is in the <a href="/wiki/Tropics" title="Tropics">tropics</a>. Many species are <a href="/wiki/Epiphyte" title="Epiphyte">epiphytes</a>, living on trees. The flowers and their pollination mechanisms are highly specialized, attracting insect pollinators by colour, pattern, scent, pheromones, and sometimes by <a href="/wiki/Mimicry_in_plants" title="Mimicry in plants">mimicking female insects</a>. Orchids have very small seeds, relying on fungal partners for germination. Some orchids have no leaves, either photosynthesizing with their roots or relying entirely on fungal partners for food.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Plant_Orchid_Cymbidium_aloifolium_P1110661_05_-_cropped.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Plant_Orchid_Cymbidium_aloifolium_P1110661_05_-_cropped.jpg/250px-Plant_Orchid_Cymbidium_aloifolium_P1110661_05_-_cropped.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="250" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Plant_Orchid_Cymbidium_aloifolium_P1110661_05_-_cropped.jpg/500px-Plant_Orchid_Cymbidium_aloifolium_P1110661_05_-_cropped.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2000" data-file-height="2000"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="urea formaldehyde" term="urea formaldehyde" wikidataID="Q146537" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urea_formaldehyde" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: urea formaldehyde<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urea_formaldehyde">Urea formaldehyde</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Urea-formaldehyde</b> (<b>UF</b>), also known as <b>urea-methanal</b>, so named for its common synthesis pathway and overall structure,<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/Transparency_(optics)" class="mw-redirect" title="Transparency (optics)">nontransparent</a> <a href="/wiki/Thermosetting_polymer" title="Thermosetting polymer">thermosetting polymer</a>.  It is produced from <a href="/wiki/Urea" title="Urea">urea</a> and <a href="/wiki/Formaldehyde" title="Formaldehyde">formaldehyde</a>. These resins are used in <a href="/wiki/Adhesives" class="mw-redirect" title="Adhesives">adhesives</a>, <a href="/wiki/Plywood" title="Plywood">plywood</a>, <a href="/wiki/Particle_board" title="Particle board">particle board</a>, <a href="/wiki/Medium-density_fibreboard" title="Medium-density fibreboard">medium-density fibreboard</a> (MDF), and molded objects. In agriculture, urea-formaldehyde compounds are one of the most commonly used types of <a href="/wiki/Controlled-release_fertilizer" class="mw-redirect" title="Controlled-release fertilizer">slow-release fertilizer</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Guo_2018_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Guo_2018-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:UFresinSyn.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/UFresinSyn.svg/330px-UFresinSyn.svg.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="138" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/UFresinSyn.svg/500px-UFresinSyn.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/UFresinSyn.svg/960px-UFresinSyn.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="2894" data-file-height="1333"></a><figcaption>Two steps in formation of urea-formaldehyde resin</figcaption></figure>

</div><p></p></div><div name="irrigation" term="irrigation" wikidataID="Q11453" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrigation" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: irrigation<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrigation">Irrigation</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Irrigation</b> is the practice of applying controlled amounts of <a href="/wiki/Water" title="Water">water</a> to <a href="/wiki/Land" title="Land">land</a> to help grow <a href="/wiki/Crop" title="Crop">crops</a>, <a href="/wiki/Landscape_plant" class="mw-redirect" title="Landscape plant">landscape plants</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Lawn" title="Lawn">lawns</a>. Irrigation has been a key aspect of <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a> for over 5,000 years and has been developed by many cultures around the world. Irrigation helps to grow crops, maintain landscapes, and <a href="/wiki/Revegetation" title="Revegetation">revegetate</a> disturbed soils in dry areas and during times of below-average rainfall. In addition to these uses, irrigation is also employed to protect crops from <a href="/wiki/Frost" title="Frost">frost</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> suppress <a href="/wiki/Weed" title="Weed">weed</a> growth in <a href="/wiki/Grain" title="Grain">grain</a> fields, and prevent <a href="/wiki/Soil_consolidation" title="Soil consolidation">soil consolidation</a>. It is also used to cool <a href="/wiki/Livestock" title="Livestock">livestock</a>, reduce <a href="/wiki/Dust" title="Dust">dust</a>, dispose of <a href="/wiki/Sewage" title="Sewage">sewage</a>, and support <a href="/wiki/Mining" title="Mining">mining</a> operations. <a href="/wiki/Drainage" class="mw-redirect" title="Drainage">Drainage</a>, which involves the removal of surface and sub-surface water from a given location, is often studied in conjunction with irrigation.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Fields_SW_from_Sevilla.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Fields_SW_from_Sevilla.jpg/250px-Fields_SW_from_Sevilla.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Fields_SW_from_Sevilla.jpg/500px-Fields_SW_from_Sevilla.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="5100" data-file-height="3400"></a><figcaption>Irrigation of agricultural fields in <a href="/wiki/Andalusia" title="Andalusia">Andalusia</a>, Spain. It is the most important of the commercially available products of neem, and is a potent <a href="/wiki/Pesticide" title="Pesticide">pesticide</a> used in organic farming.

</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:US_Patent_cover_(US_Patent_5,860,492).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/US_Patent_cover_%28US_Patent_5%2C860%2C492%29.jpg/250px-US_Patent_cover_%28US_Patent_5%2C860%2C492%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="371" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/US_Patent_cover_%28US_Patent_5%2C860%2C492%29.jpg/500px-US_Patent_cover_%28US_Patent_5%2C860%2C492%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3114" data-file-height="4620"></a><figcaption>A patent issued by the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Patent_and_Trademark_Office" title="United States Patent and Trademark Office">U.S. Patent and Trademark Office</a></figcaption></figure>

Although fungi are <a href="/wiki/Eukaryotic" class="mw-redirect" title="Eukaryotic">eukaryotic</a>, many pathogenic fungi are <a href="/wiki/Microorganism" title="Microorganism">microorganisms</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-SanBlasCalderone_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SanBlasCalderone-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Approximately 300 fungi are pathogenic to humans;<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> their study is called "<b>medical mycology</b>". Fungal infections are estimated to kill more people than either <a href="/wiki/Tuberculosis" title="Tuberculosis">tuberculosis</a> or <a href="/wiki/Malaria" title="Malaria">malaria</a>&#8212;about two million people per year.<sup id="cite_ref-geddes_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-geddes-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Candida_pap_1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Candida_pap_1.jpg/250px-Candida_pap_1.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Candida_pap_1.jpg/500px-Candida_pap_1.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4272" data-file-height="2848"></a><figcaption>Candida. <a href="/wiki/Pap_test" title="Pap test">Pap test</a> specimen. <a href="/wiki/Pap_stain" class="mw-redirect" title="Pap stain">Pap stain</a>.</figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="pathogen" term="pathogen" wikidataID="Q170065" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogen" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: pathogen<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogen">Pathogen</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a>, a <b>pathogen</b> (<a href="/wiki/Greek_language" title="Greek language">Greek</a>: <span lang="el">&#960;&#940;&#952;&#959;&#962;</span>, <span title="Greek-language romanization"><i lang="el-Latn">pathos</i></span> "suffering", "passion" and <span title="Greek-language text"><span lang="el">-&#947;&#949;&#957;&#942;&#962;</span></span>, <span title="Greek-language romanization"><i lang="el-Latn">-gen&#275;s</i></span> "producer of"), in the oldest and broadest sense, is any <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organism</a>, agent or <a href="/wiki/Micro-organism" class="mw-redirect" title="Micro-organism">micro-organism</a> that can produce <a href="/wiki/Disease" title="Disease">disease</a>. A pathogen may also be referred to as an <b>infectious agent</b>, or simply a <b><a href="/wiki/Germ_theory_of_disease" title="Germ theory of disease">germ</a></b>.<sup id="cite_ref-pmid5050429_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pmid5050429-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Shigella_stool.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Shigella_stool.jpg/330px-Shigella_stool.jpg" decoding="async" width="273" height="178" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Shigella_stool.jpg/500px-Shigella_stool.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Shigella_stool.jpg/700px-Shigella_stool.jpg 2x" data-file-width="700" data-file-height="457"></a><figcaption>A photomicrograph of a stool that has shigella dysentery. These bacteria typically cause foodborne illness.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="fungicide" term="fungicide" wikidataID="Q193237" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungicide" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: fungicide<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungicide">Fungicide</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Fungicides</b> are <a href="/wiki/Pesticide" title="Pesticide">pesticides</a> used to kill <a href="/wiki/Parasitic_fungi" class="mw-redirect" title="Parasitic fungi">parasitic fungi</a> or their <a href="/wiki/Spore" title="Spore">spores</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-KO_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-KO-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ullmann_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ullmann-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  Fungi can cause serious damage in <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a>, resulting in losses of yield and quality. Fungicides are used both in agriculture and to fight <a href="/wiki/Fungal_infections_in_animals" class="mw-redirect" title="Fungal infections in animals">fungal infections in animals</a>, including humans. Fungicides are also used to control <a href="/wiki/Oomycetes" class="mw-redirect" title="Oomycetes">oomycetes</a>, which are not <a href="/wiki/Taxonomy" title="Taxonomy">taxonomically</a>/genetically fungi, although sharing similar methods of infecting plants. Fungicides can either be contact, translaminar or systemic. Contact fungicides are not taken up into the plant tissue and protect only the plant where the spray is deposited. Translaminar fungicides redistribute the fungicide from the upper, sprayed leaf surface to the lower, unsprayed surface. Systemic fungicides are taken up and redistributed through the xylem vessels. Few fungicides move to all parts of a plant. Some are locally systemic, and some move upward.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Similar_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Similar-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg/120px-Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg.png" decoding="async" width="120" height="81" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg/250px-Captan_Structural_Formula_V.1.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="389" data-file-height="261"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Captan" title="Captan">Captan</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Phthalimide" title="Phthalimide">phthalimide</a>, is a major commercial fungicide.</figcaption></figure></div><p></p></div><div name="sugarcane agriculture" term="sugarcane agriculture" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=sugarcane%20agriculture" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: sugarcane agriculture<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=sugarcane%20agriculture">sugarcane agriculture</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

It grows primarily in <a href="/wiki/Tropical_climate" title="Tropical climate">tropical climates</a> and is commonly found in the Indian states where it forms a part of the local cuisine. <i>Coccinia grandis</i> is cooked as a vegetable dish.

</p>
<p></p></div><div name="Niger" term="Niger" wikidataID="Q1032" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Niger<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger">Niger</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Niger</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-14" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-14"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> officially the <b>Republic of Niger</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>b<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a <a href="/wiki/Landlocked_country" title="Landlocked country">landlocked country</a> in <a href="/wiki/West_Africa" title="West Africa">West Africa</a>. It is a <a href="/wiki/Unitary_state" title="Unitary state">unitary state</a> bordered by <a href="/wiki/Libya" title="Libya">Libya</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Libya%E2%80%93Niger_border" title="Libya&#8211;Niger border">northeast</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chad" title="Chad">Chad</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Chad%E2%80%93Niger_border" title="Chad&#8211;Niger border">east</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nigeria" title="Nigeria">Nigeria</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Niger%E2%80%93Nigeria_border" title="Niger&#8211;Nigeria border">south</a>, <a href="/wiki/Benin" title="Benin">Benin</a> and <a href="/wiki/Burkina_Faso" title="Burkina Faso">Burkina Faso</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Benin-Niger_border" class="mw-redirect" title="Benin-Niger border">southwest</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mali" title="Mali">Mali</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Mali%E2%80%93Niger_border" title="Mali&#8211;Niger border">west</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Algeria" title="Algeria">Algeria</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Algeria%E2%80%93Niger_border" title="Algeria&#8211;Niger border">northwest</a>. It covers a land area of almost 1.27&#160;million&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (490,000&#160;mi<sup>2</sup>), making it the largest landlocked country in West Africa and the second-largest landlocked nation in Africa behind Chad. Over 80% of its land area lies in the <a href="/wiki/Sahara" title="Sahara">Sahara</a>. Its <a href="/wiki/Islam_in_Niger" title="Islam in Niger">predominantly Muslim population</a> of about 25 million<sup id="cite_ref-UN_WPP_16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UN_WPP-16"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-UN_WPP_2022_17-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UN_WPP_2022-17"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> lives mostly in clusters in the south and west of the country. The capital, <a href="/wiki/Niamey" title="Niamey">Niamey</a>, is located in Niger's southwest corner along the namesake <a href="/wiki/Niger_River" title="Niger River">Niger River</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg/250px-1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="156" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg/500px-1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1680" data-file-height="1050"></a><figcaption>Rock engraving showing herds of giraffe, <a href="/wiki/Ibex" title="Ibex">ibex</a>, and other animals in the southern Sahara near Tiguidit, Niger</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Novaluron" term="Novaluron" wikidataID="Q1900206" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novaluron" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Novaluron<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novaluron">Novaluron</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Novaluron</b>, or <b>(&#177;)-1-[3-chloro-4-(1,1,2-trifluoro-2-trifluoro- methoxyethoxy)phenyl]-3-(2,6-difluorobenzoyl)urea</b>, is a chemical with <a href="/wiki/Pesticide" title="Pesticide">pesticide</a> properties, belonging to the class of <a href="/wiki/Insecticides" class="mw-redirect" title="Insecticides">insecticides</a> called <a href="/wiki/Insect_growth_regulator" title="Insect growth regulator">insect growth regulators</a>. It is a <a href="/wiki/Benzoylurea" class="mw-redirect" title="Benzoylurea">benzoylphenyl urea</a> developed by <i>Makhteshim-Agan Industries Ltd.</i>. In the <a href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</a>, the compound has been used on food crops, including apples, potatoes, brassicas, ornamentals, and cotton. Patents and registrations have been approved or are ongoing in several other countries throughout <a href="/wiki/Europe" title="Europe">Europe</a>, <a href="/wiki/Asia" title="Asia">Asia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Africa" title="Africa">Africa</a>, <a href="/wiki/South_America" title="South America">South America</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Australia" title="Australia">Australia</a>. The US <a href="/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency" title="United States Environmental Protection Agency">Environmental Protection Agency</a> and the Canadian <a href="/wiki/Pest_Management_Regulatory_Agency" title="Pest Management Regulatory Agency">Pest Management Regulatory Agency</a> consider novaluron to pose low risk to the environment and non-target organisms and value it as an important option for <a href="/wiki/Integrated_pest_management" title="Integrated pest management">integrated pest management</a> that should decrease reliance on <a href="/wiki/Organophosphorus" class="mw-redirect" title="Organophosphorus">organophosphorus</a>, <a href="/wiki/Carbamate" title="Carbamate">carbamate</a> and <a href="/wiki/Pyrethroid" title="Pyrethroid">pyrethroid</a> insecticides.<sup id="cite_ref-JunqueraHosking2019_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-JunqueraHosking2019-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-www.epa.gov_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-www.epa.gov-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<p></p></div><div name="ISO 9001" term="ISO 9001" wikidataID="Q206008" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_9001" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: ISO 9001<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_9001">ISO 9001</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>ISO 9000 family</b> is a set of <a href="/wiki/International_standard" title="International standard">international standards</a> for <a href="/wiki/Quality_management_system" title="Quality management system">quality management systems</a>. It was developed in March 1987 by the <a href="/wiki/International_Organization_for_Standardization" title="International Organization for Standardization">International Organization for Standardization</a>. The goal of these standards is to help <a href="/wiki/Organizations" class="mw-redirect" title="Organizations">organizations</a> ensure that they meet <a href="/wiki/Customer" title="Customer">customer</a> and other <a href="/wiki/Stakeholder_(corporate)" title="Stakeholder (corporate)">stakeholder</a> needs within the statutory and regulatory requirements related to a product or service. The standards were designed to fit into an integrated management system.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The ISO refers to the set of standards as a "family", bringing together the standard for quality management systems and a set of "supporting standards",<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and their presentation as a family facilitates their integrated application within an organisation.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> ISO 9000 deals with the fundamentals and vocabulary of QMS,<sup id="cite_ref-Tsim,_Yeung,_Leung_2002_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tsim,_Yeung,_Leung_2002-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> including the seven <a href="/wiki/Quality_management" title="Quality management">quality management</a> principles that underlie the family of standards.<sup id="cite_ref-Tsim,_Yeung,_Leung_2002_4-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tsim,_Yeung,_Leung_2002-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-iso.org_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-iso.org-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> ISO 9001 deals with the requirements that organizations wishing to meet the standard must fulfill.<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A companion document, ISO/TS 9002, provides guidelines for the application of ISO 9001.<sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> ISO 9004 gives guidance on achieving sustained organizational success.<sup id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>) is a comprehensive <a href="/wiki/International_agreement" class="mw-redirect" title="International agreement">international agreement</a> in harmony with the <a href="/wiki/Convention_on_Biological_Diversity" title="Convention on Biological Diversity">Convention on Biological Diversity</a>, which aims at guaranteeing <a href="/wiki/Food_security" title="Food security">food security</a> through the <a href="/wiki/Conservation_ethic" class="mw-redirect" title="Conservation ethic">conservation</a>, exchange and <a href="/wiki/Sustainable_use" class="mw-redirect" title="Sustainable use">sustainable use</a> of the world's <a href="/wiki/Plant_genetic_resources" title="Plant genetic resources">plant genetic resources</a> for food and agriculture (PGRFA), the fair and equitable benefit sharing arising from its use, as well as the recognition of <a href="#Farmers'_rights">farmers' rights</a>. It was signed in 2001 in Madrid, and entered into force on 29 June 2004.

The rind is usually the <a href="/wiki/Botany" title="Botany">botanical</a> <a href="/wiki/Exocarp" class="mw-redirect" title="Exocarp">exocarp</a>, but the term exocarp also includes the hard cases of <a href="/wiki/Nut_(fruit)" title="Nut (fruit)">nuts</a>, which are not named peels since they are not peeled off by hand or peeler, but rather <a href="/wiki/Nutshell" title="Nutshell">shells</a> because of their hardness.

</div><p></p></div><div name="pH range" term="pH range" wikidataID="Q40936" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PH_range" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: pH range<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PH_range">PH range</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Chemistry" title="Chemistry">chemistry</a>, <b>pH</b> (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="'p' in 'pie'">p</span><span title="/i&#720;/: 'ee' in 'fleece'">i&#720;</span><span title="/&#712;/: primary stress follows">&#712;</span><span title="'h' in 'hi'">h</span><span title="/e&#618;/: 'a' in 'face'">e&#618;</span><span title="/t&#643;/: 'ch' in 'China'">t&#643;</span></span>/</a></span></span> or <span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="'p' in 'pie'">p</span><span title="/i&#720;/: 'ee' in 'fleece'">i&#720;</span><span title="/&#712;/: primary stress follows">&#712;</span><span title="/e&#618;/: 'a' in 'face'">e&#618;</span><span title="/t&#643;/: 'ch' in 'China'">t&#643;</span></span>/</a></span></span>;  <a href="/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key" title="Help:Pronunciation respelling key"><i title="English pronunciation respelling">pee-<span style="font-size:90%">AYCH</span></i></a>) is a <a href="/wiki/Logarithmic_scale" title="Logarithmic scale">logarithmic scale</a> used to specify the <a href="/wiki/Acid" title="Acid">acidity</a> or <a href="/wiki/Base_(chemistry)" title="Base (chemistry)">basicity</a> of <a href="/wiki/Aqueous_solution" title="Aqueous solution">aqueous solutions</a>. Acidic solutions (solutions with higher concentrations of hydrogen (<a href="/wiki/Hydrogen_ion#Cation_(positively_charged)" title="Hydrogen ion"><style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1123817410">'"`UNIQ--templatestyles-0000000E-QINU`"'</style><span class="chemf nowrap">H<sup class="template-chem2-sup">+</sup></span></a>) <a href="/wiki/Cation" class="mw-redirect" title="Cation">cations</a>) are measured to have lower pH values than basic or <a href="/wiki/Alkali" title="Alkali">alkaline</a> solutions. While the origin of the symbol 'pH' can be traced back to its original inventor, and the 'H' refers clearly to hydrogen, the exact original meaning of the letter 'p' in pH is still disputed; it has since acquired a more general technical meaning that is used in numerous other contexts.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:0_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:PH_scale_3.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/PH_scale_3.jpg/250px-PH_scale_3.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="188" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/PH_scale_3.jpg/500px-PH_scale_3.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="3024"></a><figcaption>Test tubes containing solutions of pH 1&#8211;10 colored with <a href="/wiki/Universal_indicator" title="Universal indicator">an indicator</a></figcaption></figure>

Government officials that qualify as lawyers (jurist) in certain countries can get the title Legal Adviser.
</p><p></p></div><div name="Intellectual Property Rights" term="Intellectual Property Rights" wikidataID="Q131257" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_Property_Rights" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Intellectual Property Rights<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_Property_Rights">Intellectual Property Rights</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Intellectual property</b> (<b>IP</b>) is a category of <a href="/wiki/Property" title="Property">property</a> that includes intangible creations of the human intellect.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> There are many types of intellectual property, and some countries recognize more than others.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The best-known types are <a href="/wiki/Patent" title="Patent">patents</a>, <a href="/wiki/Copyright" title="Copyright">copyrights</a>, <a href="/wiki/Trademark" title="Trademark">trademarks</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Trade_secret" title="Trade secret">trade secrets</a>. The modern concept of intellectual property was developed in <a href="/wiki/England" title="England">England</a> in the 17th and 18th centuries. The term "intellectual property" began to be used in the 19th century, though it was not until the late 20th century that intellectual property became commonplace in most of the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_national_legal_systems" title="List of national legal systems">legal systems</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Lemley_2005_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Lemley_2005-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Nike,_McDonald%E2%80%99s_copyright_infringing_sandals_in_China.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Nike%2C_McDonald%E2%80%99s_copyright_infringing_sandals_in_China.jpg/250px-Nike%2C_McDonald%E2%80%99s_copyright_infringing_sandals_in_China.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="310" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Nike%2C_McDonald%E2%80%99s_copyright_infringing_sandals_in_China.jpg/500px-Nike%2C_McDonald%E2%80%99s_copyright_infringing_sandals_in_China.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1765" data-file-height="2190"></a><figcaption>Intellectual property laws such as trademark laws forbid the sale of infringing goods like these "<a href="/wiki/McDonald%27s" title="McDonald's">McDnoald's</a>" [<i><a href="/wiki/Sic" title="Sic">sic</a></i>] and "<a href="/wiki/Nike,_Inc." title="Nike, Inc.">NKIE</a>"  [<i><a href="/wiki/Sic" title="Sic">sic</a></i>] <a href="/wiki/Sandal" title="Sandal">sandals</a> from <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a>.</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="textiles" term="textiles" wikidataID="Q28823" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textiles" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: textiles<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Textiles">Textiles</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Textile</b> is an <a href="/wiki/Hyponymy_and_hypernymy" class="mw-redirect" title="Hyponymy and hypernymy">umbrella term</a> that includes various <a href="/wiki/Fiber" title="Fiber">fibre-based</a> materials, including fibres, <a href="/wiki/Yarn" title="Yarn">yarns</a>, <a href="/wiki/Staple_(textiles)#Filament_fiber" title="Staple (textiles)">filaments</a>, <a href="/wiki/Thread_(yarn)" title="Thread (yarn)">threads</a>, and different types of <a href="#Fabric">fabric</a>. in which case it is also called <b>bio-business</b><sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> or <b>bio-enterprise</b>. 
The primary goal of agribusiness is to <a href="/wiki/Profit_maximization" title="Profit maximization">maximize profit</a> while satisfying the needs of consumers for products related to <a href="/wiki/Renewable_resource" title="Renewable resource">natural resources</a>. Agribusinesses comprise <a href="/wiki/Farm" title="Farm">farms</a>, <a href="/wiki/Food_security" title="Food security">food</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fiber" title="Fiber">fiber</a> processing, <a href="/wiki/Forestry" title="Forestry">forestry</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fishery" title="Fishery">fisheries</a>, <a href="/wiki/Biotechnology" title="Biotechnology">biotechnology</a> and <a href="/wiki/Biofuel" title="Biofuel">biofuel</a> enterprises and their input suppliers.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Typical-value-Chain.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Typical-value-Chain.png/500px-Typical-value-Chain.png" decoding="async" width="340" height="159" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Typical-value-Chain.png/960px-Typical-value-Chain.png 1.5x" data-file-width="3214" data-file-height="1506"></a><figcaption>Value chain representation</figcaption></figure>

It is a commercially successful branch of <a href="/wiki/Horticulture" title="Horticulture">horticulture</a> and <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a> found throughout the world. Efficient production practices have been developed over the years, for the hundreds of plant taxa used in the <a href="/wiki/Floral_industry" title="Floral industry">floral industry</a>, increasing the overall knowledge of whole plant biology. <a href="/wiki/Plant_breeding" title="Plant breeding">Plant breeding</a> and selection have produced tens of thousands of new genotypes for human use.
</p>

</div><p></p></div><div name="sugar industry" term="sugar industry" wikidataID="Q227870" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_industry" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: sugar industry<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_industry">Sugar industry</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>sugar industry</b> subsumes the production, <a href="/wiki/Sugar_refinery" title="Sugar refinery">processing</a> and marketing of <a href="/wiki/Sugars" class="mw-redirect" title="Sugars">sugars</a> (mostly <a href="/wiki/Sucrose" title="Sucrose">sucrose</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fructose" title="Fructose">fructose</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-Ullmann_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ullmann-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  In 2017, worldwide production of table sugar amounted to 185 million tonnes.<sup id="cite_ref-prod2017_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-prod2017-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

</div><p></p></div><div name="China" term="China" wikidataID="Q148" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: China<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China">China</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>China</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>h<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> officially the <b>People's Republic of China</b> (<b>PRC</b>),<sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>i<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is a country in <a href="/wiki/East_Asia" title="East Asia">East Asia</a>. It is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_population_(United_Nations)" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by population (United Nations)">second-most populous country</a> after <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>, with <a href="/wiki/Population_of_China" class="mw-redirect" title="Population of China">a population</a> exceeding 1.4 billion, representing 17% of the world's population. China <a href="/wiki/Borders_of_China" title="Borders of China">borders fourteen countries by land</a><sup id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>j<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> across an area of 9.6&#160;million square kilometers (3,700,000&#160;sq&#160;mi), making it the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area" title="List of countries and dependencies by area">third-largest country by area</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>k<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The country is divided into 33 <a href="/wiki/Province-level_divisions_of_China" title="Province-level divisions of China">province-level divisions</a>: 22 <a href="/wiki/Provinces_of_China" title="Provinces of China">provinces</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>l<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> 5 <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_regions_of_China" title="Autonomous regions of China">autonomous regions</a>, 4 <a href="/wiki/Direct-administered_municipalities_of_China" class="mw-redirect" title="Direct-administered municipalities of China">municipalities</a>, and 2 semi-autonomous <a href="/wiki/Special_administrative_regions" class="mw-redirect" title="Special administrative regions">special administrative regions</a>. <a href="/wiki/Beijing" title="Beijing">Beijing</a> is the capital, while <a href="/wiki/Shanghai" title="Shanghai">Shanghai</a> is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_China_by_population" title="List of cities in China by population">most populous city by urban area</a> and largest <a href="/wiki/Financial_center" class="mw-redirect" title="Financial center">financial center</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:CHN_orthographic.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/CHN_orthographic.svg/250px-CHN_orthographic.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="250" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/CHN_orthographic.svg/500px-CHN_orthographic.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="550" data-file-height="550"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="abiotic stress" term="abiotic stress" wikidataID="Q4667893" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abiotic_stress" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: abiotic stress<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abiotic_stress">Abiotic stress</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Abiotic stress</b> is the negative impact of non-living factors on the living organisms in a specific environment.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>  The non-living variable must influence the environment beyond its normal range of variation to adversely affect the population performance or individual physiology of the organism in a significant way.<sup id="cite_ref-vine_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-vine-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Sunflowers_in_fields.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Sunflowers_in_fields.jpg/250px-Sunflowers_in_fields.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="167" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Sunflowers_in_fields.jpg/500px-Sunflowers_in_fields.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="4272" data-file-height="2848"></a><figcaption>Sunflowers are hyperaccumulator plants that can absorb large amount of metal.</figcaption></figure>

It is headed by the <a href="/wiki/Secretary_of_agriculture" class="mw-redirect" title="Secretary of agriculture">secretary of agriculture</a>, who reports directly to the <a href="/wiki/President_of_the_United_States" title="President of the United States">president of the United States</a> and is a member of the president's <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States" title="Cabinet of the United States">Cabinet</a>. The current secretary is <a href="/wiki/Brooke_Rollins" title="Brooke Rollins">Brooke Rollins</a>, who has served since February 13, 2025.
</p>

</div><p></p></div><div name="Botany" term="Botany" wikidataID="Q441" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Botany<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany">Botany</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Botany</b>, also called <b>phytology</b> or <b>plant science</b>, is the branch of <a href="/wiki/Natural_science" title="Natural science">natural science</a> and <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a> that studies <a href="/wiki/Plants" class="mw-redirect" title="Plants">plants</a>, especially <a href="/wiki/Plant_anatomy" title="Plant anatomy">their anatomy</a>, <a href="/wiki/Plant_taxonomy" title="Plant taxonomy">taxonomy</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Plant_ecology" title="Plant ecology">ecology</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A <b>botanist</b> or <b>plant scientist</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Scientist" title="Scientist">scientist</a> who specialises in this field. "<a href="/wiki/Plant" title="Plant">Plant</a>" and "botany" may be defined more narrowly to include only <a href="/wiki/Land_plants" class="mw-redirect" title="Land plants">land plants</a> and their study, which is also known as <b>phytology</b>. Phytologists or botanists (in the strict sense) study approximately 410,000 <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> of <a href="/wiki/Embryophyte" title="Embryophyte">land plants</a>, including some 391,000 species of <a href="/wiki/Vascular_plant" title="Vascular plant">vascular plants</a> (of which approximately 369,000 are <a href="/wiki/Flowering_plant" title="Flowering plant">flowering plants</a>)<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERGB_Kew2016_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERGB_Kew2016-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and approximately 20,000 <a href="/wiki/Bryophyte" title="Bryophyte">bryophytes</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEThe_Plant_List2013_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThe_Plant_List2013-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Myris_fragr_Fr_080112-3294_ltn.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Image of ripe nutmeg fruit split open to show red aril" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Myris_fragr_Fr_080112-3294_ltn.jpg/330px-Myris_fragr_Fr_080112-3294_ltn.jpg" decoding="async" width="310" height="273" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Myris_fragr_Fr_080112-3294_ltn.jpg/500px-Myris_fragr_Fr_080112-3294_ltn.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Myris_fragr_Fr_080112-3294_ltn.jpg/960px-Myris_fragr_Fr_080112-3294_ltn.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1300" data-file-height="1144"></a><figcaption>The fruit of <i><a href="/wiki/Myristica_fragrans" title="Myristica fragrans">Myristica fragrans</a></i>, a species native to <a href="/wiki/Indonesia" title="Indonesia">Indonesia</a>, is the source of two valuable spices, the red aril (<a href="/wiki/Mace_(spice)" class="mw-redirect" title="Mace (spice)">mace</a>) enclosing the dark brown <a href="/wiki/Nutmeg" title="Nutmeg">nutmeg</a>.</figcaption></figure>

Like its relative the <a href="/wiki/Mung_bean" title="Mung bean">mung bean</a>, it has been reclassified from the genus <i><a href="/wiki/Phaseolus" title="Phaseolus">Phaseolus</a></i> to <i><a href="/wiki/Vigna" title="Vigna">Vigna</a></i>. The product sold as black gram is usually the whole urad bean, whereas the split bean (the interior being white) is called <b>white lentil</b>. It should not be confused with the much smaller true black <a href="/wiki/Lentil" title="Lentil">lentil</a> (<i>Lens culinaris</i>).

It contained about 13 <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Tomato" title="Tomato">tomato</a> group of nightshades. First removed from the genus <i><a href="/wiki/Solanum" title="Solanum">Solanum</a></i> by <a href="/wiki/Philip_Miller" title="Philip Miller">Philip Miller</a> in 1754, its removal leaves the latter genus <a href="/wiki/Paraphyly" title="Paraphyly">paraphyletic</a>, so modern botanists generally accept the names in <i>Solanum</i>. The name <i>Lycopersicon</i> (from <a href="/wiki/Greek_language" title="Greek language">Greek</a> <i>&#955;&#965;&#954;&#959;&#960;&#941;&#961;&#963;&#953;&#954;&#959;&#957;</i> meaning "wolf peach") is a reference to German folklore about members of the nightshade family being used to summon werewolves,<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and still used by gardeners, farmers, and seed companies. Collectively, the species in this group apart from the common cultivated plant are called <b>wild tomatoes</b>.
