Some cankers are of only minor consequence, but others are ultimately lethal and therefore can have major economic implications for <a href="/wiki/Agriculture" title="Agriculture">agriculture</a> and <a href="/wiki/Horticulture" title="Horticulture">horticulture</a>. Their causes include a wide range of organisms such as <a href="/wiki/Fungus" title="Fungus">fungi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bacterium" class="mw-redirect" title="Bacterium">bacteria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mycoplasma" title="Mycoplasma">mycoplasmas</a> and <a href="/wiki/Virus" title="Virus">viruses</a>. The majority of canker-causing organisms are bound to a unique host <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> or <a href="/wiki/Genus" title="Genus">genus</a>, but a few will attack other plants. Weather (via frost or windstorm damage) and animal damage can also cause stress to the plant resulting in cankers. Other causes of cankers is pruning when the bark is wet or using un-sterilized tools.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Butternut_canker.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Butternut_canker.jpg/250px-Butternut_canker.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="363" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Butternut_canker.jpg/500px-Butternut_canker.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="2976"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Ophiognomonia_clavigignenti-juglandacearum" title="Ophiognomonia clavigignenti-juglandacearum">Butternut canker</a> is a lethal disease of <a href="/wiki/Butternut_(tree)" class="mw-redirect" title="Butternut (tree)">butternut</a> trees, and has no cure.</figcaption></figure>

The <b>production of seed</b> is a multibillion-dollar global business, which uses growing facilities and growing locations worldwide. While most of the seed is produced by large specialist growers, large amounts are also produced by small growers who produce only one to a few crop types. The larger companies supply seed both to commercial resellers and wholesalers. The resellers and wholesalers sell to vegetable and fruit growers, and to companies who package seed into packets and sell them on to the amateur gardener.

</div><p></p></div><div name="cation" term="cation" wikidataID="Q36496" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cation" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: cation<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cation">Cation</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">An <b>ion</b> (<span class="rt-commentedText nowrap"><span class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt" lang="en-fonipa"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/&#712;/: primary stress follows">&#712;</span><span title="/a&#618;/: 'i' in 'tide'">a&#618;</span><span title="/./: syllable break">.</span><span title="/&#594;/: 'o' in 'body'">&#594;</span><span title="'n' in 'nigh'">n</span></span>,<span class="wrap"> </span>-<span style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><span title="/&#601;n/: 'on' in 'button'">&#601;n</span></span>/</a></span></span>)<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is an <a href="/wiki/Atom" title="Atom">atom</a> or <a href="/wiki/Molecule" title="Molecule">molecule</a> with a net <a href="/wiki/Electrical_charge" class="mw-redirect" title="Electrical charge">electrical charge</a>. The charge of an <a href="/wiki/Electron" title="Electron">electron</a> is considered to be negative by convention and this charge is equal and opposite to the charge of a <a href="/wiki/Proton" title="Proton">proton</a>, which is considered to be positive by convention. The net charge of an ion is not zero because its total number of electrons is unequal to its total number of protons.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ionic_bonding.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/Ionic_bonding.svg/330px-Ionic_bonding.svg.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="133" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/Ionic_bonding.svg/500px-Ionic_bonding.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/Ionic_bonding.svg/960px-Ionic_bonding.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="354"></a><figcaption>Electron transfer from a neutral <a href="/wiki/Lithium" title="Lithium">lithium</a> (Li) atom on the left to a neutral <a href="/wiki/Fluorine" title="Fluorine">fluorine</a> (F) atom on the right would give <a href="/wiki/Lithium_ion" class="mw-redirect" title="Lithium ion">Li<sup>+</sup></a> and <a href="/wiki/Fluoride_ion" class="mw-redirect" title="Fluoride ion">F<sup>&#8722;</sup></a> ions.</figcaption></figure>

Established in 1906 in <a href="/wiki/Mangalore" class="mw-redirect" title="Mangalore">Mangalore</a> by <a href="/wiki/Ammembal_Subba_Rao_Pai" title="Ammembal Subba Rao Pai">Ammembal Subba Rao Pai</a>, the bank was <a href="/wiki/Nationalized" class="mw-redirect" title="Nationalized">nationalized</a> in 1969. Canara Bank also has offices in <a href="/wiki/London" title="London">London</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dubai" title="Dubai">Dubai</a> and <a href="/wiki/New_York_City" title="New York City">New York</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

The seeds are sold fresh or preserved through <a href="/wiki/Drying" title="Drying">drying</a> (a <i>pulse</i>). Beans have been cultivated since the seventh millennium BCE in Thailand, and since the second millennium BCE in Europe and in Peru. Most beans, with the exception of peas, are summer crops. As legumes, the plants <a href="/wiki/Nitrogen_fixation" title="Nitrogen fixation">fix nitrogen</a> and form seeds with a high protein content. They are produced on a scale of millions of tons annually in many countries; India is the largest producer.

More generally, the term <i>seed</i> means anything that can be <a href="/wiki/Sowing" title="Sowing">sown</a>, which may include seed and <a href="/wiki/Husk" title="Husk">husk</a> or <a href="/wiki/Tuber" title="Tuber">tuber</a>. Seeds are the product of the ripened <a href="/wiki/Ovule" title="Ovule">ovule</a>, after the <a href="/wiki/Embryo_sac" class="mw-redirect" title="Embryo sac">embryo sac</a> is <a href="/wiki/Fertilization" class="mw-redirect" title="Fertilization">fertilized</a> by <a href="/wiki/Pollen" title="Pollen">sperm</a> from <a href="/wiki/Pollen" title="Pollen">pollen</a>, forming a <a href="/wiki/Zygote" title="Zygote">zygote</a>. The embryo within a seed develops from the zygote and grows within the mother plant to a certain size before growth is halted.

Originally native to <a href="/wiki/Central_Indo-Pacific" title="Central Indo-Pacific">Central Indo-Pacific</a>, they are ubiquitous in coastal tropical regions.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg/250px-Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="253" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg/330px-Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg/500px-Coconut_half_exocarp_removed.jpg 2x" data-file-width="6000" data-file-height="8000"></a><figcaption>Fruit with husk partly removed, showing hard thin shell of <a href="/wiki/Endocarp" class="mw-redirect" title="Endocarp">endocarp</a> (left), <a href="/wiki/Coir" title="Coir">coir</a> fibre of exocarp (right)</figcaption></figure>

<p></p></div><div name="antioxidants" term="antioxidants" wikidataID="Q133948" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antioxidants" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: antioxidants<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antioxidants">Antioxidants</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Antioxidants</b> are <a href="/wiki/Chemical_compound" title="Chemical compound">compounds</a> that inhibit <a href="/wiki/Redox" title="Redox">oxidation</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Chemical_reaction" title="Chemical reaction">chemical reaction</a> that can produce <a href="/wiki/Radical_(chemistry)" title="Radical (chemistry)">free radicals</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-lpi_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lpi-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Autoxidation" title="Autoxidation">Autoxidation</a> leads to degradation of organic compounds, including living matter.<sup id="cite_ref-Autox_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Autox-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Antioxidants are frequently added to industrial products, such as <a href="/wiki/Polymer" title="Polymer">polymers</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fuel" title="Fuel">fuels</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Lubricant" title="Lubricant">lubricants</a>, to extend their usable lifetimes.<sup id="cite_ref-Ullmann_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ullmann-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Foods are also treated with antioxidants to prevent <a href="/wiki/Food_spoilage" title="Food spoilage">spoilage</a>, in particular the <a href="/wiki/Rancidification" title="Rancidification">rancidification</a> of <a href="/wiki/Vegetable_oil" title="Vegetable oil">oils</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fat" title="Fat">fats</a>. In <a href="/wiki/Cell_(biology)" title="Cell (biology)">cells</a>, antioxidants such as <a href="/wiki/Glutathione" title="Glutathione">glutathione</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mycothiol" title="Mycothiol">mycothiol</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Bacillithiol" title="Bacillithiol">bacillithiol</a>, and enzyme systems like <a href="/wiki/Superoxide_dismutase" title="Superoxide dismutase">superoxide dismutase</a>, inhibit damage from <a href="/wiki/Oxidative_stress" title="Oxidative stress">oxidative stress</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size skin-invert-image" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Glutathione-skeletal.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Glutathione-skeletal.svg/250px-Glutathione-skeletal.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="78" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Glutathione-skeletal.svg/500px-Glutathione-skeletal.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="512" data-file-height="160"></a><figcaption>Structure of the antioxidant <a href="/wiki/Glutathione" title="Glutathione">glutathione</a></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="population" term="population" wikidataID="Q2625603" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: population<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population">Population</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</a>, a <b>population</b> of <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organisms</a> is a group of individuals of the same <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a>, defined by a discontinuity or <a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/disjunction" class="extiw" title="wikt:disjunction">disjunction</a> from other groups of individuals in certain characteristics, such as living area, genetic attributes, demographic structure.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Among biologists, the term definition varies, in some cases significantly, and sometimes those variations can be confusing.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> There are also plenty of other terms to describe groups of individuals if no clear <a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/disjunction" class="extiw" title="wikt:disjunction">disjunction</a> is present.<sup id="cite_ref-:1_1-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Commonly, a population can be described by what individuals constitute the population, its size, a geographical area it occupies, and the time within which the population is examined.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In <a href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/qualitative" class="extiw" title="wikt:qualitative">qualitative</a> terms, it is usually defined like "a group of organisms of the same species occupying a particular space at a particular time".<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:3_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p></p></div><div name="Tamil Nadu Agricultural University" term="Tamil Nadu Agricultural University" wikidataID="Q3522654" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu_Agricultural_University" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu_Agricultural_University">Tamil Nadu Agricultural University</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Tamil Nadu Agricultural University</b> (<b>TNAU</b>) is the state owned Public agricultural university of Tamil Nadu<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Headquartered in <a href="/wiki/Coimbatore" title="Coimbatore">Coimbatore</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tamil_Nadu" title="Tamil Nadu">Tamil Nadu</a>, India. Most manure consists of animal <a href="/wiki/Feces" title="Feces">feces</a>; other sources include <a href="/wiki/Compost" title="Compost">compost</a> and <a href="/wiki/Green_manure" title="Green manure">green manure</a>. Manures contribute to the <a href="/wiki/Soil_fertility" title="Soil fertility">fertility of soil</a> by adding organic matter and <a href="/wiki/Nutrients" class="mw-redirect" title="Nutrients">nutrients</a>, such as <a href="/wiki/Nitrogen" title="Nitrogen">nitrogen</a>, that are utilised by <a href="/wiki/Bacteria" title="Bacteria">bacteria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fungus" title="Fungus">fungi</a>, and other organisms in the <a href="/wiki/Soil" title="Soil">soil</a>. Higher organisms then feed on the fungi and bacteria in a chain of life that comprises the <a href="/wiki/Soil_food_web" title="Soil food web">soil food web</a>.
</p>

Phytologists or botanists (in the strict sense) study approximately 410,000 <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> of <a href="/wiki/Embryophyte" title="Embryophyte">land plants</a>, including some 391,000 species of <a href="/wiki/Vascular_plant" title="Vascular plant">vascular plants</a> (of which approximately 369,000 are <a href="/wiki/Flowering_plant" title="Flowering plant">flowering plants</a>)<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTERGB_Kew2016_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTERGB_Kew2016-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and approximately 20,000 <a href="/wiki/Bryophyte" title="Bryophyte">bryophytes</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEThe_Plant_List2013_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThe_Plant_List2013-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

Phytoplasmas were discovered in 1967 by Japanese scientists who termed them <b>mycoplasma-like organisms</b>.<sup id="cite_ref-Doi_et_al._3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Doi_et_al.-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Since their discovery, phytoplasmas have resisted all attempts at <i><a href="/wiki/In_vitro" title="In vitro">in vitro</a></i> culture in any cell-free medium; routine cultivation in an artificial medium thus remains a major challenge. Phytoplasmas are characterized by the lack of a <a href="/wiki/Cell_wall" title="Cell wall">cell wall</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Pleomorphism_(microbiology)" title="Pleomorphism (microbiology)">pleiomorphic</a> or <a href="/wiki/Filamentation" title="Filamentation">filamentous</a> shape, a diameter normally less than 1&#160;<a href="/wiki/Micrometre" title="Micrometre">&#956;m</a>, and a very small <a href="/wiki/Genome" title="Genome">genome</a>.

<p></p></div><div name="split plot design" term="split plot design" wikidataID="Q7316306" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split_plot_design" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: split plot design<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split_plot_design">Split plot design</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">In <a href="/wiki/Statistics" title="Statistics">statistics</a>, <b>restricted randomization</b> occurs in the <a href="/wiki/Design_of_experiments" title="Design of experiments">design of experiments</a> and in particular in the context of <a href="/wiki/Randomized_experiment" title="Randomized experiment">randomized experiments</a> and <a href="/wiki/Randomized_controlled_trial" title="Randomized controlled trial">randomized controlled trials</a>. Restricted randomization allows intuitively poor allocations of treatments to experimental units to be avoided, while retaining the theoretical benefits of randomization.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> For example, in a <a href="/wiki/Clinical_trial" title="Clinical trial">clinical trial</a> of a new proposed treatment of obesity compared to a control, an  experimenter would want to avoid outcomes of the randomization in which the new treatment was allocated only to the heaviest patients.
</p><p></p></div><div name="Setaria italica" term="Setaria italica" wikidataID="Q161211" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Setaria_italica" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Setaria italica<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Setaria_italica">Setaria italica</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Foxtail millet</b>, <a href="/wiki/Scientific_name" class="mw-redirect" title="Scientific name">scientific name</a> <i><b>Setaria italica</b></i> (synonym <i>Panicum italicum</i> L.), is an annual grass grown for human food. It is the second-most widely planted species of <a href="/wiki/Millet" title="Millet">millet</a> and the most grown millet species in Asia. The oldest evidence of foxtail millet cultivation was found along the ancient course of the <a href="/wiki/Yellow_River" title="Yellow River">Yellow River</a> in <a href="/wiki/Cishan_culture" title="Cishan culture">Cishan, China</a>, <a href="/wiki/Carbon_date" class="mw-redirect" title="Carbon date">carbon dated</a> to be from around 8,000 years before present.

It is a <a href="/wiki/Unitary_state" title="Unitary state">unitary state</a> bordered by <a href="/wiki/Libya" title="Libya">Libya</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Libya%E2%80%93Niger_border" title="Libya&#8211;Niger border">northeast</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chad" title="Chad">Chad</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Chad%E2%80%93Niger_border" title="Chad&#8211;Niger border">east</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nigeria" title="Nigeria">Nigeria</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Niger%E2%80%93Nigeria_border" title="Niger&#8211;Nigeria border">south</a>, <a href="/wiki/Benin" title="Benin">Benin</a> and <a href="/wiki/Burkina_Faso" title="Burkina Faso">Burkina Faso</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Benin-Niger_border" class="mw-redirect" title="Benin-Niger border">southwest</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mali" title="Mali">Mali</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Mali%E2%80%93Niger_border" title="Mali&#8211;Niger border">west</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Algeria" title="Algeria">Algeria</a> to the <a href="/wiki/Algeria%E2%80%93Niger_border" title="Algeria&#8211;Niger border">northwest</a>. It covers a land area of almost 1.27&#160;million&#160;km<sup>2</sup> (490,000&#160;mi<sup>2</sup>), making it the largest landlocked country in West Africa and the second-largest landlocked nation in Africa behind Chad. Over 80% of its land area lies in the <a href="/wiki/Sahara" title="Sahara">Sahara</a>. Its <a href="/wiki/Islam_in_Niger" title="Islam in Niger">predominantly Muslim population</a> of about 25 million<sup id="cite_ref-UN_WPP_16-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UN_WPP-16"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-UN_WPP_2022_17-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UN_WPP_2022-17"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> lives mostly in clusters in the south and west of the country. The capital, <a href="/wiki/Niamey" title="Niamey">Niamey</a>, is located in Niger's southwest corner along the namesake <a href="/wiki/Niger_River" title="Niger River">Niger River</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg/250px-1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="156" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg/500px-1997_278-10_Sahara_glyph.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1680" data-file-height="1050"></a><figcaption>Rock engraving showing herds of giraffe, <a href="/wiki/Ibex" title="Ibex">ibex</a>, and other animals in the southern Sahara near Tiguidit, Niger</figcaption></figure>

It can have varying levels of <a href="/wiki/Pungency" title="Pungency">heat</a>, but the peppers used for hot paprika tend to be milder and have thinner flesh than those used to produce <a href="/wiki/Chili_powder" title="Chili powder">chili powder</a>. The milder, sweet paprika is mostly composed of the fruit of the pepper with most of the seeds removed; whereas some seeds and stalks are retained in the peppers used for hotter paprika.

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="quarantine" term="quarantine" wikidataID="Q182899" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarantine" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: quarantine<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarantine">Quarantine</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>quarantine</b> is a restriction on the <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_movement" title="Freedom of movement">movement of people</a>, animals, and goods which is intended to prevent the spread of <a href="/wiki/Disease" title="Disease">disease</a> or <a href="/wiki/Pest_(organism)" title="Pest (organism)">pests</a>. It is often used in connection to disease and illness, preventing the movement of those who may have been exposed to a <a href="/wiki/Infection" title="Infection">communicable disease</a>, yet do not have a confirmed <a href="/wiki/Medical_diagnosis" title="Medical diagnosis">medical diagnosis</a>. It is distinct from <a href="/wiki/Isolation_(health_care)" title="Isolation (health care)">medical isolation</a>, in which those confirmed to be infected with a communicable disease are isolated from the healthy population.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Coat_of_arms_of_Great_Britain_(1707%E2%80%931714).svg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="coat of arms" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Coat_of_arms_of_Great_Britain_%281707%E2%80%931714%29.svg/250px-Coat_of_arms_of_Great_Britain_%281707%E2%80%931714%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="140" height="140" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Coat_of_arms_of_Great_Britain_%281707%E2%80%931714%29.svg/330px-Coat_of_arms_of_Great_Britain_%281707%E2%80%931714%29.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1550" data-file-height="1550"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="Stress Management" term="Stress Management" wikidataID="Q1404268" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_Management" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Stress Management<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_Management">Stress Management</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Stress management</b>  includes a range of methods that can help individuals cope with stress and improve overall well-being, although results can vary depending on the person or situation. It also consists of a wide spectrum of techniques and <a href="/wiki/Psychotherapy" title="Psychotherapy">psychotherapies</a> aimed at controlling a person's level of <a href="/wiki/Psychological_stress" title="Psychological stress">psychological stress</a>, especially <a href="/wiki/Chronic_stress" title="Chronic stress">chronic stress</a>, generally for the purpose of improving the function of everyday life. Stress produces numerous physical and mental symptoms which vary according to each individual's situational factors. These can include a decline in physical health, such as headaches, chest pain, fatigue, <a href="/wiki/Psychological_stress_and_sleep" title="Psychological stress and sleep">sleep problems</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Depression_(mood)" title="Depression (mood)">depression</a>. The process of stress management is a key factor that can lead to a happy and successful life in modern society.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
. Stress management provides numerous ways to manage anxiety and maintain overall well-being.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Transactional_Model_of_Stress_and_Coping_-_Richard_Lazarus.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Transactional_Model_of_Stress_and_Coping_-_Richard_Lazarus.svg/250px-Transactional_Model_of_Stress_and_Coping_-_Richard_Lazarus.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="400" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Transactional_Model_of_Stress_and_Coping_-_Richard_Lazarus.svg/500px-Transactional_Model_of_Stress_and_Coping_-_Richard_Lazarus.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="500" data-file-height="800"></a><figcaption>Transactional Model of Stress and Coping of Richard Lazarus</figcaption></figure></div><p></p></div><div name="insects" term="insects" wikidataID="Q1390" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insects" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: insects<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insects">Insects</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Insects</b> (from <a href="/wiki/Latin" title="Latin">Latin</a> <i><span title="Latin-language text"><i lang="la">insectum</i></span></i>) are <a href="/wiki/Hexapoda" title="Hexapoda">hexapod</a> <a href="/wiki/Invertebrate" title="Invertebrate">invertebrates</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Class_(biology)" title="Class (biology)">class</a> <b>Insecta</b>. They are the largest group within the <a href="/wiki/Arthropod" title="Arthropod">arthropod</a> <a href="/wiki/Phylum" title="Phylum">phylum</a>. Insects have a <a href="/wiki/Chitin" title="Chitin">chitinous</a> <a href="/wiki/Exoskeleton" title="Exoskeleton">exoskeleton</a>, a three-part body (<a href="/wiki/Insect_morphology#Head" title="Insect morphology">head</a>, <a href="/wiki/Thorax_(insect_anatomy)" class="mw-redirect" title="Thorax (insect anatomy)">thorax</a> and <a href="/wiki/Abdomen_(insect_anatomy)" class="mw-redirect" title="Abdomen (insect anatomy)">abdomen</a>), three pairs of jointed <a href="/wiki/Arthropod_leg" title="Arthropod leg">legs</a>, <a href="/wiki/Compound_eye" title="Compound eye">compound eyes</a>, and a pair of <a href="/wiki/Antenna_(biology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Antenna (biology)">antennae</a>. Insects are the most diverse group of animals, with more than a million described <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a>; they represent more than half of all animal species. 
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Insects_-_Neoptera_-_Paleoptera_-_Apterygota.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Insects_-_Neoptera_-_Paleoptera_-_Apterygota.jpg/250px-Insects_-_Neoptera_-_Paleoptera_-_Apterygota.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="373" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Insects_-_Neoptera_-_Paleoptera_-_Apterygota.jpg/500px-Insects_-_Neoptera_-_Paleoptera_-_Apterygota.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="812" data-file-height="1210"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="PGPR strains" term="PGPR strains" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=PGPR%20strains" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: PGPR strains<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=PGPR%20strains">PGPR strains</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="termites" term="termites" wikidataID="Q546583" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Termites" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: termites<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Termites">Termites</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Termites</b> are a group of <a href="/wiki/Detritivore" title="Detritivore">detritophagous</a> <a href="/wiki/Eusociality" title="Eusociality">eusocial</a> <a href="/wiki/Cockroach" title="Cockroach">cockroaches</a><sup id="cite_ref-x911_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-x911-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-t038_4-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-t038-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-d918_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-d918-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-m647_6-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-m647-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> which consume a variety of <a href="/wiki/Detritus" title="Detritus">decaying plant material</a>, generally in the form of <a href="/wiki/Wood" title="Wood">wood</a>, <a href="/wiki/Plant_litter" title="Plant litter">leaf litter</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Humus" title="Humus">soil humus</a>. They are distinguished by their moniliform antennae and the soft-bodied, unpigmented worker caste for which they have been commonly termed "<b>white ants</b>";<sup id="cite_ref-:1_7-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> however, they are not <a href="/wiki/Ant" title="Ant">ants</a> but highly <a href="/wiki/Apomorphy_and_synapomorphy" title="Apomorphy and synapomorphy">derived</a> cockroaches.<sup id="cite_ref-inward_8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-inward-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> About 2,997 extant <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> are currently described, 2,125 of which are members of the family <a href="/wiki/Termitidae" title="Termitidae">Termitidae</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Coptotermes_formosanus_shiraki_USGov_k8204-7.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Coptotermes_formosanus_shiraki_USGov_k8204-7.jpg/250px-Coptotermes_formosanus_shiraki_USGov_k8204-7.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="375" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Coptotermes_formosanus_shiraki_USGov_k8204-7.jpg/500px-Coptotermes_formosanus_shiraki_USGov_k8204-7.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1799" data-file-height="2700"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="International Treaty" term="International Treaty" wikidataID="Q131569" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_treaty" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: International Treaty<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_treaty">International treaty</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>treaty</b> is a recorded international agreement between <a href="/wiki/Sovereign_state" title="Sovereign state">sovereign states</a> or other subjects of international law (including <a href="/wiki/International_organization" title="International organization">international organizations</a>) that is governed by <a href="/wiki/International_law" title="International law">international law</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A treaty may also be known as an <b>international agreement</b>, <b>protocol</b>, <b>covenant</b>, <b>convention</b>, <b>pact</b>, or <b>exchange of letters</b>, among other terms; however, only documents that are legally binding on the parties are considered treaties under international law.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Treaties may be bilateral (between two countries) or multilateral (involving more than two countries). 
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Treaty_of_Kadesh.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Treaty_of_Kadesh.jpg/250px-Treaty_of_Kadesh.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="319" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Treaty_of_Kadesh.jpg/330px-Treaty_of_Kadesh.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Treaty_of_Kadesh.jpg/500px-Treaty_of_Kadesh.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2154" data-file-height="3617"></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Egyptian%E2%80%93Hittite_peace_treaty" title="Egyptian&#8211;Hittite peace treaty">Egyptian&#8211;Hittite peace treaty</a>, on display at the <a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Archaeology_Museum" class="mw-redirect" title="Istanbul Archaeology Museum">Istanbul Archaeology Museum</a>, was for a long time believed to be the earliest example of any written international agreement of any kind.</figcaption></figure>

As an <a href="/wiki/Academic_discipline" title="Academic discipline">academic discipline</a>, it analyses and interprets <a href="/wiki/Evidence" title="Evidence">evidence</a> to construct <a href="/wiki/Narrative" title="Narrative">narratives</a> about what happened and explain why it happened. Some theorists categorize history as a <a href="/wiki/Social_science" title="Social science">social science</a>, while others see it as part of the <a href="/wiki/Humanities" title="Humanities">humanities</a> or consider it a hybrid discipline. Similar debates surround the purpose of history&#8212;for example, whether its main aim is theoretical, to uncover the <a href="/wiki/Truth" title="Truth">truth</a>, or practical, to learn lessons from the past. In a more general sense, the term <i>history</i> refers not to an academic field but to the <a href="/wiki/Past" title="Past">past</a> itself, times in the past, or to individual texts about the past.

<p></p></div><div name="Nanotechnology" term="Nanotechnology" wikidataID="Q11468" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanotechnology" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Nanotechnology<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanotechnology">Nanotechnology</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Nanotechnology</b> is the manipulation of matter with at least one dimension sized from 1 to 100 <a href="/wiki/Nanometers" class="mw-redirect" title="Nanometers">nanometers</a> (nm). At this scale, commonly known as the <b>nanoscale</b>, <a href="/wiki/Surface_area" title="Surface area">surface area</a> and <a href="/wiki/Quantum_mechanical" class="mw-redirect" title="Quantum mechanical">quantum mechanical</a> effects become important in describing properties of matter. This definition of nanotechnology includes all types of research and technologies that deal with these special properties. It is common to see the plural form "nanotechnologies" as well as "nanoscale technologies" to refer to research and applications whose common trait is scale.<sup id="cite_ref-Engines1_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Engines1-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> An earlier understanding of nanotechnology referred to the particular technological goal of precisely manipulating atoms and molecules for fabricating macroscale products, now referred to as <a href="/wiki/Molecular_nanotechnology" title="Molecular nanotechnology">molecular nanotechnology</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Nanotsystems_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Nanotsystems-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Fullerene_Nanogears_-_GPN-2000-001535.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Fullerene_Nanogears_-_GPN-2000-001535.jpg/330px-Fullerene_Nanogears_-_GPN-2000-001535.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="198" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Fullerene_Nanogears_-_GPN-2000-001535.jpg/500px-Fullerene_Nanogears_-_GPN-2000-001535.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Fullerene_Nanogears_-_GPN-2000-001535.jpg/960px-Fullerene_Nanogears_-_GPN-2000-001535.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2808" data-file-height="1851"></a><figcaption>Fullerene nanogears</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="Name" term="Name" wikidataID="Q82799" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Name<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name">Name</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>name</b> is a term used for identification by an external observer. They can identify a class or category of things, or a single thing, either uniquely, or within a given context. The entity identified by a name is called its <a href="/wiki/Referent" title="Referent">referent</a>. A <a href="/wiki/Personal_name" title="Personal name">personal name</a> identifies, not necessarily uniquely, a <i>specific</i> individual human. The name of a specific entity is sometimes called a <a href="/wiki/Proper_name" class="mw-redirect" title="Proper name">proper name</a> (although that term has a philosophical meaning as well) and is, when consisting of only one word, a <a href="/wiki/Proper_noun" title="Proper noun">proper noun</a>. Other nouns are sometimes called "<b>common names</b>" or (<a href="/wiki/Obsolete" class="mw-redirect" title="Obsolete">obsolete</a>) "<b>general names</b>". A name can be given to a person, place, or thing; for example, parents can give their child a name or a scientist can give an element a name.
</p>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Leaf axil" term="Leaf axil" wikidataID="Q33971" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf_axil" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Leaf axil<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf_axil">Leaf axil</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>leaf</b> (<abbr title="plural">pl.</abbr>: <b>leaves</b>) is a principal appendage of the <a href="/wiki/Plant_stem" title="Plant stem">stem</a> of a <a href="/wiki/Vascular_plant" title="Vascular plant">vascular plant</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEsau2006_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEsau2006-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> usually borne laterally above ground and specialized for <a href="/wiki/Photosynthesis" title="Photosynthesis">photosynthesis</a>. Leaves are collectively called <b>foliage</b>, as in "autumn foliage",<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHaupt1953_2-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaupt1953-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMauseth2009_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMauseth2009-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> while the leaves, stem, <a href="/wiki/Flower" title="Flower">flower</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Fruit" title="Fruit">fruit</a> collectively form the <a href="/wiki/Shoot_(botany)" title="Shoot (botany)">shoot</a> system.<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In most leaves, the primary <a href="/wiki/Photosynthesis" title="Photosynthesis">photosynthetic</a> <a href="/wiki/Tissue_(biology)" title="Tissue (biology)">tissue</a> is the <a href="/wiki/Palisade_mesophyll" class="mw-redirect" title="Palisade mesophyll">palisade mesophyll</a> and is located on the upper side of the blade or lamina of the leaf,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEsau2006_1-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEsau2006-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> but in some species, including the mature foliage of <i><a href="/wiki/Eucalyptus" title="Eucalyptus">Eucalyptus</a></i>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEJames_et_al1999_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJames_et_al1999-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> palisade mesophyll is present on both sides and the leaves are said to be isobilateral. The leaf is an integral part of the stem system, and most leaves are flattened and have distinct upper (<a href="/wiki/Glossary_of_botanical_terms#adaxial" title="Glossary of botanical terms">adaxial</a>) and lower (<a href="/wiki/Glossary_of_botanical_terms#abaxial" title="Glossary of botanical terms">abaxial</a>) surfaces that differ in color, <a href="/wiki/Trichome" title="Trichome">hairiness</a>, the number of <a href="/wiki/Stomata" class="mw-redirect" title="Stomata">stomata</a> (pores that intake and output gases), the amount and structure of <a href="/wiki/Epicuticular_wax" title="Epicuticular wax">epicuticular wax</a>, and other features. Leaves are mostly green in color due to the presence of a compound called <a href="/wiki/Chlorophyll" title="Chlorophyll">chlorophyll</a> which is essential for photosynthesis as it absorbs light energy from the <a href="/wiki/Sun" title="Sun">Sun</a>. A leaf with lighter-colored or white patches or edges is called a <a href="/wiki/Variegation" title="Variegation">variegated leaf</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Leaf_Varieties_(15_sp).png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Leaf_Varieties_%2815_sp%29.png/500px-Leaf_Varieties_%2815_sp%29.png" decoding="async" width="400" height="401" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Leaf_Varieties_%2815_sp%29.png/960px-Leaf_Varieties_%2815_sp%29.png 1.5x" data-file-width="8160" data-file-height="8189"></a><figcaption>The diversity of leaves, including <i><a href="/wiki/Bismarckia" title="Bismarckia">Bismarckia</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Araucaria" title="Araucaria">Araucaria</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Euphorbia" title="Euphorbia">Euphorbia</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Nymphaea" title="Nymphaea">Nymphaea</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Colocasia" title="Colocasia">Colocasia</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Hildegardia_(plant)" title="Hildegardia (plant)"><i>Hildegardia</i></a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Picea" class="mw-redirect" title="Picea">Picea</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Melocactus" title="Melocactus">Melocactus</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Cycas" title="Cycas">Cycas</a></i>, <a href="/wiki/Acer_(genus)" class="mw-redirect" title="Acer (genus)"><i>Acer</i></a>, <i><a href="/wiki/Yucca" title="Yucca">Yucca</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Ferocactus" title="Ferocactus">Ferocactus</a></i>, and <i><a href="/wiki/Ocimum" title="Ocimum">Ocimum</a></i>.</figcaption></figure>

The genus is native to tropical <a href="/wiki/Americas" title="Americas">America</a> but widely cultivated and naturalized in other tropical regions.<sup id="cite_ref-wwwwwwwwwwwwwww_2-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wwwwwwwwwwwwwww-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Several are grown for their <a href="/wiki/Starch" title="Starch">starchy</a> <a href="/wiki/Corm" title="Corm">corms</a>, an important <a href="/wiki/Root_vegetable" title="Root vegetable">food staple</a> of tropical regions, known variously as <i>malanga</i>, <i>otoy</i>, <i>otoe</i>, cocoyam (or new cocoyam), <i>tannia</i>, <i>tannier</i>, <i>yaut&#237;a</i>, <i>macabo</i>, <i>ocumo</i>, <i>macal</i>, <i>taioba</i>, <i>dasheen</i>, <i>quequisque</i>, <i>&#699;ape</i> and (in <a href="/wiki/Papua_New_Guinea" title="Papua New Guinea">Papua New Guinea</a>) as Singapore taro (<i>taro kongkong</i>). Many other species, including especially <i><a href="/w/index.php?title=Xanthosoma_roseum&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Xanthosoma roseum (page does not exist)">Xanthosoma roseum</a></i>, are used as <a href="/wiki/Ornamental_plant" title="Ornamental plant">ornamental plants</a>; in popular horticultural literature these species may be known as &#8216;ape due to resemblance to the true Polynesian &#699;ape, <i><a href="/wiki/Alocasia_macrorrhizos" title="Alocasia macrorrhizos">Alocasia macrorrhizos</a></i>, or as elephant ear from visual resemblance of the <a href="/wiki/Leaf" title="Leaf">leaf</a> to an <a href="/wiki/Elephant" title="Elephant">elephant</a>'s ear. Sometimes the latter name is also applied to members in the closely related genera <i><a href="/wiki/Caladium" title="Caladium">Caladium</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Colocasia" title="Colocasia">Colocasia</a></i> (<a href="/wiki/Taro" title="Taro">taro</a>), and <i><a href="/wiki/Alocasia" title="Alocasia">Alocasia</a></i>.

Like its relative the <a href="/wiki/Mung_bean" title="Mung bean">mung bean</a>, it has been reclassified from the genus <i><a href="/wiki/Phaseolus" title="Phaseolus">Phaseolus</a></i> to <i><a href="/wiki/Vigna" title="Vigna">Vigna</a></i>. The product sold as black gram is usually the whole urad bean, whereas the split bean (the interior being white) is called <b>white lentil</b>. <p></p></div><div name="Distinctiveness" term="Distinctiveness" wikidataID="Q7832136" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distinctiveness" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Distinctiveness<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distinctiveness">Distinctiveness</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Trademark distinctiveness</b> is an important concept in the law governing <a href="/wiki/Trademark" title="Trademark">trademarks</a> and <a href="/wiki/Service_mark" title="Service mark">service marks</a>. A trademark may be eligible for registration, or <b>registrable</b>, if it performs the essential trademark function, and has <b>distinctive character</b>. Registrability can be understood as a continuum, with "inherently distinctive" marks at one end, "generic" and "descriptive" marks with no distinctive character at the other end, and "suggestive" and "arbitrary" marks lying between these two points. "Descriptive" marks must acquire distinctiveness through secondary meaning&#8212;consumers have come to recognize the mark as a source indicator&#8212;to be protectable.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> "Generic" terms are used to refer to the product or service itself and cannot be used as trademarks.
</p>

The modern <a href="/wiki/Calendar_year" title="Calendar year">calendar year</a>, as reckoned according to the <a href="/wiki/Gregorian_calendar" title="Gregorian calendar">Gregorian calendar</a>, approximates the tropical year by using a system of <a href="/wiki/Leap_years" class="mw-redirect" title="Leap years">leap years</a>.

</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><span><img resource="/wiki/File:Cashew_nut_production,_World,_2023_(cropped).svg" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Cashew_nut_production%2C_World%2C_2023_%28cropped%29.svg/500px-Cashew_nut_production%2C_World%2C_2023_%28cropped%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="400" height="263" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Cashew_nut_production%2C_World%2C_2023_%28cropped%29.svg/960px-Cashew_nut_production%2C_World%2C_2023_%28cropped%29.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="850" data-file-height="559"></span><figcaption>Cashew nut production</figcaption></figure></div><p></p></div><div name="callus" term="callus" wikidataID="Q2197452" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callus" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: callus<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callus">Callus</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">A <b>callus</b> (<abbr title="plural">pl.</abbr>: <b>calluses</b>) is an area of thickened and sometimes hardened skin that forms as a response to repeated friction, pressure, or other irritation.  Since repeated contact is required, calluses are most often found on the feet and hands, but they may occur anywhere on the skin. Some degree of callus, such as on the bottom of the foot, is normal.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Evolucion_de_un_callo.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/Evolucion_de_un_callo.jpg/250px-Evolucion_de_un_callo.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="173" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/Evolucion_de_un_callo.jpg/500px-Evolucion_de_un_callo.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1124" data-file-height="778"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="biotechnology" term="biotechnology" wikidataID="Q7108" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: biotechnology<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology">Biotechnology</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Biotechnology</b> is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of <a href="/wiki/Natural_science" title="Natural science">natural sciences</a> and <a href="/wiki/Engineering_Science" class="mw-redirect" title="Engineering Science">engineering sciences</a> in order to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Specialists in the field are known as <b>biotechnologists</b>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg/250px-Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="385" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg/500px-Faculty_of_Food_Engineering_and_Biotechnology_4.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="3629" data-file-height="5594"></a><figcaption>A biologist conducting research in a biotechnology laboratory</figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="barley" term="barley" wikidataID="Q11577" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barley" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: barley<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barley">Barley</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Barley</b> (<span title="Latin-language text"><i lang="la">Hordeum vulgare</i></span>), a member of the <a href="/wiki/Poaceae" title="Poaceae">grass family</a>, is a major <a href="/wiki/Cereal_grain" class="mw-redirect" title="Cereal grain">cereal grain</a> grown in <a href="/wiki/Temperate_climate" title="Temperate climate">temperate climates</a> globally. One of the <a href="/wiki/Founder_crops" title="Founder crops">first cultivated grains</a>, it was domesticated in the <a href="/wiki/Fertile_Crescent" title="Fertile Crescent">Fertile Crescent</a> around 9000 BC, giving it <a href="/wiki/Shattering_(agriculture)" title="Shattering (agriculture)">nonshattering</a> <a href="/wiki/Spikelet" title="Spikelet">spikelets</a> and making it much easier to <a href="/wiki/Harvest" title="Harvest">harvest</a>. Its use then spread throughout <a href="/wiki/Eurasia" title="Eurasia">Eurasia</a> by 2000 BC. Barley prefers relatively low temperatures and well-drained soil to grow. It is relatively <a href="/wiki/Drought_tolerance_in_barley" title="Drought tolerance in barley">tolerant of drought</a> and <a href="/wiki/Soil_salinity" title="Soil salinity">soil salinity</a>, but is less <a href="/wiki/Hardiness_(plants)" title="Hardiness (plants)">winter-hardy</a> than <a href="/wiki/Wheat" title="Wheat">wheat</a> or <a href="/wiki/Rye" title="Rye">rye</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Barley_Barn_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Barley_Barn_%28cropped%29.jpg/500px-Barley_Barn_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="380" height="133" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/09/Barley_Barn_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="688" data-file-height="240"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/The_Barley_Barn" title="The Barley Barn">The Barley Barn</a> at <a href="/wiki/Cressing" title="Cressing">Cressing</a>, <a href="/wiki/Essex" title="Essex">Essex</a>, built around 1220; its name means "barley barley-store".<sup id="cite_ref-ayto-1990_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ayto-1990-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>
</div><p></p></div><div name="aroids" term="aroids" wikidataID="Q48227" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aroids" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: aroids<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aroids">Aroids</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">The <b>Araceae</b> are a <a href="/wiki/Family_(biology)" title="Family (biology)">family</a> of <a href="/wiki/Monocotyledon" title="Monocotyledon">monocotyledonous</a> <a href="/wiki/Flowering_plant" title="Flowering plant">flowering plants</a> in which <a href="/wiki/Flower" title="Flower">flowers</a> are borne on a type of <a href="/wiki/Inflorescence" title="Inflorescence">inflorescence</a> called a <a href="/wiki/Spadix_(botany)" title="Spadix (botany)">spadix</a>. The spadix is usually accompanied by, and sometimes partially enclosed in, a <a href="/wiki/Spathe" class="mw-redirect" title="Spathe">spathe</a> (or leaf-like <a href="/wiki/Bract" title="Bract">bract</a>). Also known as the <b>arum family</b>, members are often colloquially known as <b>aroids</b>. This family of 114 <a href="/wiki/Genera" class="mw-redirect" title="Genera">genera</a> and about 3,750 known species<sup id="cite_ref-Christenhusz-Byng2016_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Christenhusz-Byng2016-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> is most diverse in the <a href="/wiki/New_World" title="New World">New World</a> tropics, although also distributed in the <a href="/wiki/Old_World" title="Old World">Old World</a> tropics and northern <a href="/wiki/Temperate_regions" class="mw-redirect" title="Temperate regions">temperate regions</a>.
</p>
<div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Spathiphyllum_cochlearispathum_RTBG.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Spathiphyllum_cochlearispathum_RTBG.jpg/250px-Spathiphyllum_cochlearispathum_RTBG.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="375" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Spathiphyllum_cochlearispathum_RTBG.jpg/500px-Spathiphyllum_cochlearispathum_RTBG.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1224" data-file-height="1835"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="area expansion" term="area expansion" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=area%20expansion" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: area expansion<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=area%20expansion">area expansion</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="aphid" term="aphid" wikidataID="Q183350" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aphid" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: aphid<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aphid">Aphid</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Aphids</b> are small <a href="/wiki/Sap" title="Sap">sap</a>-sucking <a href="/wiki/Insect" title="Insect">insects</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Taxonomic_rank" title="Taxonomic rank">family</a> <b>Aphididae</b>. Common names include <b>greenfly</b> and <b>blackfly</b>,<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> although individuals within a species can vary widely in color. The group includes the fluffy white <a href="/wiki/Eriosomatinae" title="Eriosomatinae">woolly aphids</a>. A typical life cycle involves flightless females giving <a href="/wiki/Viviparity" title="Viviparity">live birth</a> to female <a href="/wiki/Nymph_(biology)" title="Nymph (biology)">nymphs</a>&#8212;who may also be already <a href="/wiki/Pregnancy" title="Pregnancy">pregnant</a>, an adaptation scientists call <a href="/wiki/Telescoping_generations" title="Telescoping generations">telescoping generations</a>&#8212;without the involvement of males. <a href="/wiki/Developmental_biology" title="Developmental biology">Maturing</a> rapidly, females breed profusely so that the number of these insects multiplies quickly. <a href="/wiki/Alate" title="Alate">Winged females</a> may develop later in the season, allowing the insects to colonize new plants. In <a href="/wiki/Temperate_climate" title="Temperate climate">temperate</a> regions, a phase of <a href="/wiki/Sexual_reproduction" title="Sexual reproduction">sexual reproduction</a> occurs in the <a href="/wiki/Autumn" title="Autumn">autumn</a>, with the insects often overwintering as <a href="/wiki/Egg" title="Egg">eggs</a>.
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg/250px-Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="296" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg/500px-Aphids_September_2008-1.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="1914" data-file-height="2270"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="agronomic characters" term="agronomic characters" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=agronomic%20characters" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: agronomic characters<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=agronomic%20characters">agronomic characters</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Zinc" term="Zinc" wikidataID="Q758" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zinc" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Zinc<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zinc">Zinc</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Zinc</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Chemical_element" title="Chemical element">chemical element</a>; it has <a href="/wiki/Symbol_(chemistry)" class="mw-redirect" title="Symbol (chemistry)">symbol</a> <b>Zn</b> and atomic number 30. It is a slightly brittle metal at <a href="/wiki/Room_temperature" title="Room temperature">room temperature</a> and has a shiny blue whitish appearance when surface oxidation is removed. It is the first element in <a href="/wiki/Group_11_element" title="Group 11 element">group 12 (IIB)</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Periodic_table" title="Periodic table">periodic table</a>. Zinc is the 24th most abundant <a href="/wiki/Abundance_of_elements_in_Earth%27s_crust" title="Abundance of elements in Earth's crust">element in Earth's crust</a>, with an average concentration of 70 grams per ton.<sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Zinc also has five stable <a href="/wiki/Isotope" title="Isotope">isotopes</a>; the most abundant of which, Zn-64, comprises nearly half of zinc's total abundance. In some respects, zinc is chemically similar to <a href="/wiki/Magnesium" title="Magnesium">magnesium</a>: both elements exhibit only one normal oxidation state (+2), and the Zn<sup>2+</sup> and Mg<sup>2+</sup> <a href="/wiki/Ion" title="Ion">ions</a> are of similar size.<sup id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>b<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The most common zinc <a href="/wiki/Ore" title="Ore">ore</a> is <a href="/wiki/Sphalerite" title="Sphalerite">sphalerite</a> (zinc blende), a <a href="/wiki/Zinc_sulfide" title="Zinc sulfide">zinc sulfide</a> mineral. The largest concentration of economically feasible <a href="/wiki/Lode" title="Lode">lodes</a> in descending order are located in China, Peru, and Australia and among others. Zinc is refined industrially by <a href="/wiki/Froth_flotation" title="Froth flotation">froth flotation</a> of the ore, <a href="/wiki/Roasting_(metallurgy)" title="Roasting (metallurgy)">roasting</a>, and final <a href="/wiki/Extractive_metallurgy" title="Extractive metallurgy">extraction</a> using <a href="/wiki/Electricity" title="Electricity">electricity</a> (<a href="/wiki/Electrowinning" title="Electrowinning">electrowinning</a>).
</p><div title="figure"><a href="/wiki/File:Zinc_fragment_sublimed_and_1cm3_cube.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Zinc_fragment_sublimed_and_1cm3_cube.jpg/250px-Zinc_fragment_sublimed_and_1cm3_cube.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="153" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Zinc_fragment_sublimed_and_1cm3_cube.jpg/500px-Zinc_fragment_sublimed_and_1cm3_cube.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="5135" data-file-height="3138"></a></div><p></p></div><div name="PGSC Award" term="PGSC Award" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=PGSC%20Award" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: PGSC Award<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=PGSC%20Award">PGSC Award</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para">

It is distinct from other object properties, such as <a href="/wiki/Color" title="Color">color</a>, <a href="/wiki/Surface_texture" class="mw-redirect" title="Surface texture">texture</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Material" title="Material">material</a> type.
In <a href="/wiki/Geometry" title="Geometry">geometry</a>, <i>shape</i> excludes information about the object's <a href="/wiki/Position_(geometry)" title="Position (geometry)">position</a>, <a href="/wiki/Size" title="Size">size</a>, <a href="/wiki/Orientation_(geometry)" title="Orientation (geometry)">orientation</a> and <a href="/wiki/Chirality" title="Chirality">chirality</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Kendall_1-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kendall-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>

This is due to their motion through the fluid in response to the <a href="/wiki/Force" title="Force">forces</a> acting on them: these forces can be due to <a href="/wiki/Gravitation" class="mw-redirect" title="Gravitation">gravity</a>, <a href="/wiki/Centrifugal_acceleration" class="mw-redirect" title="Centrifugal acceleration">centrifugal acceleration</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Electromagnetism" title="Electromagnetism">electromagnetism</a>. <a href="/wiki/Settling" title="Settling">Settling</a> is the falling of suspended particles through the liquid, whereas sedimentation is the final result of the settling process.

A <b>quantitative trait locus</b> (<b>QTL</b>) is a <a href="/wiki/Locus_(genetics)" title="Locus (genetics)">locus</a> (section of <a href="/wiki/DNA" title="DNA">DNA</a>) that correlates with variation of a <a href="/wiki/Quantitative_trait" class="mw-redirect" title="Quantitative trait">quantitative trait</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Phenotype" title="Phenotype">phenotype</a> of a <a href="/wiki/Population_genetics" title="Population genetics">population</a> of <a href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organisms</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> QTLs are mapped by identifying which molecular markers (such as <a href="/wiki/Single-nucleotide_polymorphism" title="Single-nucleotide polymorphism">SNPs</a> or <a href="/wiki/Amplified_fragment_length_polymorphism" title="Amplified fragment length polymorphism">AFLPs</a>) correlate with an observed trait. This is often an early step in identifying the actual <a href="/wiki/Gene" title="Gene">genes</a> that cause the trait variation.
</p>
<div title="figure"><figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Example_of_QTL-Scan_on_a_single_Chromosom_from_PLoS_Biology.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Example_of_QTL-Scan_on_a_single_Chromosom_from_PLoS_Biology.jpg/250px-Example_of_QTL-Scan_on_a_single_Chromosom_from_PLoS_Biology.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="266" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Example_of_QTL-Scan_on_a_single_Chromosom_from_PLoS_Biology.jpg/500px-Example_of_QTL-Scan_on_a_single_Chromosom_from_PLoS_Biology.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="2500" data-file-height="2663"></a><figcaption>A QTL for <a href="/wiki/Osteoporosis" title="Osteoporosis">osteoporosis</a> on the human chromosome 20</figcaption></figure>

You can <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Article_wizard" title="Wikipedia:Article wizard">create a draft and submit it for review</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Articles_for_creation/Redirects" title="Wikipedia:Articles for creation/Redirects">request that a redirect be created</a>, but consider checking the search results below to see whether the topic is already covered.</i></p><p></p></div><div name="Personality Development" term="Personality Development" wikidataID="Q3520110" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_Development" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: Personality Development<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_Development">Personality Development</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Personality development</b> encompasses the dynamic construction and deconstruction of integrative characteristics that distinguish an individual in terms of interpersonal behavioral traits.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Personality development is ever-changing and subject to contextual factors and life-altering experiences. Personality development is also dimensional in description and subjective in nature.<sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> That is, personality development can be seen as a continuum varying in degrees of intensity and change. It is subjective in nature because its conceptualization is rooted in social norms of expected behavior, self-expression, and personal growth.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The dominant viewpoint in personality psychology indicates that personality emerges early and continues to develop across one's lifespan.<sup id="cite_ref-Roberts,_B._W._2010_pp._375-39823_5-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Roberts,_B._W._2010_pp._375-39823-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Adult personality traits are believed to have a basis in infant <a href="/wiki/Temperament" title="Temperament">temperament</a>, meaning that individual differences in disposition and behavior appear early in life, potentially before language of conscious self-representation develop.<sup id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Big_Five_personality_traits" title="Big Five personality traits">The Five Factor Model of personality</a> maps onto the dimensions of childhood temperament.<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This suggests that individual differences in levels of the corresponding personality traits (neuroticism, extraversion, openness to experience, agreeableness, and conscientiousness) are present from young ages.<sup id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<p></p></div><div name="starch" term="starch" wikidataID="Q41534" wikipedia_url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starch" role="ami_entry"><p>search term: starch<br><span>Wikipedia URL: </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starch">Starch</a></p><p class="wpage_first_para"><b>Starch</b> or <b>amylum</b> is a <a href="/wiki/Polymeric" class="mw-redirect" title="Polymeric">polymeric</a> <a href="/wiki/Carbohydrate" title="Carbohydrate">carbohydrate</a> consisting of numerous <a href="/wiki/Glucose" title="Glucose">glucose</a> units joined by <a href="/wiki/Glycosidic_bond" title="Glycosidic bond">glycosidic bonds</a>. This <a href="/wiki/Polysaccharide" title="Polysaccharide">polysaccharide</a> is produced by most green <a href="/wiki/Plant" title="Plant">plants</a> for energy storage. Worldwide, it is the most common carbohydrate in human diets, and is contained in large amounts in <a href="/wiki/Staple_food" title="Staple food">staple foods</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Wheat" title="Wheat">wheat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Potato" title="Potato">potatoes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Maize" title="Maize">maize</a> (corn), <a href="/wiki/Rice" title="Rice">rice</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Cassava" title="Cassava">cassava</a> (manioc).

It is a <a href="/wiki/Federal_republic" title="Federal republic">federal republic</a> of 50 <a href="/wiki/U.S._state" title="U.S. state">states</a> and a <a href="/wiki/Capital_districts_and_territories" title="Capital districts and territories">federal capital district</a>, <a href="/wiki/Washington,_D.C." title="Washington, D.C.">Washington, D.C.</a> The 48 <a href="/wiki/Contiguous_states" class="mw-redirect" title="Contiguous states">contiguous states</a> border <a href="/wiki/Canada" title="Canada">Canada</a> to the north and <a href="/wiki/Mexico" title="Mexico">Mexico</a> to the south, with the <a href="/wiki/Semi-exclave" class="mw-redirect" title="Semi-exclave">semi-exclave</a> of <a href="/wiki/Alaska" title="Alaska">Alaska</a> in the northwest and the <a href="/wiki/Archipelago" title="Archipelago">archipelago</a> of <a href="/wiki/Hawaii" title="Hawaii">Hawaii</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Pacific_Ocean" title="Pacific Ocean">Pacific Ocean</a>. The United States also asserts sovereignty over five <a href="/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States" title="Territories of the United States">major island territories</a> and <a href="/wiki/United_States_Minor_Outlying_Islands" title="United States Minor Outlying Islands">various uninhabited islands</a> in <a href="/wiki/Oceania" title="Oceania">Oceania</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Caribbean" title="Caribbean">Caribbean</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>j<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It is a <a href="/wiki/Megadiverse_country" class="mw-redirect" title="Megadiverse country">megadiverse country</a>, with the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area" title="List of countries and dependencies by area">third-largest land area</a><sup id="cite_ref-largestcountry_15-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-largestcountry-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>c<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population" title="List of countries and dependencies by population">third-largest population</a>, exceeding 341 million.<sup id="cite_ref-pop_clock_32-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pop_clock-32"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>k<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
